– Ein Klick auf die Vorschau fährt zum Rahmen; der Name lässt sich direkt umbenennen.

– Ziehen am Griff (oder ⌥ + Pfeiltasten) ändert die Reihenfolge – sie ist die Reihenfolge der Präsentation und wird mit dem Board gespeichert. Solange niemand sortiert, gilt die Leserichtung (von oben nach unten, links nach rechts).
– In der Präsentation ausblenden (Augensymbol) lässt einen Rahmen beim Präsentieren aus, ohne ihn zu löschen.
– Sprechernotizen je Rahmen, sichtbar nur in der Präsentation.
– Außerdem: Link zu diesem Element kopieren, Rahmen exportieren und Ab hier präsentieren.

de.heading: Präsentieren
paragraphs: Sobald es Rahmen gibt, erscheint Präsentieren in der Leiste unten links; die Pfeile daneben fahren auch ohne Präsentation zum vorigen bzw. nächsten Rahmen. Die Rahmen werden in der Reihenfolge der Rahmen-Übersicht nacheinander bildschirmfüllend gezeigt, ausgeblendete Rahmen fehlen; alles außerhalb des aktuellen Rahmens tritt zurück. Pfeiltasten oder die Knöpfe blättern, Präsentation beenden oder Esc schließt.
– Sprechernotizen blendet die Notizen des Rahmens ein.

– Referentenansicht öffnet dieselbe zweite Ansicht wie bei Dokumenten: aktuelle und nächste Folie, die Notizen und die verstrichene Zeit. Beide Fenster bleiben im Gleichschritt – Blättern geht in jedem von beiden.

de.heading: Vorlagen
paragraphs: Vorlagen öffnet eine durchsuchbare Galerie mit Vorschau, nach Kategorien sortiert:
Kategorie Vorlagen
Retrospektiven Retrospektive, 4L-Retrospektive, Seestern-Retrospektive
Planung Kanban, User Story Map, Sprint-Planung, Projektzeitplan, Eisenhower-Matrix, Aufwand-Nutzen-Matrix
Strategie OKR, SWOT-Analyse, Lean Canvas, Business Model Canvas, Customer Journey
Ideen Empathy Map, Brainstorming, Mindmap
Diagramme Flussdiagramm, Entscheidungsbaum, Organigramm
Besprechungen Besprechungsagenda, Eisbrecher
Eine Vorlage landet in der Mitte der Ansicht und ist danach normaler Inhalt des Boards.

Eigene Vorlagen: Unter Als Vorlage speichern wird das ganze Board oder die Auswahl zur Vorlage – Für den Arbeitsbereich oder Nur für mich. Kommentare, Stimmen und Stempel bleiben draußen, Bilder und PDFs bleiben Dateien des Arbeitsbereichs. Eigene Vorlagen stehen im Reiter Eigene Vorlagen; löschen können sie die Person, die sie gespeichert hat, und Besitzer. Höchstens 500 Vorlagen je Arbeitsbereich.

de.heading: Excalidraw und draw.io importieren
paragraphs: Über Importieren … unter + – oder indem du die Datei aufs Board ziehst – übernimmst du Zeichnungen aus:
– Excalidraw (.excalidraw),
– draw.io / diagrams.net (.drawio, .xml, auch komprimiert und mit mehreren Seiten) sowie SVG-Exporte von draw.io mit eingebettetem Diagramm.

Formen, Texte, Pfeile mit ihren Verbindungen und Beschriftungen, Freihandstriche, Rahmen, Farben, Linienstärken, Strichelungen und Drehungen werden zu Whiteboard-Elementen. Mehrere draw.io-Seiten landen nebeneinander, jede in einem eigenen Rahmen. Was Flowplan nicht kennt (Schablonen, Einbettungen, externe Bilder), wird zu einer Notiz mit seinem Text. Eingebettete Bilder (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) werden als Dateien der Seite gespeichert und zählen zum Speicherkontingent.
– Ziehst du eine solche Datei in ein Dokument, entsteht darunter ein neues Whiteboard, das gleich eingebettet wird.
– Im ZIP-Import (siehe Importieren) werden .excalidraw- und .drawio-Dateien zu Whiteboard-Seiten.
– Grenzen: 20 MB je Datei (30 MB entpackt), 3.000 Elemente, 50 Seiten. Flowplan lädt beim Import nichts aus dem Internet; Texte werden als reiner Text übernommen.

de.heading: Einbetten und exportieren
paragraphs: – Mit /board im Dokument wird ein Whiteboard Teil einer Seite; der Knopf oben rechts öffnet es groß.
– Als PNG exportieren oder Als SVG exportieren speichert das Whiteboard als Bild.

– Exportieren … (PNG, SVG, PDF) öffnet den Export-Dialog: Was (Ganzes Board, Auswahl oder ein einzelner Rahmen), Format und bei PNG die Auflösung 1×, 2× oder 4×. Als PDF kommt das Board Alles auf einer Seite oder mit Eine Seite pro Rahmen in der Reihenfolge der Präsentation (ausgeblendete Rahmen fehlen). Der Export entsteht im Browser; der Server sieht davon nichts.
– Im Markdown-Export kommt jedes Whiteboard automatisch als SVG mit.
– Die Texte auf dem Board sind durchsuchbar und erscheinen in Exporten.
– Als Mermaid kopieren übernimmt Formen und Verbindungen als Mermaid-Flussdiagramm (siehe oben).
Alle Knoten, die ein Workflow kennt – mit Typ (so steht er im JSON und in der API), Ausgängen und den Ausgaben, die spätere Knoten als Platzhalter nutzen.
Diese Liste wird aus dem Knotenkatalog von Flowplan erzeugt; die Einstellungen jedes Knotens als JSON Schema liefert GET /api/workflows/catalog.

de.heading: Auslöser
paragraphs: Knoten Typ Was er tut Ausgänge Ausgaben
Neuer Eintrag ⚡ trigger.record.created Ein Eintrag wird in einer Datenbank angelegt. out record, actor, via
Eintrag geändert ⚡ trigger.record.changed Eigenschaften eines Eintrags ändern sich. out record, before, changed, actor
Eintrag erledigt ⚡ trigger.record.done Ein Eintrag wird erledigt. out record, actor
Datum erreicht trigger.record.date Ein Datum eines Eintrags ist erreicht oder überfällig. out record, date
Formularantwort ⚡ trigger.form.submitted Jemand schickt das Formular einer Datenbank ab. out record, answers, respondent
Zeitplan trigger.schedule Täglich, wöchentlich oder monatlich zu einer Uhrzeit. out slot
Neue Seite trigger.page.created Eine Seite wird angelegt. out page, actor
Seite geändert trigger.page.changed Titel oder Inhalt einer Seite ändert sich (2 Minuten nach der letzten Änderung). out page, actor, changes
Seite verschoben trigger.page.moved Eine Seite bekommt eine neue Elternseite oder einen neuen Bereich. out page, from, to, actor
Tag hinzugefügt trigger.page.tagged Eine Seite bekommt einen Tag. out page, tag, actor
Neuer Kommentar trigger.comment.created Jemand kommentiert eine Seite oder einen Eintrag. out comment, page, record, actor
Erwähnung trigger.mention Jemand wird in einer Seite, einem Eintrag oder Kommentar erwähnt. out page, record, mentioned, actor
Manuell starten trigger.manual Startet über „Ausführen“, die API oder einen Knopf. out inputs, startedBy, source
Eingehender Webhook trigger.webhook Ein anderer Dienst ruft die Adresse des Workflows auf. out body, query, headers, receivedAt
E-Mail empfangen trigger.mail.received Eine E-Mail kommt an einer Adresse an, die an diesen Workflow geht. out mail, authenticated
Neuer Journaltag trigger.journal.day Die Seite eines Tages wird im Journal angelegt. out day, date, journal

de.heading: Logik
paragraphs: Knoten Typ Was er tut Ausgänge Ausgaben
Wenn ⚡ logic.if Verzweigt nach Bedingungen. true, false matched
Werte setzen ⚡ logic.set Benannte Werte für spätere Knoten. out –
Beenden ⚡ logic.stop Beendet den Lauf erfolgreich oder als Fehler. – –
Unterscheiden ⚡ logic.switch Verzweigt nach dem ersten passenden Fall. case:…, default case
Für jedes logic.foreach Führt die folgenden Knoten für jedes Element einer Liste aus. item, done count, results
Warten logic.wait Wartet eine Dauer, bis zu einem Zeitpunkt oder bis zur nächsten Uhrzeit. out waitedUntil
Freigabe logic.approval Wartet, bis eine Person genehmigt oder ablehnt. approved, rejected, timeout decidedBy, comment, decidedAt

de.heading: Einträge
paragraphs: Knoten Typ Was er tut Ausgänge Ausgaben
Eintrag anlegen action.record.create Legt einen Eintrag in einer Datenbank an. out record
Eintrag ändern ⚡ action.record.update Ändert Eigenschaften eines Eintrags. out record, before
Einträge finden action.record.find Sucht Einträge nach Bedingungen. out records, first, count
Vorlage anwenden ⚡ action.record.template Wendet eine Eintragsvorlage auf einen Eintrag an. out record

de.heading: Seiten
paragraphs: Knoten Typ Was er tut Ausgänge Ausgaben
Seite anlegen action.page.create Legt eine Seite unter einer Elternseite an. out page
An Seite anhängen action.page.append Fügt Blöcke am Ende, am Anfang oder unter einer Überschrift ein. out page, appended
Seite taggen action.page.tag Fügt einer Seite Tags hinzu oder entfernt sie. out page
Seite verschieben action.page.move Verschiebt eine Seite unter eine neue Elternseite. out page

de.heading: Benachrichtigen
paragraphs: Knoten Typ Was er tut Ausgänge Ausgaben
Person benachrichtigen ⚡ notify.person Benachrichtigung in der App, per Push, E-Mail oder Chat-App. out notified
E-Mail senden notify.email Schickt eine E-Mail an Personen oder Adressen. out sent
Chat-Nachricht notify.chat Postet in einen Chat-Webhook des Arbeitsbereichs (Slack, Matrix, Teams, Discord). out sent

de.heading: KI
paragraphs: Knoten Typ Was er tut Ausgänge Ausgaben
KI: Zusammenfassen ai.summarize Fasst einen Text zusammen. out summary
KI: Einordnen ai.classify Ordnet einen Text einer der Kategorien zu. out, unclear category, categories, confidence
KI: Felder auslesen ai.extract Liest benannte Werte aus einem Text. out fields, missing
KI: Eigene Anweisung ai.prompt Eine eigene Anweisung, Antwort als Text oder JSON. out text, json

de.heading: HTTP
paragraphs: Knoten Typ Was er tut Ausgänge Ausgaben
HTTP-Anfrage http.request Ruft eine HTTPS-Adresse auf (fester Host). out status, headers, body, json
⚡ – kann im Sofortteil laufen: direkt beim Speichern eines Eintrags, in derselben Änderung.
Jeder Knoten kann Bei Fehler wiederholen (bis 5-mal), den Lauf beenden, über den Ausgang error weitergehen oder den Fehler übergehen.

Ein Workflow ist ein Ablauf aus Knoten auf einer Fläche: ein Auslöser (eine neue Seite, ein geänderter Eintrag, ein Zeitplan, eine E-Mail …), dann Logik und Aktionen – Einträge und Seiten ändern, Personen benachrichtigen, KI fragen, andere Dienste aufrufen. Ganz ohne Code.

Workflows sind ein eigener Seitentyp. Sie laufen im Hintergrund auf dem Server, Schritt für Schritt, überstehen Neustarts, wiederholen sich bei Fehlern und warten auch Tage auf ein Datum oder eine Freigabe. Ein Workflow kann nie mehr als die Person, die ihn aktiviert hat.

de.heading: Erste Schritte: die Vorlage aus dem Issue
paragraphs: So verlinkst du jede neue Unterseite einer Übersichtsseite automatisch dort – mit einem Satz Beschreibung:
– In der Seitenleiste + → Workflow wählen und einen Titel geben.
– Auf der leeren Fläche die Vorlage Unterseiten auf der Übersicht verlinken wählen.
– Der kurze Assistent fragt nach der Übersichtsseite und ob eine Kurzbeschreibung mit KI dazukommt. Als Entwurf anlegen.
– Probelauf (nichts wird verändert) oder Testlauf (echt, als du) – das Ergebnis steht an jedem Knoten.
– Aktivieren. Ab jetzt landet jede neue Unterseite als „• Link – Kurztext“ auf der Übersicht, nie doppelt.

de.heading: Wie ein Workflow beginnt
paragraphs: Eine neue Workflow-Seite zeigt vier Wege:
– Leer beginnen – du wählst den Auslöser und baust selbst.
– Vorlagen – sechs fertige Abläufe mit Lücken, die ein Assistent abfragt (Seite, Datenbank, Eigenschaft, Person, Chat-Webhook, E-Mail-Adresse):
Vorlage Was sie tut
Unterseiten auf der Übersicht verlinken Neue Seite direkt unter X → optional KI-Kurzbeschreibung → „• Link – Kurztext“ an X anhängen, nie doppelt
Erinnerung vor Fälligkeit Zwei Tage vor dem Datum um 9:00 → nur wenn nicht erledigt → Verantwortliche per Push erinnern
Formular → KI-Kategorie → Zuweisung Formularantwort → KI ordnet einer Kategorie zu → je Kategorie zuständig machen und benachrichtigen; unklar → Teamleitung
Wochenbericht Freitags 15:00 → diese Woche erledigte Einträge finden → KI fasst zusammen → Berichtsseite anlegen → optional im Chat posten
Eingehende Mail → Ticket E-Mail an die Adresse des Workflows → KI liest Titel, Beschreibung, Dringlichkeit → Eintrag anlegen → Absender bestätigen
Webhook → Eintrag Ein anderer Dienst ruft die Adresse des Workflows auf → Eintrag anlegen
– Mit KI entwerfen – ein Satz genügt, siehe KI-Builder.
– Aus Datei importieren – eine exportierte Workflow-Datei, siehe Export und Import.
Was du wählst, landet als Entwurf auf der Fläche – mit Rückgängig wieder weg. Aktiv wird ein Workflow nie von selbst.

de.heading: Die Fläche
paragraphs: – Knotenliste links: Auslöser, Logik, Einträge, Seiten, Benachrichtigen, KI, HTTP – mit Suche. Ziehen oder anklicken (hängt hinter dem gewählten Knoten an).
– Knoten zeigen Symbol, Bezeichnung und eine Zeile Zusammenfassung; ein Punkt markiert Fehler oder Warnungen der Prüfung. Das ⚡ heißt: läuft sofort beim Speichern des Eintrags (der „Sofortteil“).
– Seitenpanel rechts: die Einstellungen des gewählten Knotens, „Bei Fehler“, Notiz und Ein-/Ausgabe des letzten Tests.
– Liste zeigt denselben Ablauf als Gliederung – voll per Tastatur bedienbar. Aufräumen ordnet die Knoten von links nach rechts.
– Mehrere Personen bearbeiten denselben Entwurf gleichzeitig; was läuft, ändert sich erst mit Aktivieren.

de.heading: Platzhalter und Filter
paragraphs: In jedem Textfeld fügt {} (oder {{ tippen) Werte früherer Knoten ein, etwa {{Neue Seite.Titel}} oder {{Auslöser.Eintrag.Felder.Status}}. Filter hängen mit an:
Filter Beispiel Ergebnis
truncate / kürzen {{KI.summary \ kürzen: 140}} höchstens 140 Zeichen
date / datum {{$heute \ datum: "dd.MM.yyyy"}} Datum in eigener Form
add_days / plus_tage {{$heute \ plus_tage: 3}} drei Tage später
default / standard {{Webhook.body.titel \ standard: "Ohne Titel"}} Ersatz für leere Werte
required / pflicht {{Webhook.body.titel \ pflicht}} Fehler, wenn leer
join, first, last, count {{Finden.records \ verbinden: ", "}} Listen zu Text
upper, lower, trim, replace, number, plain, json Text umformen
Eingebaute Werte: $heute, $jetzt, $lauf, $workflow, $ausführende, in „Für jedes“ $element und $index. Platzhalterwerte werden immer als Text eingefügt, nie als HTML.

de.heading: Testen
paragraphs: – Probelauf: Schreibende Knoten berichten nur, was sie täten („würde Eintrag anlegen …“); E-Mail, Chat und Push gehen nicht raus, Warten wird übersprungen, Freigaben gelten als genehmigt oder abgelehnt (wählbar). KI-Knoten laufen und kosten Tokens.
– Testlauf: führt echt aus – als du, nicht als die ausführende Person.
– Daten des Auslösers: Beispiel, letztes echtes Ereignis, ein Eintrag oder eine Seite zum Auswählen oder eigene Werte.
Tests nutzen immer den Entwurf. Das Ergebnis steht als Statusring an jedem Knoten; ein Klick zeigt Ein- und Ausgabe.

de.heading: Aktivieren, pausieren, „läuft als“
paragraphs: Aktivieren prüft den Entwurf (fehlende Angaben, gelöschte Datenbanken, Seiten ohne Zugriff …) und zeigt, was der Workflow tun wird und als wer er läuft: als die Person, die aktiviert. Er sieht und ändert nur, was diese Person darf. Verliert sie ihre Rechte, pausiert der Workflow und meldet sich.

Pausieren hält offene Läufe an (wahlweise brechen sie ab); nach dem Aktivieren laufen sie auf ihrer Version weiter. Nach zehn Fehlschlägen in Folge oder wenn die Hälfte der letzten Läufe scheitert, pausiert ein Workflow von selbst.

de.heading: Läufe und Versionen
paragraphs: Der Reiter Läufe listet jeden Lauf mit Status, Dauer und Version; filtern nach fehlgeschlagen, wartend, offen und Tests, suchen nach Fehlern. Ein Lauf öffnet die Fläche in seiner Version mit der Zeitleiste der Schritte (Versuche, Wartezeiten, Fehler). Wiederholen ab fehlgeschlagenem Knoten und Abbrechen stehen dort.
Ein- und Ausgaben eines Laufs sieht nur die Person, als die er lief; Kolleginnen sehen Status und Fehler und debuggen mit einem eigenen Testlauf.
Versionen zeigt aktivierte Versionen und Entwurfsstände in einer Zeitleiste, vergleicht zwei Stände und stellt einen als Entwurf wieder her.

de.heading: KI-Builder
paragraphs: Mit KI entwerfen (auf der leeren Fläche oder oben in der Leiste) baut aus einem Satz einen Entwurf – zum Beispiel: „Wenn im Wiki unter Docker eine Seite entsteht, trage sie mit einem Satz Beschreibung auf der Übersicht ein.“
– Die KI sieht nur Namen von Datenbanken, Eigenschaften, Optionen, Bereichen und Seiten, die du sehen darfst und die für die KI freigegeben sind – keine Inhalte.
– Was sie vorschlägt, wird gegen den Knotenkatalog geprüft: Unbekannte Knoten fallen weg, unbekannte Seiten oder Eigenschaften bleiben leer und sind markiert.
– Du siehst den Vorschlag zuerst; In den Entwurf übernehmen fügt ihn als eine Änderung ein. Aktivieren musst du selbst.
– Es zählt dein persönliches KI-Kontingent, nicht das Budget des Workflows. Siehe KI.

de.heading: Workflow-Knopf auf Seiten
paragraphs: Mit /Workflow-Knopf kommt ein Knopf in ein Dokument, der einen Workflow mit dem Auslöser Manuell starten startet. Hat der Auslöser Eingabefelder, zeigt der Knopf ein kleines Formular. Nach dem Klick steht dort Gestartet – Bearbeitende des Workflows sehen den Weg zu den Läufen.

Wer drücken darf, legt der Auslöser fest: standardmäßig die Bearbeitenden des Workflows, umschaltbar auf alle Mitglieder, die die Seite mit dem Knopf sehen. Gäste und Freigabelinks sehen den Knopf nie. Der Lauf läuft immer als die ausführende Person; die klickende Person steht als „Gestartet von“ im Lauf.

de.heading: Export und Import
paragraphs: Als JSON exportieren (Pfeil oben rechts) speichert den Ablauf als .flowplan-workflow.json: Bearbeitende bekommen den Entwurf, Lesende die aktive Version. Die Datei nennt die verwendeten Seiten, Datenbanken (mit Eigenschaften) und Personen mit Titel. Zugangsdaten, Webhook-Adressen und Läufe sind nie enthalten – Zugangsdaten nur mit Name, Art und Host, damit du sie neu verknüpfen kannst.

Aus Datei importieren ordnet Verweise im Arbeitsbereich zu: gleiche ID, sonst gleicher Titel (Seiten, Datenbanken), gleicher Name (Personen, Eigenschaften). Was offen bleibt, fragt der Assistent ab oder bleibt leer. Importiert wird immer als Entwurf.

Inhaltsarchive und der Instanzumzug nehmen Workflows mit Entwurf und Versionen mit, ohne Läufe und Geheimnisse. Aktive Workflows kommen pausiert an, damit auf der neuen Instanz nichts unbeabsichtigt loslegt.

de.heading: Telefon und Tablet
paragraphs: – Telefon: Status mit Ein/Aus-Schalter, der Ablauf als Liste, Läufe und Freigaben. Bearbeitet wird auf Tablet oder Computer.
– Freigaben: Die Benachrichtigung öffnet die Workflow-Seite mit dem Reiter Freigaben – Nachricht, Kommentar, Ablehnen oder Genehmigen.

– Freigaben in der App: In der iPhone- und Android-App trägt die Mitteilung die Knöpfe Genehmigen und Ablehnen, sofern Mitteilungen auf dem Sperrbildschirm ihren Text zeigen. Genehmigen fragt vorher Face ID, Touch ID oder den Fingerabdruck ab – ohne Biometrie öffnet sich stattdessen der Reiter Freigaben. Ablehnen geht ohne Biometrie, das Telefon muss aber entsperrt sein. Das Gerät muss angemeldet und in den letzten 14 Tagen aktiv gewesen sein; auf Android öffnet das allererste Genehmigen einmal den Reiter, weil dabei der Schlüssel angelegt wird.
– Tablet: der volle Editor; Verbinden auch per Tippen auf einen Ausgang und dann das Ziel.

de.heading: Tastatur
paragraphs: Taste Wirkung
Tab / Umschalt+Tab zwischen Knoten
Pfeiltasten (mit Umschalt weiter) gewählten Knoten verschieben
Enter / Esc Panel öffnen / schließen
A Knoten anhängen
C verbinden mit …
Entf löschen
Strg+Z / Strg+Y rückgängig / wiederholen
Strg+D duplizieren
L Liste ↔ Fläche
F Ansicht einpassen

de.heading: Grenzen
paragraphs: Grenze Standard
Läufe je Minute und Workflow 60
Läufe je Minute und Arbeitsbereich 600
Schritte je Lauf 200
Gegenseitige Auslösung (Kaskade) 5 Ebenen
Elemente je „Für jedes“ 100
KI-Tokens je Workflow und Tag 100 000
E-Mails je Workflow und Tag 100
Aufbewahrung der Läufe 30 Tage
Aktive Workflows je Arbeitsbereich 100
Admins ändern die Werte in der Administration oder per Umgebungsvariable. Bearbeitende können je Workflow niedrigere Werte setzen.

de.heading: API, MCP und SDKs
paragraphs: Workflows lassen sich per REST-API anlegen, prüfen, testen, aktivieren (mit Schreib-Token) und starten; die SDKs bringen fertige Methoden mit. Über MCP liest ein KI-Assistent Workflows und Läufe, speichert Entwürfe, testet und startet – aktivieren und Freigaben entscheiden kann er nicht.

de.heading: Häufige Fragen
paragraphs: Ersetzen Workflows die Automationen der Datenbanken? Nein. Die einfachen Regeln bleiben im Formular unter … → Automationen und laufen über dieselbe Engine. Jede Regel lässt sich mit Im Canvas öffnen zu einem Workflow erweitern, siehe Automationen.
Warum sehe ich eine Workflow-Seite nicht? Gäste sehen keine Workflow-Seiten. Sonst gelten die normalen Seitenrechte.
Gibt es Workflows in verschlüsselten Bereichen? Nein – der Server müsste die Inhalte lesen.
Alle Knoten im Einzelnen: Knoten-Referenz.
Ein Arbeitsbereich gehört einem Team: eigene Mitglieder, Gruppen, Bereiche und Vorlagen. Rechte wirken von Arbeitsbereich über Bereich bis zur einzelnen Seite und zum einzelnen Eintrag.

de.heading: Arbeitsbereiche
paragraphs: – Anlegen: Name oben in der Seitenleiste → Arbeitsbereich erstellen. Ob alle das dürfen, legt die Administration fest.
– Wechseln: über denselben Namen; jede Person kann Mitglied mehrerer Arbeitsbereiche sein.
– Einstellungen → Allgemein: Name und Symbol ändern (Name & Symbol). Verlassen und Löschen stehen am Ende in der Gefahrenzone; ist ein Knopf ausgegraut, steht darüber, warum.

Beim Verlassen muss ein letzter Eigentümer vorher unter Einstellungen → Mitglieder jemand anderen zum Eigentümer machen; eigene Bereiche gehen an einen gewählten verbleibenden Eigentümer über. Löschen geht erst, wenn du einen weiteren Arbeitsbereich hast, entfernt alle Inhalte, Vorlagen, Dateien und Freigaben für alle Mitglieder und lässt sich nicht rückgängig machen. Beides bestätigst du mit dem Namen des Arbeitsbereichs.

de.heading: Rollen
paragraphs: Rolle Darf
Eigentümer Alles, dazu Mitglieder, Gruppen, Bereiche (auch ihre Reihenfolge in der Seitenleiste), Tags und Seiteneigenschaften und den Arbeitsbereich selbst verwalten
Bearbeiten Seiten anlegen und ändern, Tags und Eigenschaftswerte vergeben, neue Tags anlegen, kommentieren, teilen
Ansehen Lesen und kommentieren
Gast Nur ausdrücklich freigegebene Seiten und Bereiche, mit Ansehen oder Bearbeiten

de.heading: Mitglieder einladen
paragraphs: Einstellungen → Mitglieder → Mitglied einladen öffnet ein Fenster (auf dem Handy von unten): E-Mail-Adresse, Rolle und – wenn nötig – Als Gast einladen. Ist auf der Instanz E-Mail eingerichtet, bekommt die Person eine Einladung. Sie legt mit dieser Adresse ein Konto an – auch wenn die Registrierung sonst geschlossen ist – oder meldet sich per SSO an; der Arbeitsbereich erscheint, sobald die Adresse bestätigt ist. Ohne E-Mail-Versand kopierst du danach unter Ausstehende Einladungen den Einladungslink (Link kopieren) und schickst ihn ihr selbst.

Einladungslink: Der Link öffnet die Registrierung mit der eingeladenen Adresse schon eingetragen – auch wenn die Registrierung sonst geschlossen ist. Ein Konto lässt sich damit nur für diese Adresse anlegen. Ohne E-Mail-Versand braucht die Person den Link; die Adresse allein reicht dann nicht.

Nur bestätigte Adressen: Ein bestehendes Konto übernimmt eine Einladung automatisch nur, wenn seine Adresse nachweislich ihm gehört – bestätigt per E-Mail-Link, durch die Administration oder vom SSO-Anbieter. Sonst (etwa auf einer Instanz ohne E-Mail-Versand, auf der sich jede Adresse registrieren lässt) zählt nur der Einladungslink: Wer ihn öffnet und sich anmeldet oder registriert, nimmt die Einladung an. Gib den Link deshalb nur der eingeladenen Person.

Wo die Einladung ankommt: Offene Einladungen stehen unter Einstellungen → Mitglieder → Ausstehende Einladungen – mit Rolle, Gast-Status und geteilten Seiten, wann und von wem eingeladen wurde. Dort lassen sie sich erneut senden (mit E-Mail-Versand) oder zurückziehen. Die eingeladene Person findet den Arbeitsbereich im Arbeitsbereich-Wechsel oben links und eine Benachrichtigung im Posteingang – mit einem neuen Konto sofort, mit einem bestehenden beim nächsten Öffnen von Flowplan (bei Single Sign-on beim nächsten Anmelden). Eine Seite lässt sich auch einzeln teilen, ohne den ganzen Arbeitsbereich: Eine Seite mit einer Person teilen.
Bestehende Mitglieder lassen sich Zum Gast machen und umgekehrt Zum Mitglied machen.

de.heading: Gäste
paragraphs: Gäste sind Personen außerhalb des Teams, etwa Kunden oder Freelancer. Sie sehen nur Seiten und Bereiche, die für sie freigegeben wurden, samt Unterseiten, und können keine Seiten anlegen, niemanden einladen und keine Einstellungen ändern. Vorlagen des Arbeitsbereichs sehen sie nicht, nur eigene. Für Personen ganz ohne Konto gibt es stattdessen Links mit eigenen Berechtigungen.

de.heading: Gruppen
paragraphs: Einstellungen → Gruppen & Rechte: Unter Gruppen eine Gruppe anlegen, etwa „Design“ oder „Vertrieb“, und mit Verwalten Mitglieder an- oder abhaken (mit Suche bei vielen Mitgliedern). Unter Zugriff auf Bereiche stellst du je Bereich die Sichtbarkeit ein und darunter je Gruppe Ansehen oder Bearbeiten; einzelnen Seiten gibst du eine Gruppe über Teilen. Neue Mitglieder einer Gruppe erhalten sofort ihre Rechte.
Mit Single Sign-on können Gruppen des Identitätsanbieters Mitglieder und Gruppen automatisch pflegen – siehe SSO-Gruppen zuordnen.

de.heading: Wie Rechte zusammenwirken
paragraphs: – Der Bereich gibt die Grundlage: öffentlich für alle Mitglieder oder privat für Freigegebene.
– Seiten erben die Rechte ihres Bereichs und ihrer übergeordneten Seiten; unter Teilen kommen Personen oder Gruppen dazu.
– Einträge einer Datenbank lassen sich schreibgeschützt oder privat stellen (siehe Datenbanken).
– Eigenschaften einer Datenbank lassen sich nur für Bearbeiter, Eigentümer oder ausgewählte Gruppen sichtbar oder bearbeitbar machen (siehe Sichtbarkeit von Eigenschaften).
– Verknüpfte Datenbanken, Erwähnungen und Links geben nie zusätzliche Rechte: Wer die Quelle nicht lesen darf, sieht sie auch eingebettet nicht.
Eigentümer eines Arbeitsbereichs verwalten auch Bereiche anderer Mitglieder, erhalten dadurch aber keinen Lesezugriff auf deren private Seiten.

Verschlüsselte Bereiche gehen einen Schritt weiter: Dort entscheidet nicht nur das Recht auf dem Server, sondern der Schlüssel. Wer keinen Bereichsschlüssel bekommen hat, liest nichts – auch nicht Eigentümer des Arbeitsbereichs oder die Administration. Siehe Verschlüsselte Bereiche.

de.heading: Workflows: Rechte und „läuft als“
paragraphs: Workflow-Seiten folgen den normalen Seitenrechten: Lesende sehen Status, Ablauf und Läufe; Bearbeitende (Vollmitglieder mit Bearbeitungsrecht) bauen, testen, aktivieren und pausieren. Gäste sehen Workflow-Seiten nicht und können keinen Workflow starten oder freigeben. Ein aktiver Workflow läuft als die Person, die ihn zuletzt aktiviert hat – er sieht und ändert nur, was sie darf, und pausiert, wenn sie ihre Rechte verliert.

de.heading: Speicherkontingent
paragraphs: Jeder Arbeitsbereich kann ein Kontingent haben. Uploads, Kopien, Vorlagen und Importe darüber werden abgelehnt. Die Belegung sehen Admins unter Administration → Arbeitsbereiche.

Whoever administers the instance sees Administration in the sidebar: the instance's first account and everyone it gives the admin right to – with single sign-on also the members of the group in OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP.

en.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The administration opens with an overview. At the top is the state of the instance: problems and notices (linked to the area concerned), six live figures – people active now, people active today (different people since midnight), requests per minute, error rate of the last hour, sign-ins today and the response time (p95: how long the slowest 5 % of the last hour's requests took) – and the requests of the last 24 hours as a chart. The figures refresh every 15 seconds while the page is visible (“Live”). Below, one tile per area with its state and, where it fits, a figure with its trend: active people (Users), the fullest quota (Workspaces), storage of the last 30 days, AI tokens today, changes in the activity log, requests or errors (Monitoring). Errors are marked red, notices yellow. On phones the tiles are a list with a small trend on the right.

The sections are grouped into People (Users, Sign-in & SSO, Workspaces), Data (Storage & backup, Limits & retention, Markdown & Git export), Services (E-mail, Push notifications, AI, Extensions & domains), Security (Threats & incidents, Encryption, Activity log – see Security) and Operations (Monitoring, Maintenance & notices, Instance). Every section starts with a status line – e.g. “Scheduled backup off” with a link to the switch, or “S3 off” with a link to the guide. Every setting has exactly one home. Switches and choices save at once, with “Saving …” or “Saved” next to them; single text fields show Save once you have changed them. Every section has its own address, e.g. /#admin/storage or /#admin/monitoring.

en.heading: Users
paragraphs: All accounts as a searchable table (cards stacked on phones) with their state: Active, Inactive (30 days or more without signing in), Disabled (blocked), plus Admin (local accounts with admin rights and everyone who last signed in with the admin group, also via SSO or LDAP) and E-mail unconfirmed, how many workspaces the person is a member of (the tooltip shows how many of them they own), the storage used against their limit, when they were last here and when the account was created. Clicking a column header – Person, Status, Workspaces, Storage, Last active, Created – sorts by it, a second click reverses the order; at first the most recently active come first. On phones, choose the order under Sort by. At the bottom the table pages through 25, 50 or 100 accounts at a time (“1–25 of 112”). The filter buttons above the table (with their counts) show only active, inactive or disabled accounts, admins or who is here now. Several accounts at once: tick them, then End sessions, Block or Unblock. To give the table room, Sign-in & SSO and Workspaces sit as tabs above the heading on this page instead of beside it.

Who is here right now shows in the Last active column and refreshes every 30 seconds: a green dot for Active now (Flowplan is open and was used in the last few minutes), an amber one for Open · idle for … (open but untouched since then – a tab in the background, too), a grey one with the time of the last visit when Flowplan is closed, and an empty circle for accounts that were never here. For this the open app only reports once a minute that it is open and how long ago it was last used (typing, clicking, scrolling, touching) – not what someone does or which page is open.

Clicking the row or the name opens the account in a side panel (from the bottom on phones). ⋯ at the end of the row is quicker: Details and settings, Sign out everywhere and Block … or Unblock. At the top the panel shows the person's workspaces (with their names, how many they own), when they were last active, when the account was created and how they sign in (e.g. “E-mail + password · SSO · Passkey”), below that the Storage used with a bar – everything they upload or copy, across all workspaces – and:
– Role: for accounts with e-mail and password Member or Admin (someone always administers the instance); for SSO accounts it comes from the sign-in group.
– Storage limit for this person.
– Sessions: on how many devices the person is signed in; Sign out ends all sessions.
– Password (accounts with e-mail and password): Create link makes a reset link valid for two hours – to hand over when the instance does not send e-mails.
– E-mail address: Mark as confirmed for accounts that have not opened the link from the confirmation e-mail yet.
– Folded under More: … (the line names what is inside):

– Own workspaces and Largest file as further limits. Empty = instance default, 0 = unlimited; admins are not limited. As soon as you change one of these limits or the storage limit, the Save limits bar appears at the bottom.
– AI features: if Administration → AI is set to "Selected people", you allow or deny AI per person here.

– Two-factor sign-in (for accounts with an authenticator app): Reset (e.g. for a lost phone) turns off the account's authenticator app; this is recorded in the activity log, and the person gets an e-mail if the instance sends e-mail.

– Sign-in methods: whether the account has a password (or removed it), whether it signs in through LDAP and which SSO identities are connected – with issuer, address, when connected and last used. The person connects and disconnects them under Settings → Account & security.
– Merge accounts: Merge … combines the account with a second account of the same person (see Merge accounts).

– At the end: Block blocks the account at once and ends all sessions; Unblock releases it again. Delete account (Delete …) is possible only once an account is blocked. The dialog says beforehand what happens: name, e-mail, password, passkeys, sessions and personal settings are deleted, as are workspaces where only this person was a member and their private spaces. Shared workspaces get another member as owner if needed; contributions there stay and appear as "Deleted account". Your own account and the last admin account cannot be deleted.

Accounts with e-mail and password are created with Create account (see Sign-in); SSO accounts on their first sign-in via OIDC, and their admin right comes from the group at the provider. Whether people may sign up themselves is set under Sign-in & SSO.

en.heading: Merge accounts
paragraphs: When a person has two accounts – such as a local one and one created at their first SSO sign-in – merge them with Merge … under More in their account's side panel. Choose the other account (accounts with the same e-mail address are listed first) and, with the arrow, which one stays. The preview lists what moves before anything happens.

Everything of the account taken over moves to the one that stays: own pages and spaces, memberships of workspaces and spaces with their shares (the higher role stays; guest only if the person was a guest everywhere), groups, comments and reactions, mentions in comments and documents, assignments and person properties in databases, favourites, collections, sidebar, journal, notifications and their settings, webhooks, calendar and contact connections, time tracking, passkeys, SSO identities, the LDAP and SCIM link and the history in the activity and security logs. Where both accounts have the same thing (a favourite, or the sidebar of a workspace), the one of the account that stays wins.
– Sessions of the account taken over end; its API tokens are revoked (scripts need a new token of the remaining account – so no token suddenly reads another account's data).
– Password: if the remaining account has none, it takes over the other's; otherwise it keeps its own. A local account's admin right goes along.
– Authenticator app: taken over when the remaining account has none; recovery codes must then be created again.
– End-to-end encryption: if only the account taken over has keys, they move. If both have keys, those of the remaining account stay; encrypted spaces only the other account had must be shared again.
– Older versions of documents keep their mentions as they were.

The merge runs as one step – all or nothing –, is recorded in the activity log and as "Accounts merged" in the security log. The account taken over is deleted afterwards. Your own account can only be the one that stays.

en.heading: Sign-in & SSO
paragraphs: – Sign-up & access: Sign-up with email and password (anyone may create an account; without this setting only invited addresses and the instance's first account), Everyone may create workspaces and Block inactive accounts after a number of days without signing in. Blocked accounts lose their sessions and their API tokens stop working; the block appears in the activity log and can be lifted under Users. Delete inactive accounts goes one step further: after a number of days without any use (at least 60, and more than for blocking) an account is deleted – as when an admin deletes it: personal data and the workspaces and private spaces only this person belongs to go, contributions to shared workspaces stay under “Deleted account”. 14 and 3 days before, the person gets an e-mail with the date; signing in before then keeps the account. If it is already blocked, the e-mail asks them to contact the administrators – unblocking it under Users cancels the deletion. Without e-mail delivery set up, for admin accounts and for accounts without an e-mail address nothing is ever deleted. Under Users, “Deleted on …” shows where a deletion is pending; every deletion appears in the activity log.

– Two-factor sign-in: Require two-factor sign-in – not required, only for admins or for all local accounts –, plus how many local accounts already have a second factor. Accounts without an authenticator app and without a passkey set up a second factor right after signing in (Two-factor sign-in). SSO accounts are not affected.

– Sessions: how long people stay signed in – Browser without “Stay signed in” (hours after signing in, default 8), Offer “Stay signed in” in the browser (default off), Browser with “Stay signed in” (7, 30, 90 or 365 days without use, default 7), Desktop and mobile apps (default: stay signed in; or as in the browser without “Stay signed in”) and Apps: end without use (30, 90 or 365 days, default 90). Default follows the SESSION_* environment variables (Configuration); a value chosen here takes precedence. The apps' lifetime applies only to sign-ins the app proves – the hand-off through the browser, or the password with the app's device key; the user agent alone does not count, and older app versions sign in with a password like a browser. See Stay signed in.
– Single sign-on (OIDC): whether a provider is set up, the admin group and Map SSO groups centrally – provider groups get roles and groups in any workspace (SSO groups).
– SCIM tokens and the LDAP directory with their state (User provisioning (SCIM), Sign-in with LDAP).

– Contacts from LDAP: base DN, people filter, sync and More attributes (which LDAP attributes may be mapped beyond the default mapping, on top of LDAP_CONTACTS_ATTRIBUTES) for contacts databases; changes are recorded as security events. See Contacts from LDAP.

en.heading: Workspaces
paragraphs: All workspaces with members, pages, usage (a bar when there is a quota) and Own quota – saved when you leave the field. Empty = default, 0 = unlimited. The default is set under Limits & retention.

en.heading: Storage & backup
paragraphs: The one place for backups:

– Backups: S3 mirror and Litestream with their state, the scheduled Daily database backup – a consistent copy of the database per day, with S3 in the bucket under backups/, otherwise in the data folder –, Hourly instead of daily (meant for encrypted backups in place of Litestream, see Encryption; keep more copies then, e.g. 72 for three days), Backups kept, the last backup and Back up now. The Markdown export still runs once a day.
– Usage: what is local and what is in the bucket, by kind, and how the database is split.
– Whole instance → Download creates a verified copy of the database and files while running. With FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY the file is encrypted (.zip.enc).
– Content: how many workspaces, pages, databases, records, files, accounts and comments there are.

– Move instance: on the old instance Prepare the move (a move token, visible once, valid for 24 hours, revocable; confirmed with your password or a fresh sign-in), then read-only, "moved to …" and Redirect the web interface. On the new instance, also in red, Take over from another instance: first copy with progress, pre-flight check of the settings (names and check values only), Make the source read-only and fetch the last state and Apply on the next restart (previous state as pre-move-…). Guide: Moving an instance.

– At the very end, in red: Restore from backup. An uploaded backup is checked and applied on the next restart; the previous state stays as pre-restore-… in the data directory. An encrypted backup is decrypted with the current or an earlier key. With PostgreSQL it also takes a scheduled backup (flowplan-….dump) – then only the database is replaced, the files stay.
Details: Storage and backups.

en.heading: Limits & retention
paragraphs: Setting Effect
Storage per workspace For workspaces without a quota of their own.
Storage per person For people without a limit of their own; everything they upload or copy.
Own workspaces per person How many workspaces a person may own.
Largest upload The limit per file in MB. Also applies to importing an AFFiNE workspace file (at least 100 MB; FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_MB takes precedence).
Keep versions Days after which automatic versions are deleted.
Empty the trash after Days after which deleted pages, spaces, database records and templates are deleted permanently with their files (1–3650, default 30, 0 = never automatically). See Trash.
Empty fields fall back to the environment variables. Everyone sees their limits and the storage they use under Settings → Account & security → Your limits.

en.heading: Workflows
paragraphs: Limits & retention → Workflows holds the limits of workflows: runs per minute (per workflow and workspace), steps per run, cascade depth, items per “For each”, AI tokens and e-mails per workflow and day, how long runs are kept, the longest wait, active workflows per workspace, the HTTP node (on/off, only certain hosts, internal addresses) and e-mails to addresses outside the members. Left empty, the value from the environment applies. Next to it, monitoring shows the load: active workflows, runs per minute, waiting and running steps, the oldest step due, the failure rate and today's AI tokens.

en.heading: Markdown & Git export
paragraphs: Choose pages and databases for the Markdown export, switch on the Git export of spaces, and the (deprecated) instance Git repository – see Markdown export and Git.

en.heading: E-mail
paragraphs: Sending e-mail shows the configured server, the sender, the queue and the last error; without SMTP a note with the variables (E-mail (SMTP)). Test e-mail checks the connection right away.

en.heading: Push notifications
paragraphs: Whether notifications can reach the apps and through which service (/#admin/push). The overview's tile shows the relay with a green, yellow or red badge – e.g. “Reachable (85 ms)” – and the deliveries of the last 24 hours; the same tile is under Monitoring → Health.

– Push relay: the address in use – the official https://push.flowplan.org or your own from PUSH_RELAY_URL (credentials in the address are never shown) –, whether it is on and otherwise exactly why not (PUSH_RELAY=off, APP_URL not an HTTPS address, PUSH_RELAY_URL invalid), the APP_URL the relay knows the instance by, and whether /.well-known/flowplan-push is published.

– Reachability: the instance requests GET /healthz – at most 5 seconds, HTTPS only, following no redirects – and shows “Reachable” with the response time (and the relay's version if it names one) or the reason: timeout, connection refused, DNS, TLS, redirect, HTTP status. It also fetches its own /.well-known/flowplan-push at APP_URL, as the relay does, and checks that the current signing key is listed. If that fails from inside, it is only a warning: behind NAT or a proxy that does not resolve its own address internally this is normal – what counts is that the relay reaches it from outside (test notification). A result is kept for a minute; Check now checks again at once.
– Signing key: key ids with their status (signing, waiting, retiring) and dates. Rotate key … asks first and rotates as described in Push relay and end-to-end encryption, optionally immediately.

– Deliveries of the last 24 hours per channel (relay, Expo, Web Push) and result (delivered, gone, forbidden, invalid, rate limited, error), the last delivery through the relay, the last error as a code (e.g. signature HTTP 401 or unreachable), the queue and the registered devices per channel. Counted only while the usage statistics are on (see Monitoring).
– Expo and Web Push: MOBILE_PUSH on or off, what MOBILE_PUSH_CONTENT sends along, where the VAPID keys come from and whether WEB_PUSH_SUBJECT is set.
The answers never contain tokens, keys or push addresses. /api/admin/push is for signed-in administrators only, never for API tokens.

en.heading: Chat apps
paragraphs: Administration → Chat apps governs notifications to chat apps. At the top: allowed services, the instance's bot, active connections and those switched off after errors, and the deliveries of the last 24 hours.

– Allowed services: Telegram, Gotify, ntfy and Matrix can be switched off one by one (default: FLOWPLAN_MESSENGERS). Services switched off get no more messages; people's connections stay stored and resume when the service is switched on again.

– Instance Telegram bot: bot token from @BotFather and optionally an own API address (Bot API server or relay/proxy, also in the own network). Check and save asks Telegram for the bot with getMe and stores the token only when it is accepted – encrypted, shown only as “…abcd”. Remove bot deletes it (a token from FLOWPLAN_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN then applies again). A conflict with a webhook or another program polling the bot shows under Last error.

– Server addresses: empty allows any public server; otherwise only the hosts listed, one per line (*.example.org for subdomains). api.telegram.org and ntfy.sh always work. Internal addresses need FLOWPLAN_MESSENGER_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true.
Changing the bot is recorded as the security event “Instance Telegram bot changed”, changing services and hosts as “Security-relevant setting changed” – both also in the activity log.

en.heading: AI
paragraphs: Optional and off by default: provider (Ollama, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini), who may use AI, individual features and users' own keys. A switch of its own: On-device AI (Apple) – allowed by default because nothing leaves the device. Everything in AI.

en.heading: Extensions & domains
paragraphs: Block extensions from any HTTPS address (off: only from PLUGIN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS) and Custom domains for publications – see Block extensions and Coolify and reverse proxies.

en.heading: Encryption
paragraphs: The key ID, earlier keys, how many files in the bucket are not yet encrypted with this key (Encrypt existing objects catches up), and what leaves the server unencrypted regardless (Litestream, Git export). See Encryption.

en.heading: Activity log
paragraphs: The latest changes with person, action and affected resource – such as shares, role changes, deletions, settings and the billing status of time entries –, searchable and filtered by person and kind, a list on phones. Under Export, optionally pick a from and to date (UTC, as stored) and download the log as CSV (semicolons, with BOM, for Excel) or as JSON. In the CSV, values a spreadsheet would run as a formula start with an apostrophe. Only signed-in administrators can export, never API tokens.

en.heading: Monitoring
paragraphs: Health, usage and events of the instance – live: five key figures at the top (Active 24 h, Storage, Deliveries 7 days, AI tokens 14 days, Errors 24 h) with their trend and, where it fits, a comparison with the period before, below them cards in two columns with charts, queues, background workers, refused requests, alerts by webhook and the usage statistics. Details under Operations and troubleshooting.

en.heading: Maintenance & notices
paragraphs: Notice for everyone – a banner for everyone until you clear it – the maintenance notice with start and end, which disappears by itself afterwards, and banners to click away that each person sees until they close them – e.g. for the apps or your Discord server (Maintenance & notices).

en.heading: Instance
paragraphs: Setting Effect
Instance name Shown when signing in, in the sidebar and in the browser tab.
Public demo Visitors try Flowplan without an account, see Demo.

Version Running version, commit (linked to GitHub) and build date. Docker images from our workflow know their commit; with Coolify it comes from SOURCE_COMMIT. For your own build pass --build-arg GIT_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD), otherwise it says "commit unknown". When a newer version is out, a notice with How to update shows there.
Admin group The SSO or LDAP group from OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP.

Everyone sees version, licence and source code under Settings → About Flowplan; for our images it also says whether it is a beta or a release (own builds: --build-arg FLOWPLAN_CHANNEL=beta or release). If you run modified code, name its source with FLOWPLAN_SOURCE_URL; FLOWPLAN_HIDE_SPONSOR=true hides the link to GitHub Sponsors (Configuration).
Below, More instance settings leads to the sections that earlier instance settings moved to.

en.heading: Demo
paragraphs: The demo is off on every instance until an administrator switches it on under Administration → Instance → Public demo.

Then the address /demo of your instance starts a demo (on flowplan.org the button Try the demo links there). Without an account it creates a demo guest with an example workspace of its own. Every demo gets fresh example pages that show all features: a welcome page, an editor tour with all blocks, a project database with relation, rollup, formula, recurrence and all views (table, board, calendar, timeline, gallery, list, feed, chart, form), a whiteboard, a journal and a small wiki.
– The demo ends with End demo, on signing out, after 45 minutes without activity and after three hours at the latest. Then the account, workspace, pages and files are deleted completely.
– Demo guests cannot take anything outside: no publishing, no share links, no invitations, no further workspaces, no public forms, no administration.
– Every demo workspace has 25 MB of storage. New demos are limited to five per hour and address and 40 at the same time.
– Running and total started demos are shown under Administration → Monitoring → Instance in numbers.

Optional AI for writing, summaries, questions to your workspace and databases – off by default, completely local with Ollama if you like, or with a key for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible service. In the apps for iPhone, iPad and Mac optionally also right on the device with Apple Intelligence.

[!NOTE] AI in Flowplan is always optional. After installation it is off. Administrators decide whether it is available, which provider is used, who may use it and which features are allowed. Everyone can switch it off again for themselves and decide which pages the AI may read. With Ollama your text never leaves the server. The one exception to “off by default”: on-device AI (Apple) is allowed because nothing leaves the device – administrators and everyone can switch it off too.

en.heading: Principles
paragraphs: – Off until someone switches it on – on the instance and for every person. The one exception is on-device AI (Apple): it is allowed because nothing leaves the device, and it can be switched off just the same.

– Every feature separately: writing assistant, summaries, questions to the workspace, AI in databases, AI actions and AI on whiteboards can each be allowed or switched off by administrators and by every person.
– Only with your permissions: the AI never reads more than you may see yourself – and only what you allow it (What the AI may access).
– You see where your text goes: every AI feature names the provider and whether data leaves the server.
– Keys stay secret: API keys are stored encrypted and never shown again (Security of keys).

en.heading: Providers
paragraphs: Provider Data leaves the server Typical address
Ollama no (when Ollama runs on your own server or network) http://ollama:11434
OpenAI-compatible yes, to the chosen service – except for local servers such as LM Studio, vLLM or LocalAI https://api.openai.com/v1, https://api.mistral.ai/v1, https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
Anthropic (Claude) yes, to Anthropic https://api.anthropic.com
Google Gemini yes, to Google https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com
You enter the model freely – any model ID the provider knows. Test connection checks address, key and model with a short request.

en.heading: Ollama: completely local
paragraphs: Ollama runs open models on your own server. Flowplan's compose.yaml includes a matching service that only starts on request:
docker compose --profile ai up -d
In .env:
OLLAMA_URL=http://ollama:11434

Then choose the provider Ollama under Administration → AI. Load installed models shows what is there; Download model fetches more models with a progress bar, such as llama3.1, qwen2.5 or mistral. For search by meaning, also download an embedding model such as nomic-embed-text and enter it under Embedding model.

[!TIP] How well and how fast local models answer depends on the server. Small models (3–8 billion parameters) run on current CPUs; a graphics card makes them much faster. If Ollama runs on another machine in your network, enter its address – addresses in your own network are allowed for the instance provider.

en.heading: On-device AI (Apple)
paragraphs: [!NOTE] Optional and can be switched off at any time. In the Flowplan apps for iPhone, iPad and Mac, Flowplan can use Apple Intelligence right on the device. The text does not leave the device – it goes neither to the Flowplan server nor to an AI provider. AI through the server is not affected and stays available.

What you need: the Flowplan app for iPhone or iPad with iOS/iPadOS 26 or later, or the desktop app 1.2.0 or later on a Mac with macOS 26 or later, a device that supports Apple Intelligence (such as iPhone 15 Pro or later, iPad and Mac with an M chip), and Apple Intelligence switched on (Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri). In the browser and on other devices this path does not exist. The server needs a Flowplan version newer than 0.7.0 (currently the beta image).
What runs on the device – the light actions on an open page:
– the writing assistant for selected text (improve, rephrase, shorten, expand, explain more simply, change tone, translate, as a list/table, your own instruction) and free writing at the cursor,
– the summary of the open page, a record or a voice note – with key points and open tasks that the model extracts in a structured way.
What stays on the server: questions to the workspace, AI in databases, AI actions and summaries of database views. They still need an instance provider.

Results from the device carry the label On this device, and the bottom line reads “Apple Intelligence · only on this device”. The answer appears piece by piece as usual, and Stop cancels on the device too.

Limits: the on-device model is small and has little room (about 4,000 tokens for instruction, text and answer together). For the writing assistant that is enough for a few paragraphs; longer pages are summarised in parts. What is too long is taken over by the server if you may use AI there – otherwise Flowplan says the text is too long, or summarises only the beginning. If the model declines a request under Apple's safety rules, it is not sent to the server instead.
Switching it on and off:

– Everyone under Settings → AI → On this device (Apple): When possible (default) – on the device when it can, otherwise on the server; Only without AI on the server – the device only when the server offers no AI; Off – Flowplan never asks the device. It also shows whether Apple Intelligence on this device is available, turned off in Settings or not supported. Switching off Use AI features turns off on-device AI too.

– Administrators under Administration → AI → On-device AI (Apple) for the whole instance (or with FLOWPLAN_AI_DEVICE=off, configuration). The main switch Turn on AI applies to AI through the server; on-device AI has its own switch and is allowed by default – also without a provider.

– On the Mac also in the desktop app under Settings… → Apple Intelligence (optional) → Use Apple Intelligence on this Mac – on by default where it is available. Off, the app never starts the model and the instance cannot reach it. This switch applies to this Mac only.
– Pages and spaces closed to the AI stay closed, as do your own rules, the switches of the individual features, Selected people and Guests too.

Encrypted spaces: in end-to-end encrypted spaces there is otherwise no AI, because the server does not know the text. On the device there is: the writing assistant (AI button in the toolbar) and the summary work with the decrypted text on the device – nothing goes to the server, not even as a fallback.

[!TIP] Apple's Writing Tools (proofread, rewrite, summarise in the text menu) also work right in the editor in the app for iPhone and iPad. They are part of the system and run independently of these settings.

en.heading: Writing assistant
paragraphs: The writing assistant edits selected text or writes new text at the caret. It is available to people who may edit the page – if administrators allowed AI and the writing assistant and you haven't turned it off under Settings → AI.
How to open it:
– Select text → AI in the text menu.
– ⌘ J (Ctrl J): works on the selection; without one, on the current line; on an empty line, a free prompt opens.
– /ai or /ki in the block menu: free prompt at the caret.
Action What happens
Improve Fixes spelling, grammar and punctuation and changes as little as possible.
Rephrase Same content, other words.
Shorten To about half; what matters stays.
Expand More explanation and examples, without inventing facts.
Explain more simply Short sentences, plain words.
Change tone Factual, friendly or casual.
Translate Into a language you choose – by default German text to English, other text to German.
As a list / As a table Restructures the text.
What should the AI do? Your own instruction, e.g. "Turn this into an email".
Free writing (/ai, ⌘ J on an empty line): describe what you want – e.g. "Write an introduction about …". With Page as context (on by default), the page's content is sent along.

The AI answers in the language of the text; for free writing, in the language of your instruction. The answer first appears in a preview under the text, not in the document; a pulsing caret shows more is coming, Stop ends it early. Then:
– Replace (for free writing Insert) – the answer replaces the selection or the empty line.
– Insert below – under the paragraph or list.
– Retry – the same request again; Other action – back to the choices; Discard – nothing changes.

Headings, lists, tasks, tables, code and callouts are inserted as real blocks. Inserting is a single step that ⌘ Z undoes, and it works during collaboration like any other edit. Inserted blocks briefly light up in the accent colour – display only, not saved and invisible to others.

[!NOTE] Images in answers are not inserted (only their alt text), and links only if they point to http(s), e-mail or Flowplan itself. This stops manipulated content from sending text out through image addresses.

en.heading: Linking existing pages
paragraphs: With Link existing pages (in the writing assistant, on by default; your browser remembers the choice) Flowplan looks for up to eight pages of the workspace that fit your instruction and the selected text – with the same search as Ask your workspace – and gives the AI their titles and a short excerpt. Where a page really fits, the AI links it in its text. This works for every action, free writing and the summary of a voice note.

– The links already show in the preview; below it, Linked: … lists the linked pages. They are inserted as real page links – like [[ in the editor: they appear in backlinks, follow a rename and survive the Markdown export.

– Only pages the AI may read for you are offered (see What the AI may access) – never the page you are writing in, and never closed, private, deleted or PIN-protected content. The AI only knows the pages by number; Flowplan sets the links itself. Addresses the AI makes up never become links.

– Lists of pages: when you ask for a list ("List all Docker Compose pages with links"), the AI also gets the titles of further matching pages (at most 120, 30 with local AI) – without excerpts. Once the answer is complete, Flowplan links every list item that names exactly the title of a page (also at its start, as in "Gitea – Git server"). Upper and lower case, emoji, hyphens and spaces do not matter ("it-tools" finds "🛠️ IT-Tools"). A link is only set when exactly one page the AI may read for you has that title – with two pages called "Notes" the item stays text; Flowplan never guesses.
– Introductions and closing lines such as "Sure! Here is the list:" or "I hope this helps!" do not end up in the document – not as a bullet of their own either.
– The on-device AI and end-to-end encrypted spaces do not link: that would mean searching the text on the server.
– Administrators can switch the Link pages feature off, and so can you under Settings → AI.

en.heading: Summaries
paragraphs: The AI returns a short summary, the key points and the open tasks – in the language of the content.

– Page: page menu … → Summarise with AI. The result appears in a side panel with Insert as callout at the top (summary and key points as a callout at the start of the page), Insert tasks as checklist (below the caret), Copy and Retry.

– Database: the AI button in the toolbar summarises the records of the current view – with its filters, search and sort order, at most 300 records. The panel says how many were included ("120 of 340 records").
– Record: AI button in the record's header; callout and checklist go into the record's document.
– Voice note: if the server turns voice notes into text (Voice notes), Then summarise with AI summarises the transcript; Insert below puts the summary under it.

Long pages are read in parts: each part is summarised, then the parts are merged (in smaller parts with local AI). Very long content is cut after twelve parts, and the panel says so. Records you may not see or that are closed to the AI are left out.

en.heading: Where your data goes
paragraphs: Every AI panel names the provider at the bottom, e.g. "Ollama · llama3.1 · local" or "… · Data goes to api.openai.com". With local AI the text stays on your server; otherwise the selected text, your instruction and – with Page as context and summaries – the page content go to that provider. Flowplan loads page and database content itself on the server and first checks that the AI may read it.
On pages the AI may not read, every AI entry is greyed out with the hint "The AI has no access to this page" – also for selected text. The server refuses such requests as well.

en.heading: Ask your workspace
paragraphs: Ask AI (sidebar, ⌘ ⌥ A or Ctrl Alt A, ⌘ K → "Ask AI …" or the button in search) answers questions about your pages and databases – such as "When is the next heating maintenance due?" or "What did we decide about onboarding?".

A panel at the right edge: on a computer and an iPad, Ask AI opens as a panel to the right of the page; the page gets narrower, nothing is covered. You can keep writing, scrolling and opening other pages while the answer is written – it keeps going, and the conversation stays when you switch pages. A click on a source opens the page beside it, the panel stays open. The panel starts at about 420 px and takes at most 45 % of the window; drag its left edge (or use the arrow keys) to change the width – a double-click resets it – and this browser remembers it. The page beside it lays out for the room it has left: when it gets tight it switches to its narrow layout, and the table of contents collapses to a button that opens the outline as a list. In narrow windows (below about 1100 px) the panel lies over the page instead of squeezing it; Pin puts it beside the page, Unpin over it again – this browser remembers that too. Esc in the panel, the × or the same shortcut close it again. Ask AI and the comments share the right edge: opening one closes the other. In focus mode the panel is hidden. On phones, Ask AI is a sheet above the bottom bar; swiping it down (or the arrow at its top) shrinks it to an "AI is answering …" button – the answer keeps going.

– This page: with a page open, the This page switch sits above the question field – on by default. The whole page then goes to the AI with your question: text, headings, lists, tables and code blocks as Markdown. So the AI answers questions like "What does this code block do?" or "Summarise this page" from the page itself; it appears as source [1], marked This page, and the search in the chosen scope runs as well. If the page is too long for the model, only its beginning goes along (about 60,000 characters, 12,000 with local AI), and a note below the answer says so. The server first checks that you may read the page and that the AI may read it; closed pages and end-to-end encrypted spaces have no switch. A click turns it off for this page; when you open another page it is on again.

– Suggest as changes: below an answer given with This page, this button puts the answer into the page as suggested changes – for example after "Switch the stack to Postgres 16" or "Fix the spelling in the second section". Nothing is overwritten: removed words are struck through, new ones are marked, each change is a suggestion of its own with your name and "(AI)", which you accept or reject one by one in the Suggestions bar (or all at once). In a code block the lines are compared – only the changed lines are suggested. New paragraphs, list items or code blocks go to the right place; if you reject them they disappear completely. If a passage has changed in the meantime or Flowplan cannot find it again unambiguously, it is not applied – the panel says how many suggestions were inserted and how many were not. The button only appears when you may edit the page (and it is not locked); people who may only read get the answer. It works with every provider, local ones too.

– The answer names its sources as numbered references [1], [2] …; a click opens the page or record. The references come from the search, never from the AI's text. Below the answer you see the sources it actually cites; further sources found sit behind n more sources and unfold on a click (if an answer cites none, the first three show).
– If the AI finds nothing that fits, it answers "I found nothing about that." instead of making something up.

– Where to look: the whole workspace, the open page with its sub-pages, or one space – in the menu at the top left. With All my workspaces (its last entry) the question searches every workspace you belong to – each only when AI is usable for you there (not as a guest when guests have no AI, for example), and with your rules for each workspace. Sources from other workspaces carry its name; a click switches there.

– Questions about Flowplan itself: The Flowplan help – this documentation, in English and German – is built into the app and searched along with Whole workspace and All my workspaces. Questions like “How do I set up two-factor sign-in?” or “Where do I choose the AI provider?” are answered from the help; such sources are marked Flowplan help and open the matching section on docs.flowplan.org. Only the Flowplan help in the menu asks there alone. The help lives in the app itself – no request goes out for it, and it matches the installed version.

– Journal and dates: journal days reach the AI with their date, and so does today's date. Questions like “What was the last thing with Batu?” or “What did I last …” take the newest matching day. A name or a rare word finds its pages even when a common word of the question hits many other pages.
– Formatting: answers are formatted – bold, italic, lists (also nested), code and links; the source numbers stay clickable.

– Copy: Copy below the sources takes the whole answer. Each code block also has its own Copy code button in its top right corner – handy when the AI puts a command, a snippet or a ready text (such as an issue to file) into a code block. This applies wherever AI answers appear formatted.
– Propose actions: below an answer, the AI can propose what to create from it – see AI actions.
– Conversation: follow-up questions take the last questions and answers into account; New conversation starts over. The conversation stays in this browser tab only and is not stored on the server.

– The search uses the full-text index; the best-matching passages go with your question to the provider shown at the top of the panel. The AI only reads what you may read and what is open to the AI (What the AI may access). A page's tags and property values count as part of its text.
– While the answer is written, a shimmer and a typing cursor show progress; the sources appear one after another.

en.heading: Semantic search (optional)
paragraphs: Questions in Chinese, Japanese, Korean or Thai are split into words even though these languages don't use spaces. "浦东新区的发票在哪里" searches for 浦东新区 and 发票; small particles like 的 are left out.
In addition to full text, Flowplan can store content as vectors ("embeddings"). Ask AI then also finds passages without the same words – "trip" finds "company outing".
– Set an embedding model at the instance provider:
– Ollama: download nomic-embed-text (under Administration → AI → Download model or ollama pull nomic-embed-text) and enter it.
– OpenAI-compatible: e.g. text-embedding-3-small; Gemini: text-embedding-004. Anthropic has no embeddings.
– Turn on semantic search and save. Or via the environment: FLOWPLAN_AI_SEMANTIC_SEARCH=on and FLOWPLAN_AI_EMBEDDING_MODEL=nomic-embed-text.
– A background job embeds changed pages and records chunk by chunk; unchanged chunks are not embedded again. At most FLOWPLAN_AI_EMBED_PER_HOUR chunks per hour (default 5,000).
– Never embedded: journals with a PIN, pages and spaces closed to AI, and the trash. Permissions and personal AI rules apply to every question.
– Semantic search always uses the instance provider. People using their own provider search full text only.

– Storage: 4 bytes per dimension and chunk (up to about 900 characters) – with nomic-embed-text (768 dimensions) about 3 KB per chunk, roughly three to four times the text; with 1,536 dimensions about 6 KB. Only a checksum of each chunk is stored, not its text. The administration shows the number and size.
– Switching off deletes all vectors; changing the model rebuilds them.
– For very large instances (hundreds of thousands of chunks) there is no vector index yet; the search stays correct but gets slower.

en.heading: Related pages
paragraphs: Below a page and in a database record, Related pages shows up to eight pages and records that belong with it. It also works without AI:
– Without semantic search, it counts links from the page, links to the page, pages with the same links, the same tags (multi-select) for records, and similar titles in the full-text index.

– With semantic search, pages with similar content are added ("by meaning"). Only the vectors already stored are compared – no request goes to the provider, no text leaves the server. The open page must be readable for the AI; every hit passes the same rules as Ask AI.
Only what you may read is shown – no private spaces of others, no hidden records, nothing from the trash or locked journals.

en.heading: AI actions
paragraphs: From an answer of Ask AI, from the writing assistant (Propose actions below the answer) or from the transcript of a meeting, the AI proposes actions:
Action What happens
Create page A new page with title and content in a space where you may create pages.
Create tasks Tasks at the end of a document, optionally with an assignee (@mention) and due date – they appear in My tasks like ones you wrote.
Append text A summary, for example, at the end of a document.
Create record / Change record In a database, only in properties you may change and only with valid values (existing options, members, dates).

Nothing happens without you: the proposals appear as a preview with checkboxes. What is not possible – a space without write access, a restricted property or a database closed to the AI – is greyed out with the reason. Only Run creates the chosen actions.

– Actions run in your name and with your permissions; the server checks each action again when running it. Version history, notifications, automations and webhooks work as for your own change; the audit log records ai.action.
– Undo: created pages and records can be taken back right in the result (they go to the trash); appended text and changed records are in the version history.

– The AI only sees a catalogue of the spaces, databases, properties and members you may write to and the AI may read – no content beyond that. The AI's answer is plain JSON and is never executed directly.
– Like every other feature, AI actions can be switched off by the administration and under Settings → AI.

en.heading: Using data from databases
paragraphs: When you name a database in your request, the AI reads its records and works with the real values instead of a template full of placeholders. Example: "Create documentation from the Server table" gives you a table of your servers with their IP addresses and URLs.
The AI reads a database when
– you name its title in the request (case does not matter, quotes are fine, e.g. "Server"),
– you link it in the request or the text (page link with [[),
– it is linked or embedded as a view in the open document and your request speaks of a table or database ("Summarise the linked table") – in the writing assistant only with "Page as context",
– in "Ask AI" the question is limited to the open database, or a source found is the database itself.

This applies to AI actions, the writing assistant (free prompt with /ai and a custom instruction for a selection) and "Ask AI". Below the answer or above the proposed actions you see which data was read, e.g. "Data from: Server (12 records)". In "Ask AI" the database is listed as a source.
What the AI sees:

– only records you may see and the AI may read – no private records of others, nothing from journals with a PIN, from pages and spaces closed to AI, from end-to-end encrypted spaces, from the trash, or from places you excluded in your AI settings,
– only properties visible to you (per-property read permissions apply); relations, formulas, rollups, files, progress, time and sprints are not sent, nor the text of the records' documents,
– the records in the database's order.

Limits: at most 3 databases and 200 records per request and about 40,000 characters (about 8,000 in the writing assistant with a model on your own server). If not everything fits, the data says so ("… and 57 more records") and the AI points it out. Apple's on-device AI does not read databases.

en.heading: AI on whiteboards
paragraphs: On whiteboards, AI in the toolbar opens three features:
– Group by theme (AI): arrange the selected notes – or all in view – by theme in labelled columns.
– Summarise as a page: a new page next to the board with summary, themes, decisions, open questions and action items (optionally as real tasks with person and due date), linking back.
– Create with AI …: a mind map or a flowchart from a description.

When creating database records from notes there is also Split with AI: the AI fills further properties from the note's text, with a preview before anything is created. Creating the records itself needs no AI.

– People who may edit the board can use it. The AI's answer is strictly checked (only known notes, shapes and properties, limits) and then applied like your own edit – live for everyone, undone in one step.

– Only the text of the elements concerned goes to the provider – without hidden notes and without linked pages or records the AI may not read. When creating, only your description goes there, nothing from the board. The audit log records ai.whiteboard.
– The AI on whiteboards feature can be switched off like all others by administrators and under Settings → AI; it is on as soon as AI is on.

en.heading: AI property
paragraphs: When adding a property, choose AI property and write an instruction naming other properties in curly braces:
– Summarize {Description} in one sentence
– Category from {Title}: one of Novel, Non-fiction, Crime
– {Content} stands for the record's page content.

The output is text, select, multi-select (existing options only – invented ones are dropped) or number. Since an AI property is a normal property, filters, sorting, grouping, forms and exports work as usual.
– Fill in for all in the property dialog computes all records in the background; an indicator shows how many values are still being computed.
– In a record, Recompute computes one value right away and shows when and with which model it was made.

– Recompute automatically when the properties used change: values follow changes with a short delay and within the AI limits. This runs in the name of the person who switched it on or last changed the instruction. If they lose access, it stops; if AI is off on the instance, it pauses.
– Values are written like edits: with version history, automations and webhooks. Freshly computed cells light up briefly.
– Viewers, guests and API tokens cannot write AI values. Private records and databases closed to AI are skipped.

en.heading: Fill in fields with AI
paragraphs: Select records in the table → Fill in with AI → choose a property (e.g. tags). The AI fills only empty cells – from the title, the other properties and the content; for selects only with existing options.

en.heading: Create a database with AI
paragraphs: New page → Database → Create with AI and describe it, e.g. "Reading list with author, genre, status, rating". The AI proposes properties with types, select options and a few example records. You rename, remove properties or leave out the examples – only Create page creates the database. The proposal is checked strictly (allowed types, at most 25 properties and 30 options, matching example values); nothing from the AI's answer is executed.

en.heading: AI in workflows
paragraphs: Workflows have four AI nodes: Summarize, Classify (into categories or the options of a select, with an “unclear” port), Extract fields and Custom prompt (text or JSON). They use the AI feature AI in workflows – admins switch it off under Administration → AI, everyone for themselves in their own AI settings.
– Budget: at most 100,000 tokens per workflow and day (FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_AI_TOKENS_PER_DAY); when it is used up, the node fails with a message.
– What the AI reads: only pages and records the person the workflow runs as may see and that are open to the AI; blocked pages and journals with a PIN stay out.

– Prompt injection: foreign text (e-mails, webhooks, page contents) is marked in the prompt as data. The AI only returns data, never actions – its answer is checked (categories from the list, typed fields). Where an AI output decides recipients, an address or a target, the check warns before activating.
– AI builder: “Draft with AI” builds a draft from one sentence; the AI only sees names of databases, properties and pages, no contents, and it counts against your personal AI allowance.

en.heading: For admins
paragraphs: Under Administration → AI:
– Turn on AI.
– Choose the instance provider (or No provider, see below), enter address, model and – if needed – the API key. Test connection.
– Who may use AI:
– All or Selected people – enable the latter per person under Administration → Users: click the person, then More → AI features.
– Guests too – when off, guests have no AI features.

– People may add their own provider/key – then everyone can set up their own provider with their own key in their settings. This also works with no instance provider at all: people use AI with their own account at a provider, without the instance paying for it.
– Features: allow or forbid each one separately. Optionally turn on semantic search.
– On-device AI (Apple): allowed by default, independently of the switch in step 1 (on-device AI). Switch it off if there should be no AI on the instance at all.
– Save.
This covers three typical setups:
Setup Settings
