Draw /draw, /sketch, /handwriting Handwriting and sketches with a pen or finger (Handwriting in documents)
Linked database /db A view of an existing database
Two columns /columns Content side by side
Embed /embed Players for YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Spotify, Figma, CodePen; a link card otherwise
Spoiler /spoiler Hidden text, revealed by a click
Voice note /voice Record (up to two hours) and insert as audio, optionally also as a transcript
Synced block /sync Content that stays the same on several pages
Insert synced block /sync Show an existing synced block
Divider /hr A horizontal line
AI /ai, /ki Let the AI write (when switched on)
Footnote /footnote, /fußnote Numbered note at the end of the page (Footnotes)
Citation /cite, /zitat Cite a source – DOI, BibTeX or Zotero (Citations)
Bibliography /bibliography, /references All cited works as a list

Tables: with the cursor in a table, a small bar appears right below it: insert a row above or below, a column left or right; under … turn the header row on or off and delete a row, a column or the whole table. When the end of the table is off screen, the bar stays at the bottom of the visible area – above the keyboard on phones. Tab moves to the next cell and adds a row in the last one.

Convert a table to a database: when a table outgrows itself, choose Convert to database under … in the table bar. Flowplan creates a database from it below the document and puts an embedded view of it where the table was. The first row gives the column names, the first column becomes the records' titles. The other columns get their type from the filled cells: number (German or English separators), date (2026-11-04 or 04.11.2026), checkbox (✓, x, yes/no, ja/nein, true/false), URL, otherwise text. The database is named after the table's caption, else the nearest heading above it, else "Table". ⌘/Ctrl+Z brings the table back. Limits as for CSV import: up to 80 columns and 5,000 rows. Encrypted spaces don't offer it; in a database record the new database goes to the top of the space.

Hiding the keyboard (phone): while you write, the formatting bar sits above the on-screen keyboard. Its last button on the right, Hide keyboard, closes the keyboard so you see more of the document; the text and the cursor position stay. A tap into the text brings it back. In the content of a database record the bar sits above the keyboard in the same way while you write. For every other text field – titles of pages, databases and records, tags, properties, the name in the New page dialog, search fields, comments – the same button appears as a round button on the right, just above the keyboard. This works in the browser and in the apps.

en.heading: Voice notes and meetings
paragraphs: /voice opens the recorder: tap the microphone, speak, Stop recording – up to two hours, enough for a meeting. You can listen to the recording or discard it; Insert puts it into the page as audio (within the instance's upload limit). If speech recognition is set up, the spoken words follow below as text; otherwise the dialog only offers the audio.
– Long recordings go to the server in parts; it puts them together and sends them to speech recognition. WHISPER_MAX_MB limits the size (default 200).

– Transcript with timestamps: if speech recognition returns segments with times (OpenAI-compatible verbose_json, e.g. faster-whisper-server, speaches or whisper.cpp), a collapsible Transcript · duration block appears with one paragraph per passage and its timestamp (00:04, 1:02:05).

– Speakers: only when the service itself separates speakers (diarization, switched on with WHISPER_DIARIZE=on for servers that know diarize) and returns a speaker per segment, each passage starts with Speaker 1, Speaker 2 … Flowplan never guesses speakers from pauses. If the service only knows plain JSON, the text is inserted as paragraphs as before.
– Then summarise with AI summarises the transcript (Summaries).
– In the apps for iPhone, iPad and Android the app records; iPhone and iPad turn the words into text on the device, without speech recognition on the server (Voice notes in pages).

– Generate tasks and summary (when AI actions are on for you): the AI proposes a summary with decisions and a task list with assignees and dates – as a preview with checkboxes; only Run adds them to the page.

en.heading: Table of contents
paragraphs: The list icon at the top right of a document opens the table of contents beside the text – in every document, journal days and database records included. It is built from the headings and grows while you write, marks the section you are reading and jumps to a heading on click. Whether it is open is remembered in this browser for all documents. On a phone a round button at the bottom right opens it.

en.heading: Collapsing sections
paragraphs: Every heading can be collapsed: the small arrow to the left of a heading (it shows on hover; on touch devices and for collapsed headings always) hides everything below it – up to the next heading of the same or a higher level. A collapsed heading shows how much is hidden behind it (… 3 blocks); another click expands it again. With the cursor in the heading, ⌘ ⌥ Enter does the same. On a phone the arrow sits at the end of the heading, in right-to-left text on the other side.

– Collapse / expand all sections: in a document's page menu ⋯, at the top of the table of contents, in quick search (> sections) or with ⌘ ⌥ X and ⌘ ⌥ O (changeable). With a database record open, it applies to the record's text.
– Just for you: what is collapsed is remembered on this device (per page or record) – it does not change the document, others still see everything. Documents you open for the first time are expanded.

– Nothing gets lost: when the cursor gets into a collapsed part (arrow keys, undo, a click in the table of contents), it expands. So it does when Find on page (⌘ F) goes to a match inside, or a search hit, backlink or notification leads there. You can keep typing in the collapsed heading itself; it stays collapsed.
– Moving: dragging a collapsed heading by its handle ⋮⋮ (or moving it with ⌘ ⇧ ↑/↓) takes its whole section along.
– Printing and PDF always show everything; so do export, presentations and published pages.

– Headings directly in the document collapse – in reading mode and in encrypted spaces too. Headings inside callouts, toggles, tables, columns or lists have no arrow; such blocks simply belong to the section they are in.

en.heading: Toggles
paragraphs: A toggle (/toggle) has a title and content below it that folds in and out.

– Collapse and expand: click (or tap) the arrow in front of the title. By keyboard: ⌘ ⌥ Enter (Windows/Linux: Ctrl Alt Enter) in the content collapses it and puts the cursor in the title, where the same keys expand it again.
– Edit the title: a click in the title puts the cursor there. Enter or ↓ moves into the content (expanding it), ↑ at the start of the content back to the title.

– Nothing gets lost: when the cursor gets into a collapsed toggle (arrow keys, undo) or Find on page goes to a match in it, it expands. Collapse it while the cursor is inside, and the cursor moves in front of the toggle.

– Just for you: as with collapsed sections, collapsing does not change the document – others editing at the same time keep their own state, and the toggle is expanded again the next time you open the page. It is always stored, exported (Markdown ``, HTML) and published expanded; readers collapse it there themselves.
– In reading mode a click on the whole title line collapses and expands it.

en.heading: Pasting answers from ChatGPT
paragraphs: Text copied from ChatGPT or another assistant is formatted when pasted: LaTeX formulas (\[ … \], \( … \), $$ … $$) become formula blocks and inline formulas, Markdown (headings, bold, lists, tables) is applied, lines with tabs become a table, ☐ a task list, and each line becomes its own paragraph. Formulas already rendered on a copied web page stay formulas. This also applies when copying straight from the ChatGPT web page. If formulas are already in the document as text (such as \[ A(3;2;1) \]), select them – or everything with ⌘/Ctrl+A – and choose Turn into formulas in the text menu. Ordinary text is pasted as before.

en.heading: Callouts
paragraphs: Callouts come in five kinds, as on GitHub, Forgejo and Obsidian: Note (blue), Tip (green), Important (purple), Warning (yellow) and Caution (red). Each kind has its icon and a title in the reader's language. With the cursor in a callout, /tip, /warning etc. change its kind; so does the block menu (click the handle ⋮⋮) → Callout type.

en.heading: Your own symbol and colour
paragraphs: So that a callout serves other purposes too – an idea 💡, a date 📅, a key point ★ –, the block menu gives it a symbol and a colour of its own:

– Symbol → Choose emoji or character … opens the emoji picker (the same as for page icons, with search, categories and skin tone). Under Or a character of your own you can also type a character such as ★, → or ✓ – exactly one emoji or symbol character is allowed, no letters, digits, punctuation or spaces. Remove symbol brings back the icon of the kind.
– Colour offers the nine text colours (grey, brown, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, red); Default goes back to the kind's colour. The colours read well in the light and the dark theme.

The kind stays: it gives the title (“Tip”, “Warning” …) and is used for the Markdown export. Symbol and colour are kept when copying, duplicating, in templates, versions, published pages, when printing and in the PDF, EPUB and Word export. Encrypted spaces have no callouts.

en.heading: Callouts in Markdown
paragraphs: Markdown export writes callouts as GitHub alerts (> [!WARNING]). A symbol of its own leads the text, a colour of its own follows as a comment at the end that GitHub does not show:
> [!TIP]
> 💡 The / menu is quicker.
> <!-- flowplan:callout color=green -->

Import (Markdown, ZIP, Notion) turns > [!NOTE] to > [!CAUTION] back into callouts of that kind; Obsidian's further kinds map to the nearest one (e.g. danger → Caution, hint → Tip), and a custom title (> [!WARNING] Read first) becomes a bold first line. A single emoji or symbol followed by a space at the start of the text becomes the callout's symbol; the colour comment restores the colour. Callouts from Notion's Markdown export (💡 …) become callouts with their emoji.

en.heading: Reading mode
paragraphs: The book icon in the top bar (or ⌘ ⌥ E, quick search → > reading) opens a document for reading only: nothing changes by accident, handles and the block menu disappear – handy on the phone and when reading aloud or presenting. The pencil switches back to editing. The device remembers the mode per page; permissions stay the same, and others keep their own mode. Database records have the same book icon at the top of the record (see Databases).

Reading mode also covers everything embedded in the page: in linked databases you can't edit cells, add, delete or move records, or change views; a record opened from there is read-only too. Other people's changes keep showing up live. Synced blocks, drawings, metrics, function graphs and extension blocks are locked in reading mode as well.

en.heading: Focus mode
paragraphs: Focus mode (quick search → > focus) hides the sidebar, toolbar and page margins; the top bar only appears on hover. At the bottom, a bar counts the words of the page and those added in this session. With a goal (e.g. 500 words) a bar shows the progress; the device remembers the goal per page. Esc ends the mode.

en.heading: Present
paragraphs: Present in the … menu at the top right (or ⌘ ⌥ P, quick search → > present) shows a document as full-screen slides – without rebuilding it:
– Each heading 1 starts a new slide. If the document has none, each heading 2 does. A divider (---) always starts a new slide.
– Whatever comes before the first heading becomes a title slide with the page title.
– Images, tables, code, formulas and diagrams are scaled down so the whole slide fits on the screen.
Key Effect
→, ↓, Space, Page Down Next slide
←, ↑, Page Up Previous slide
Home / End First / last slide
Esc End the presentation

A click into the right two thirds of the slide moves on, into the left third back. At the bottom, a counter and a bar show where you are; the bar of buttons fades out while the mouse rests. It also switches between light and dark slides. If “Reduce motion” is set on your system, slides change without a fade.

en.heading: Speaker notes and presenter view
paragraphs: A callout (/callout, kind “Note”) as the last block of a slide holds the speaker notes: it does not appear on the slide. Presenter view (notepad icon in the bar) opens a second window with the current and the next slide, the notes and the elapsed time – handy on the laptop while the projector shows the slides. Both windows stay in step: you can move on in either of them.

en.heading: Slides as PDF
paragraphs: The printer icon in the bar prints the slides – each on its own page in landscape. Choose Save as PDF in the print dialog to pass the slides on.

en.heading: Synced blocks
paragraphs: A synced block (/sync → Synced block) is content that is the same in several places – such as contact details, a checklist or a status notice. Insert synced block shows it on another page. You can edit it everywhere; the change appears on all pages, live on pages that are open.
– An orange frame marks the block; at the top it shows the number of pages and the page it was created on.
– The trash icon in the frame removes the block only in this place; it stays in the others.
– Permissions come from the page the block was created on: whoever may not read that page sees a notice instead of the content.
– The search finds the text on the original page. The block does not appear on published pages.

en.heading: Tasks with assignee and date
paragraphs: A task (/todo or [] + space) with a mention such as @Anna is assigned to Anna: she gets a notification and finds the task under My tasks in the sidebar. You set a date while the cursor is in the task, with the calendar button in the toolbar or through the text menu (select text or right-click → Due date). The date appears as a chip at the right of the line (highlighted today, red when overdue); a click on it changes the date or removes it with Remove date. A new task made with Enter starts without a date.

My tasks collects all tasks given to you, your own tasks with a date and all tasks from your journals (even without @name and without a date) – grouped into Overdue, Today, Next 7 days, Later and No date. Below, From other workspaces lists your tasks from your other workspaces, per workspace; clicking the page switches there. Ticking off and changing the date take effect right in the document, also for others who have it open. On the due date a reminder arrives in the morning; the number next to "My tasks" shows how many are due today or overdue.

en.heading: Markdown shortcuts
paragraphs: While you type, the editor converts:
Type Result
#, ##, ### + space Heading 1–3
- or * + space Bulleted list
1. + space Numbered list
[] + space Task
> + space Quote
` Code block
--- Divider
bold, italic, ` code , ~~strike~~` Formatting in the text

Code blocks carry their language in the fence: `python , `typescript , `terraform . The export writes the ids of VS Code/Shiki; the import also understands aliases and older names (js, ts, py, sh, yml, cpp, csharp, plaintext …) and stores them with the full id ( `js becomes JavaScript, exported again as `javascript ). Unknown languages are kept and show as "(imported)" in the block, without highlighting.

Line numbers, highlighted lines, the view and collapsing follow the language in the fence, in the usual notation: `ts {3-5} showLineNumbers startLine=10 , plus view=preview/view=split/view=code, collapsed and collapsedLines=15. The import also understands showLineNumbers{10} (rehype-pretty-code), showLineNumbers=10 and hl_lines="3 4"/linenums="10" (MkDocs). The numbers in {…} count from the block's first line, whatever its start number. `mermaid fences become code blocks that show the diagram.

en.heading: Format text
paragraphs: Selecting text – or right-clicking it – opens the text menu: reactions for the paragraph, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, highlight, code, link, Comment and Copy, in tasks also Due date. The toolbar above the text adds headings, colour and background colour, superscript and subscript, inline formulas and Hide (spoiler).
– Formatting only applies to the current line. After Enter the new line starts as normal text – only lists and tasks continue with a new item, and a heading is followed by a paragraph.

– Turn into: in the text menu (also on right-click in a line) a line changes its type without losing its text – text, heading 1–3, bulleted list, numbered list, task, quote or code block. The current type is highlighted.

en.heading: Spoiler
paragraphs: Hidden text stays hidden while you write. A click on the area reveals it, another one hides it again. ⌘ ⌥ H hides the selection. Sticky notes and text on whiteboards can be hidden too.

en.heading: Indent
paragraphs: – Tab at the start of a paragraph or heading indents it (up to eight levels), ⇧ Tab outdents it.
– Backspace at the start of an indented line first removes one level.
– In lists Tab nests the item below the previous one; in code blocks it inserts two spaces.

en.heading: Move blocks
paragraphs: A handle (⋮⋮) appears to the left of a block – to keep the page calm, only where you are: at the block under the mouse pointer and at the block with the cursor. You can still reach the handles by keyboard (Tab outside the text); a handle with keyboard focus always shows, with a ring. On touch devices only the block with the cursor has a handle, large enough to tap – so tap into the block first. Empty paragraphs have no handle unless the cursor is in them. To see every handle as before, turn on Settings → Appearance & language → Editor → Always show block handles (on this device). Reading mode and locked pages have no handles.
Dragging shows an insertion line in the middle of the gap between two blocks – also into callouts, quotes or columns; when you let go, the block glides to its new place.
A click on the handle opens the block menu (from the bottom on phones):
– Move up / Move down – past the neighbour
– Move below … – right below a heading of the page, to the top or to the end
– Duplicate and Delete
– Turn into … – text, heading 1–3, bulleted list, numbered list, task list, quote, callout or code; list items switch the kind of list, quotes and callouts can be dissolved
– Callout type, Symbol and Colour (callouts), Width (videos and embeds) and Text direction where they fit
– Select several – the selection mode

In the selection mode circles take the place of the handles. A tap selects a block, another one extends the selection up to it; when all items of a list are chosen, the whole list is. The bar at the bottom moves, duplicates, moves below a heading or deletes the selection, ⋯ holds the rest of the block menu. Done or Esc ends the mode.

List items and tasks stay what they are when moved: outside their list they form a list of the same kind of their own, and a numbered item keeps its number. Right next to a matching list they become part of it; in another kind of list they adapt.
⌘ ⇧ ↑/↓ moves the current block past its neighbour. Every block action can be undone on its own.

en.heading: Images, files and embeds
paragraphs: – Pasting from the clipboard (⌘ V) or dragging in uploads images and files. Images can be resized at their edges.

– Photos are scaled down before uploading: at most 2560 px on the longer side, stored as WebP. The camera rotation is kept, metadata such as the location is removed. GIFs, SVGs and files that would hardly get smaller stay unchanged. Attachments in file properties and forms are stored as they are.

– PDFs appear as a card with a preview of the first page. A click opens the PDF viewer with all pages, zoom (also ⌘ +/−) and Download; Esc closes it. The same applies to PDFs in the media library, in files properties of databases and on published pages. In editable text, ⌘-click a link to a PDF to open the viewer. In the viewer you can write on the PDF – see Annotate PDFs.

– Mark up images: double-click an image (or the pen in the toolbar while the image is selected) to open it for editing – with pen, highlighter, arrow, rectangle, circle and text, seven colours and three line widths, undo with ⌘ Z. Save creates a new image with the markings; the original and the markings stay with the image, so you can change or remove them later.
– Media in the sidebar collects all uploads of the workspace for reuse.

en.heading: Deleting media
paragraphs: In Media, select files with their checkbox and put them in the trash with Move to trash (or the trash icon on the file). There is no confirmation because it can be undone. Anyone who may edit the file's page may delete it; viewers and guests can't.

– Not used: files that no page, record, whiteboard or comment of the workspace contains any more carry this badge. The Not used filter shows only them, and Delete all unused moves them to the trash together after a confirmation. Older versions in the version history don't count as a use and may still show such files.
– Removing an image from a document doesn't delete the file – it then just counts as not used.

– While a file is in the trash it can't be opened anywhere, including through shares and publications. Pages that still show it have a File missing placeholder in its place. Restoring brings it back unchanged.

– It is deleted for good – including in the uploads folder and in object storage such as S3 – only when the trash is emptied, with Delete permanently, or when the retention period ends, see Trash. Until then it counts towards storage.
– Embed (/embed) takes an address: YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Spotify, Figma and CodePen appear as players with an adjustable width, other sites as a link card with title and preview image.
– Links to pages and mentions of people show a preview on hover.
– The administrators set the maximum file size (10 MB by default).

en.heading: Annotate PDFs
paragraphs: If you may edit the page a PDF belongs to, the PDF viewer shows Annotate (not in encrypted spaces and on locked pages). A toolbar appears below it: Pen (with the Apple Pencil or another tablet pen, the line width follows the pressure), Highlighter (translucent, stays under the text and the ink), Eraser (Whole strokes or Partial – then only what is under the eraser goes), Lasso, Text and Laser pointer (points at something without staying). Plus colours, three widths, undo and redo (⌘ Z, ⇧ ⌘ Z).
– Favourite pens: the three pens next to the tools remember colour and width; change them while one is chosen and the favourite changes with it. They apply on this device.

– Shapes: hold the pen still for a moment at the end of a stroke – a drawn line becomes straight, a rectangle, circle, triangle or diamond becomes the clean shape. Switch this off in the Pen settings (gear).
– Lasso: draw around strokes and text to move them, resize them with the handle at the bottom right, recolour, copy (⌘ C, paste with ⌘ V – also on another page), duplicate or delete them.
– Text is placed with a tap on the page; a tap on existing text changes it. On the iPad, Scribble writes into it with the pen.

– Draw with the pen only: once you have written with the pen on a device, only the pen writes – fingers scroll and zoom, a resting hand leaves no marks. PDFs, whiteboards and images share the setting; switch it off in the Pen settings, then a finger writes too, and two fingers scroll and zoom.

– Apple Pencil: the eraser end of a pen erases. In the iPad app, double-tap or squeeze switches to the eraser and back – as set in the iPad settings, or in the Pen settings always to the eraser, the last tool or nothing.

The annotations belong to the page of the PDF, not to the screen: they stay in place at any zoom and apply to everyone who opens the PDF – readers see them but cannot change them. The PDF itself stays unchanged. Done (or ⌘ S) saves; every save is a version you can load again from the clock icon. If someone else saved the annotations in the meantime, your version wins and a notice says who; theirs is kept as a version. Search finds text you write on a PDF – in the app for iPhone and iPad also the handwriting itself, and Convert to text turns selected handwriting into typed text (see Recognising handwriting).
To turn a PDF into a notebook you write in page by page and add sheets to, open it as a notebook: every PDF page becomes a sheet.

Download still downloads the original. Download with annotations (next to it once there are annotations) creates a new PDF with the same pages and the annotations on top as vector graphics – they stay sharp when zooming in. Protected (encrypted) PDFs can only be downloaded without annotations; text appears in Helvetica, characters outside the Western European character set as “?”.

en.heading: Captions
paragraphs: Images, tables and code blocks can have a short caption – one line that says what the block shows. It appears small and muted below the block.
– Add: point at the block or put the cursor in it (tapping an image is enough), and Add caption appears below it. Or use the block menu (handle ⋮⋮) → Add caption.

– Typing: a caption is plain text on one line (up to 500 characters). Enter or ↓ continue below the block, Esc or ↑ go back into it. Others see the caption right away when editing together; ⌘ Z in the document undoes changes.
– Remove: delete the text and leave the field (or press ⌫ in the empty field), or block menu → Remove caption.
– Images: the caption does not replace the alt text for screen readers. When an image has a caption, the block menu offers Use caption as alt text.

– Captions are kept when copying and pasting, moving, duplicating, in templates, versions, on published pages, when printing and in every export, and search finds them. From HTML (for example pasted web pages or Notion's HTML export), ` with and tables with ` become captions.

en.heading: Numbering captions
paragraphs: Page actions (…) → Number captions puts a number in front of the captions of a page: "Figure 1", "Table 1", "Listing 1" (for code). Each kind is counted separately in document order, and only blocks that have a caption count. The label follows the language Flowplan is shown in (English: Figure/Table/Listing, German: Abbildung/Tabelle/Listing, French: Figure/Tableau/Listing). The switch applies to the whole page and everyone who reads it – also on published pages, when printing and in the exports. Copies of the page keep it. Record documents in databases don't have it.

en.heading: Formulas, diagrams and code
paragraphs: – Formulas in LaTeX: as a block with /math, inside the text with /inlinemath. The preview appears while you type. Building blocks such as fraction, root, superscript, subscript, vector, cross product, ±, π and sum sit above the input.
– Mermaid diagrams: a click or Enter opens the source and preview. Up to 20,000 characters and 500 edges.

– draw.io diagrams (/drawio): open the draw.io editor in a large window; Save applies the diagram as one step you can undo. A double-click, Enter or the pencil on the block opens it again. Flowplan stores the drawing and a picture of it: when viewing – on shared pages, in presentations and offline too – it doesn't load draw.io at all and only shows the picture (cleaned, without scripts and without content from elsewhere). Drawing and picture may each be up to 800 kB.

– Maximize: the arrows button at the top right of the window (next to the close button) enlarges draw.io to the whole browser window; the same button (Restore size) brings the window back. It works from the keyboard too. The diagram stays open and unsaved changes are not lost; Esc and Close ask before discarding changes as before. The device remembers the choice: the next diagram opens the way you left the last one. On a phone draw.io fills the screen anyway (keeping clear of the notch and the home indicator), so there is no button there.

– A page for one diagram: the Diagram page template (under Templates, category Knowledge & documentation) creates a full-width page with one empty draw.io diagram and opens draw.io right away. On a full-width page the saved picture uses the whole width, and an empty diagram is a large area rather than a thin strip. There is no separate page type for this as there is for whiteboards – the diagram page is a document, so you can add text, more diagrams or other blocks.

– Where draw.io runs: by default Flowplan uses embed.diagrams.net. While you draw, the diagram's content goes to that service; the window says so. With DRAWIO_URL the instance points to its own draw.io (for example the jgraph/drawio container), and everything stays with you (see Configuration).
– Look: under Settings → Appearance → Editor: draw.io theme Automatic (follows Flowplan), Light or Dark, and draw.io interface Default, Minimal or Sketch. The choice applies to this device.

– Export: in the ZIP export every diagram becomes a .drawio.svg file that draw.io can open again; in a single Markdown file and in the Git export it is a `drawio block with the drawing, which the import turns back into a diagram (the picture is made the next time it is saved). PDF and EPUB show the picture.

– Code blocks: the language is shown in the block's header with its full name ("JavaScript", "C++", "Angular TypeScript", "Plain text"). A click opens a list with a search – it finds names, aliases and file extensions (ts, py, yml, tf, .rs …). The languages you chose last come first (remembered in this browser). There are more than 240 languages with the same grammars as in VS Code – among them Svelte, Vue, Astro, JSX/TSX, Terraform, TOML, Typst, Zig, Prisma, GDScript, Nushell, systemd units, SSH config, Git commit messages, log files, CSV/TSV and .env files. Line wrap and Copy are at hand. Tab indents by two spaces.

– Language detection: when you paste code into a block without a language (plain text), Flowplan suggests a language if it is clearly recognisable – "Looks like Python – set?". One click sets it, the × dismisses the suggestion. Flowplan never changes the language by itself.

– Preview: code blocks in HTML, SVG (language XML with ``), Markdown, Mermaid, LaTeX and Typst show the switch Code / Preview / Split in their header. Split puts code and preview side by side, on a phone one below the other. The view is stored in the block; people who only read a page (read access, published pages, presentations) see the preview unless the block says otherwise, and can switch for themselves without changing anything. Errors (such as a typo in the diagram or in Typst, with the line number) show in place of the preview.
– HTML runs in a sealed frame: no scripts, no forms, no access to Flowplan or the network. Pictures from the web stay blank; embedded pictures (data:) and styles work. The height follows the content.
– SVG, Mermaid and Typst show as a picture – without scripts or links.
– Markdown is converted as on import, LaTeX shows formulas with KaTeX (separated by blank lines, with or without $$ … $$; not whole LaTeX documents with \documentclass).
– Typst loads the first time it is used (a few MB, from your own server, not from the web); Typst packages (@preview/…) and files are not available.
– New Mermaid code blocks ( `mermaid or the language Mermaid chosen) show the diagram right away, empty ones code and diagram side by side. The separate Mermaid block (/mermaid) stays.

– Line numbers: the … menu in a code block's header turns Line numbers on or off for that block, sets the First line number (say 10 for an excerpt) and highlights lines – e.g. 3-5, 8, counted as shown. The numbers cannot be selected and are not copied; with line wrap they stand at the first row of a wrapped line. Blocks without a setting of their own follow Settings → Appearance & language → Editor → Show line numbers by default (on this device).

– Collapse: code blocks with more than 25 lines appear collapsed – 10 lines high, scrolling inside, faded at the bottom. Show all N lines expands them, Collapse folds them again (both reachable by keyboard). People who may edit store the state in the block; readers only expand for themselves. The … menu sets Collapsed and the Collapsed height (5, 10, 15, 20 or 30 lines). Printing and every export always show the whole code.

– A language's highlighting loads with the first code block of that language; until then the code shows briefly without colours. Very long code blocks (more than 50,000 characters) stay without highlighting.
– Fractions: /Fraction (or /Bruch) inserts a formula inside the sentence.

en.heading: Calculating in text
paragraphs: Flowplan only calculates when you want it to – exactly, with fractions, in German or English notation (2,5 or 2.5, ×, ², √, €):
– Hint after "=": type a calculation followed by =, such as 12 × 2,400 € = or 3/4 + 1/6 =, and the result appears greyed out behind it. Tab accepts it, Esc or typing on dismisses it.
– Selected text: select a calculation, a term or an equation; the text menu (also on right-click) shows what is possible under Calculate and inserts the result after it with one click:
– Result and Reduce as an exact fraction, plus As a decimal – 12/18 = 2/3
– Expand, including the binomial formulas – (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

– Factor – x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3), 4x² − 12x + 9 = (2x − 3)², 6x² + 9x = 3x(2x + 3), also with several variables: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²), x² + 2xy + y² − 1 = (x + y − 1)(x + y + 1), by grouping ax + ay + bx + by = (x + y)(a + b); Factor with roots splits further into real factors: x² − 2 = (x − √2)(x + √2)
– Simplify algebraic fractions – (x² − 1)/(x − 1) = x + 1, 1/x + 1/(x + 1) = (2x + 1)/(x(x + 1))

– Solve for x – linear and quadratic equations exactly (x² + 2x − 4 = 0 ⇒ x = −1 ± √5), higher degrees exactly where possible (x³ = 2 ⇒ x = ∛2, x⁴ − 5x² + 6 = 0 ⇒ x = ±√2, ±√3), otherwise as rounded decimals (x³ + x − 1 = 0 ⇒ x ≈ 0.682328); with several variables, for each one that appears linearly. Equations with x in a denominator are solved with the common denominator; values that would make a denominator 0 are excluded and named (x/(x − 1) = 1/(x − 1) ⇒ no solution (x = 1 excluded)).

– Function graph: select a term in x, such as x² − 2 or f(x) = 2x + 1, and choose Draw graph in the text menu – a graph with axes, grid and marked zeros appears below. /Function graph inserts one too. The functions are edited below the graph: it changes while you type, + Function adds up to six functions in their own colours (sin(x), cos, tan, exp, ln, abs, √ and π work). Dragging moves the view, +/− or ⌘/Ctrl + scrolling zoom, ⟲ resets the view. On published pages the graph can be moved and zoomed but not changed.

– Vectors: write vectors as (1 2 3), (1; 2; 3) or (1, 2, 3). Flowplan calculates sums and multiples (2 · (1; −2) − (3; 1) = (−1; −5)), the dot product with · including the angle ((1, 0) · (0, 1) = 0 ⇒ ∠ = 90°), the cross product with × ((1 0 0) × (0 1 0) = (0 0 1)) and the magnitude with … ( (1, 1) = √2). A vector selected on its own shows its magnitude and unit vector ((3, 4) ⇒ v⁰ = (3/5, 4/5)). Draw vectors in the text menu shows vectors in the plane as arrows in a coordinate system – for (1, 2) + (3, 1) both vectors and their sum. More vectors such as (3, 2) can be entered in the graph next to functions. Vectors in space such as (1, 2, 3) – cross products too – are drawn in a 3D coordinate system with x, y and z axes, a floor grid and dashed guides to the floor; dragging turns the view, and the view is saved with the page. The formula editor has the building blocks Vector (column vector), Vector arrow and Cross product; column vectors in formulas are calculated the same way.
– In formulas: the formula editor shows the same options under Calculate and appends the result in LaTeX, such as \frac{3}{4} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{11}{12}.

en.heading: Dashboards and metrics
paragraphs: /Metric inserts a card with a number from a database, /Dashboard three side by side. With the gear you choose:
– the database (every database in the workspace you can read),
– optionally a view – then only the records its filters show count, such as “Open tickets”,
– the calculation: number of records, sum, average, minimum or maximum of a number, formula or rollup property,
– a label.

The server calculates the number for the person looking at the page and refreshes it every minute; private records only count for people allowed to see them. On published pages, visitors without access see a dash. Add charts by inserting a linked database below the metrics and choosing a chart view there – that makes a dashboard from several databases.

en.heading: Page links and mentions
paragraphs: @ searches pages, database records and people – keep typing to narrow the list. The arrow keys move through the hits, Enter inserts the highlighted one. @ opens the list at the start of a line, after a space or after an opening bracket or quote; inside a word – such as an e-mail address like ada@example.org – @ is simply typed. Esc (or Enter without a hit) closes the list and types the @ and what you searched for into the text. Journal days come after the other pages. @today, @yesterday (also @heute, @gestern) or a date such as @2026-10-27 offer a link to that day of the journal under Journal. Records appear with their database, such as "Heating – maintenance · Notes"; only records you may read are offered. Mentioning a person notifies them in the inbox.

Links to pages and records stay valid even if they are renamed or moved. A link that shows the old title gets the new one on a rename – in all documents and records you may edit; a link with its own text keeps it. The target lists all links to it under Linked from – including records whose text contains the link. Records and pages you may not read do not appear there.

A link to a page or record shows the target's icon in front of its text: its emoji, symbol or own picture – without one, the sign of its kind (document, database, whiteboard, record). When someone changes the icon, every link follows, just as the title does on a rename. This also applies in reading mode, comments, published pages, the hover preview, the @ list, Linked from, Related pages and search. A link to a block keeps its paragraph mark unless the page has its own icon. For pages and records you may not read, the link shows only the general link sign. Printing includes the icons; Markdown exports contain only the link text.

en.heading: Links to blocks
paragraphs: Every block can be linked: a paragraph, a heading, a list item, a table, an image, a diagram … The link is the page's address with the block, such as https://flowplan.example.org/#page=…&block=k3x9a2b1 (records add &row=…), and works anywhere in the same workspace.
Copying a link
– in the block menu (the ⠿ handle left of the block, tap it on a phone): Copy link to block,
– for headings via the link symbol that appears after the heading on hover,
– in the table of contents via the link symbol next to each heading (always visible on phones),
– with ⌘ ⇧ L (Windows/Linux: Ctrl Shift L) for the block the cursor is in.
The address is copied; pasted into other apps (mail, chat, Word) it shows as a link with the text "Page › start of the block".
Pasting a link

Paste a copied block link into a document or record of the same workspace (⌘ V): it becomes a link styled like a page link, with the text "Page › start of the block". If text is selected, that text becomes the link. @ also finds headings and blocks of other pages: @Project › Goals (or @Project#Goals) shows the headings of the page "Project" that contain "Goals"; a single search word also finds paragraphs with that text. Headings of the current page are listed as "This page › …".
When the linked page (or record) is renamed, the page title in the link text changes along; the part after "›" stays as it is. On hover, the preview shows the block's current text.
Opening a link

A click opens the page (for a record, the record in its dialog), scrolls to the block and briefly highlights it. A block in a collapsed section is expanded. If the block no longer exists, the page opens with the notice "This block no longer exists – the page is open."
Good to know

– A block keeps its link when it is edited, moved (also cut and pasted) or turned into another kind. Copies – Duplicate or copy and paste within the same document – get a link of their own. When Enter splits a block, the link stays with the first part.
– Preview and link text only show what you may read: for a page you cannot read, only "Linked block" appears, without text.
– In encrypted spaces block links work within the space as well; the server does not know the text there, so there is no text preview.
– People who may only read a page can copy links to its blocks, too.
– Align left no longer has a keyboard shortcut (⌘ ⇧ L now copies the block link); left is the default alignment and stays in the toolbar.

en.heading: Footnotes
paragraphs: /footnote, ⌘ ⌥ F (Ctrl Alt F) or Footnote in the text menu inserts a footnote at the cursor and opens its text.
– The notes appear numbered under Footnotes at the end of the page. Numbers follow the order in the text and update by themselves when you move, copy or delete markers.
– Clicking a number jumps to its note, ↩ jumps back. Double-click the number (or press ⌘ ⌥ F with a footnote selected) to edit or remove it.
– Notes are plain text; web addresses in them become links.
– Footnotes also show on shared and published pages, in print and in the HTML export, and search finds their text.
– In the Markdown export they become [^1] with [^1]: text at the end; the import reads them back – including Obsidian's short form ^[text].

en.heading: Citations and bibliography
paragraphs: For papers, theses and research notes you cite sources right in the text:
– /cite (or /zitat) opens the workspace's bibliography.
– Search a title, paste a DOI (e.g. 10.1000/xyz123 – Flowplan fetches authors, title and year from Crossref and other DOI services) or bring in a whole list via Import BibTeX or CSL-JSON (Zotero) ….
– Optionally add a page and insert.

The text then reads "(Müller 2021)", "(Müller & Schmidt 2021, p. 12)" or "(Müller et al. 2021)"; hovering shows the full reference. /bibliography inserts a bibliography: all works cited on the page in an APA-like style, updating itself as you cite – also on shared and published pages.
– The bibliography belongs to the workspace; guests don't see it. Each citation carries its details along, so copies, exports and shared pages are complete without the list.
– Zotero: export a collection from Zotero as BibTeX or CSL JSON and import it in the dialog.
– In the Markdown export citations become Pandoc citations ([@key], [@key, p. 12]) and the bibliography a section of its own – so a text can be processed further with Pandoc.

en.heading: Show authors
paragraphs: Show authors (in the toolbar or the page menu …) colours the text by the person who wrote it – each person always in the same colour. A legend shows names and shares; Hide authors turns the colouring off again.
– The content itself doesn't change; the colouring is just a view.
– Recording starts with this feature: older, imported or restored text appears as "earlier", and so does text written by guests through links with their own permissions.
– Images, mentions and other embedded objects are not coloured.
– Only people who may read the page see names.

en.heading: Edit as Markdown
paragraphs: Page menu … → Edit as Markdown shows the whole page as Markdown text with line numbers – handy for big rearrangements, find and replace, or if you prefer writing Markdown.
– Apply (⌘ Enter) saves a version first and replaces the content in one step; Undo takes the change back.

– Blocks without a Markdown form – embeds, whiteboards, linked databases, synced blocks, columns, tables with merged cells or widths, sized images, function graphs, metrics and bibliographies – appear as a marker ``. You can move or delete them but not change them; they come back unchanged. If one is deleted, Flowplan asks before applying.
– Formatting without a Markdown form (colours, superscript, spoilers, mentions, citations) is kept as HTML in the text.
– Alignment, indent, text direction and reactions are lost when applying; the view says beforehand what is affected.
– If someone changes the page while you write in Markdown, a notice appears; Apply anyway then overwrites their changes.
– People who may only read – also on locked pages and in reading mode – see View as Markdown without Apply.

en.heading: Text direction
paragraphs: Paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, callouts and table cells in Arabic, Hebrew or Persian run right to left automatically: the direction follows the block's first letter. Bullets, checkboxes, quote bars, callout icons and block handles are then on the right.

In the block menu (click the handle ⋮⋮) → Text direction you set Automatic, Left to right or Right to left for a block and everything inside it. The direction is kept in the HTML export; Markdown has no place for it.

en.heading: More blocks
paragraphs: – Table of contents: lists the headings of the page and jumps there on click.
– Two columns: blocks side by side; stacked on a phone.
– Linked database: a view of an existing database with its own filters and sorting; changes to records go to the source. See Views.
– Whiteboard: a whiteboard right in the document; the button at the top right opens it large.
– Draw (/draw): a block for handwriting across the full width, blank, lined or grid, with a height you drag; several people draw at once without overwriting each other. See Handwriting in documents.

An encrypted space is meant for journals, passwords and other confidential notes. Content, files and – if you choose – titles are encrypted and decrypted in your browser. The server – and with it the operators, backups and the storage provider – only sees ciphertext.

en.heading: What is protected – and what is not
paragraphs: Encrypted
Text of the documents yes
Files and images in the documents yes, including file name and type
Page titles only with Encrypt titles when creating the space
Page structure, icons, times, sizes no
Name of the space and who is a member no

The encryption protects against reading along on the server and in backups. It does not protect against a server that deliberately serves modified program code: a web app runs the code the server sends. If you do not trust the operator of an instance at all, do not edit confidential data on that instance.

en.heading: Set up your keys
paragraphs: With your first encrypted space – or under Settings → Account & security → End-to-end encryption – you set up your keys:
– Choose a passphrase (at least 10 characters, ideally a whole sentence). It is not your sign-in password and never leaves your browser.
– Keep the recovery key safe: 52 characters in groups of four, to Download or Print. Setup only completes once you confirm you have stored it safely.
Important: whoever loses the passphrase and the recovery key loses access to their encrypted data. Neither the administrators nor the operator can restore it – the server never saw the keys.

Under Settings → Account & security → End-to-end encryption you can change the passphrase and create a new recovery key (the old one stops working). Only if both are lost: Reset keys … at the very bottom, in the Danger zone. Afterwards a member has to give you access to each encrypted space again.

en.heading: Unlock and automatic locking
paragraphs: Encrypted pages first show Unlock. With the passphrase (or the recovery key plus a new passphrase) you decrypt your keys – only in this browser tab and only in memory. Reloading, Lock now or a period without activity (15 minutes by default, adjustable to 5, 15, 30 or 60) locks again. No readable copy stays on the device; that is why encrypted pages cannot be edited offline.

en.heading: Create a space
paragraphs: Add space → name → tick Encrypted space, optionally Encrypt titles → Create space. An encrypted space is always private. In the sidebar it carries a green lock.
Encrypted spaces hold documents only. Databases, whiteboards, dashboards and journals are not possible here (yet) – write a journal as documents, e.g. one page per month.

en.heading: Members
paragraphs: The lock next to the space name (or Members on a page) opens Members and keys:

– Add: owners of the space or of the workspace give a member the key (Give key). This works only while unlocked, and only for people who have already set up their own keys. New members also read all older content.

– Remove or Leave space: the space gets a new key right away; the removed person cannot read new content. What they could decrypt before, they may have kept – old content is not re-encrypted. Whoever is removed from the workspace loses the keys as well.

en.heading: What does not work in encrypted spaces
paragraphs: Everything that would need the server to read the content is switched off here and refused by the server:
– Search, AI, previews, "Related pages" and unlinked mentions
– Comments and text comments, mentions with notifications
– Share links, sharing single pages and publishing
– Version history, templates, duplicating, moving to other spaces (in or out)
– Tags and page properties
– Export as PDF, DOCX, EPUB, server-side Markdown, Git export
– Webhooks only receive the page ID, MCP clients only metadata

en.heading: Export and backup
paragraphs: The editor offers two ways:
– Markdown (decrypted): the browser turns the page into Markdown and saves the file – the plaintext does not pass through the server.
– Encrypted archive: all pages of the space as ciphertext, plus your encrypted space keys and your key secured with passphrase and recovery key. Without passphrase or recovery key it is unreadable.
Regular instance backups also contain encrypted spaces only as ciphertext.

en.heading: Technical details
paragraphs: X25519 key pairs, AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations for the passphrase, all through the browser's WebCrypto interface (current versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari). The full design with the threat model is in docs/e2ee-design.md.
From signing in for the first time to your first own page: what you do with Flowplan in the first ten minutes.

en.heading: Sign in or sign up
paragraphs: You sign in with your e-mail and password, with a passkey (fingerprint, face or device PIN) or – if your organisation has set it up – with Sign in with SSO through your organisation's login (OpenID Connect, such as Keycloak, Authentik, Zitadel or Entra ID). You create an account with Create account, provided the instance allows sign-ups or you have been invited. Afterwards you set up passkeys under Settings → Account & security. Everything else is described under Sign-in.
On a brand-new instance you create the first account – it administers the instance. If you are moving or reinstalling, choose Restore from a backup there instead (Restore while setting up).

When you sign in for the first time, Flowplan creates a private workspace with example pages. With single sign-on, your name, e-mail address and – if available – your profile picture come from the login provider.

[!TIP] If the instance offers a demo, you can try Flowplan without an account. The demo gets its own example workspace and is deleted completely when you end it, sign out or after 45 minutes without activity.

Language: Flowplan follows your browser's language. Under Settings → Appearance & language → Language you pick German 🇩🇪, English 🇬🇧, English (US) 🇺🇸, French 🇫🇷 or Chinese 🇨🇳 from the list – it then applies on all devices, also to e-mails and push notifications. Further languages can be added: Languages and translations.

en.heading: The introduction
paragraphs: After creating an account, Flowplan walks you through the essentials once. Every step can be skipped, and everything can be changed later in the settings:
– Welcome: language and appearance (automatic, light or dark).
– What would you like to start with? Set the workspace's name (as its owner) and, if you like, create pages right away: a Tasks database, a Notes database, a Journal or a Whiteboard.
– What Flowplan does: a short tour of pages and blocks, databases, whiteboards, the journal, collaboration, sharing, search and offline – each with a tip and a link into this documentation.
– Notifications: e-mail summaries (when the instance sends e-mail) and push on this device.
– All set: the created pages to open and the most important shortcuts.

Later, Settings → Appearance & language → Start introduction (or "introduction" in the search with ⌘/Ctrl + K) opens it again. Accounts that existed before the introduction was added do not see it automatically.

The settings open with an overview: one tile per section, grouped into Personal, Connections, Workspace and Help & info. The search at the top (“Search settings …”) helps – “passkeys” finds Account & security, for example –, and every section has its own link, e.g. /#settings/notifications.

en.heading: The interface
paragraphs: – Sidebar on the left: workspace switcher, search, home, inbox, your spaces with the page tree, and below them templates, media, trash and settings.
– Home: recently edited pages, quick starts for a new idea or project, and all pages of your workspace – customizable with widgets (see Customize your home page).
– Header of a page: path, share, comments, favourite and the Page actions menu (…).

On a computer, drag the sidebar's right edge to make it wider or narrower (200 to 480 pixels); a double click on the edge restores the original width. Flowplan remembers the width per device. On a phone the sidebar folds away: the icon at the top left opens it, and so does a swipe to the right that starts just inside the left edge of the screen (or Navigation in the bar at the bottom). On the iPhone the very edge stays the back gesture. Swipe it to the left or tap beside it to close it. For iPhone and iPad there is also an app on the App Store, for Android an app to download (Apps for iPhone, iPad and Android).

en.heading: Back and forward
paragraphs: At the top left, next to the sidebar icon, the arrows ← and → take you to the page opened before and forward again. Every place with an address of its own is a step: pages, databases, journal days, whiteboards, a record opened from a database, home, inbox, My tasks, tags, collections, media, trash and the sections of the settings. Dialogs, menus and the search do not count, and closing a record you opened in its database takes you back there without an extra step. When there is nothing in one direction, its arrow is greyed out.
– List: a right click or a long press on an arrow shows the last (up to ten) pages in that direction with their icon and title – a click jumps straight there.

– Keyboard shortcuts: ⌘ [ and ⌘ ] or ⌥ ← and ⌥ → (Windows and Linux: Alt ← / Alt → or Ctrl [ / Ctrl ]). While typing, ⌥/Alt with an arrow moves the cursor as usual; the shortcuts can be changed like all others (Keyboard shortcuts).
– Browser: the arrows take the same steps as the browser's back and forward buttons and the mouse's side buttons – you can mix them.
– Desktop app: also the Navigation menu → Back / Forward, the mouse's side buttons and, on a Mac, swiping on the trackpad (More from the desktop app).
– Phone: there are no arrows there – the back gesture (iPhone) or the back button (Android) goes back.

Short animations show what just moved: cards and rows glide into their new place, bars that move along in the timeline visibly follow, and the target of a jump – from the table of contents, search or a notification – lights up briefly. Moving to another page briefly cross-fades the content area; when you open a page in the page tree, its icon and title fly to their place, and a card from a board or gallery grows into its record (on a phone the record comes up as a sheet). A tap or a key ends such a transition at once, and clicking quickly from one page to the next goes without one. While uploaded images load, they show a blurred preview in their final size and then fade in – nothing below them moves. The animations follow the system setting Reduce motion: when it is on, everything moves to its target without motion, and jump targets are only highlighted briefly and still.

en.heading: Customize your home page
paragraphs: The home page is yours: Customize at the top right (or “Customize home page” in quick search) lets you arrange it from widgets the way you work. On phones everything sits in one column, on tablets in two, on large screens in three or four – the iPhone, iPad and Android apps and the desktop app show the same home page.
While customizing:

– Widget opens the gallery: greeting, recently edited or viewed, favourites, the workspace's pages, my tasks, inbox, journal today, agenda, database view, pinned page, quick capture, focus & time, habits, counter, scratchpad, activity, my activity, this week, links and – for administrators – the instance status.
– Move: drag the handle, use the up/down arrows, or the keyboard – focus the handle, then the arrow keys, Home and End.
– Size: small (one column), medium (two), large (three) or full width. A widget never gets wider than the space there is.

– Settings (gear): a heading of your own and what the widget shows – for My tasks “Due today and overdue”, “Due today”, “Overdue” or “All open”, from your tasks or the open records of a database view; for the Agenda the period (today, 3 or 7 days) and which calendar and timeline views count (also those connected to Google, Microsoft 365 or CalDAV).
– Appearance: a header with a colour, a gradient or a page's cover image, an emoji as icon, comfortable or compact spacing, a subtle background (dots, grid, tinted) and a normal or wide page.
– Done saves, Cancel discards. In the … menu you save the home page for all your workspaces (otherwise it applies to this one only) or reset it.

My activity shows how many pages you created and edited – per week, month or year (switchable in the widget), with a chart and the comparison with the same stretch of the previous period. An edited page counts at most once per day, and autosaves don't add to it. Only you see these numbers; Flowplan records nothing new for them and no times – it counts from what is stored anyway (creator, versions, activity log).

You tick off tasks right in the widget, habits too; the journal widget adds a few lines to today's entry, and the scratchpad holds whatever fits nowhere else – it saves as you type and is the same on all devices.
Widgets only show what you may see anyway: pages of other workspaces do not appear, journals behind a PIN only show their name, and the home page sees no content of end-to-end encrypted spaces.
[!TIP] Workspace owners can use … → Set as default for members to choose the home page new members (and everyone without their own) see. Personal notes are not passed on.

en.heading: Your first page
paragraphs: – Click + next to a space in the sidebar or choose New page on the home screen.

– Enter a name at the top and choose the kind below it: Document, Database, Whiteboard, Journal, Dashboard, Notebook, Workflow or From a template (the arrow keys work too). A line below describes the chosen kind, a database or notebook shows its options right there, and Space sets where the page is created.
– Create page (on phones the buttons stay above the on-screen keyboard) and start writing. Everything is saved automatically, even without a connection.
In a document, / opens the block menu: type /h2, /todo or /table and press Enter to insert. How the editor works in detail is explained under Documents and the editor.

en.heading: Find instead of search
paragraphs: ⌘ K (Windows/Linux: Ctrl K) opens the quick search across titles, text, database records, comments and even the content of uploaded PDFs and Office files. More under Search, inbox and push.

en.heading: Where to go next
paragraphs: – Pages and spaces: page tree, favourites, moving and trash.
– Databases: tables, boards, calendars and more from the same records.
– Collaboration and comments: write together, comment, mention.

en.heading: Help and community
paragraphs: Questions, ideas or just saying hello: in the Flowplan Discord users and admins help each other. Bugs and feature requests are best filed as GitHub issues, so nothing gets lost.

en.heading: About Flowplan
paragraphs: Settings → Help & info → About Flowplan (/#settings/about, also in the account menu ⋯ at the bottom of the sidebar and with ⌘/Ctrl + K → “About Flowplan”) shows:

– Version: the running version, the commit and the build date; for our Docker images also whether it is a beta (:beta) or a release. Admins also see here when a newer version is known. Best mention the version when reporting a bug.
– Licence & source code: Flowplan is free software under the GNU AGPL-3.0 – with links to the licence text and to the source of the code running on this instance.
– Links: website, documentation, Discord and “Report a bug” (GitHub issues).
– Support Flowplan ♥: a link to GitHub Sponsors. It never appears in the iPhone, iPad and Android apps (app store rules); admins can hide it with FLOWPLAN_HIDE_SPONSOR=true (Configuration).

The search finds the page with “About”, “Version”, “Licence”, “Source”, “Support” or “Sponsor” (and the German words). The sign-in page also names the licence (AGPL-3.0) and the source code at the bottom.
A form view collects answers directly as records in the database – from members or, if enabled, from anyone with the link.

en.heading: Design a form
paragraphs: – Create a view of the type Form in the database.
– Design form opens the editor:
– title, description and the label of the submit button,
– questions: order, hide, required, help text per question,
– question type: short or long text, radio buttons instead of a list, a linear scale 1–10 for numbers,
– Only show if … per question (see Conditions and pages),
– Text block before, Text block at the end and New page from here for explanations and several pages,
– title after submitting and confirmation text,
– what happens after sending (see Settings).
– Save form.
Flowplan checks required fields and input types in the browser and on the server. Files properties allow uploads in the form.

en.heading: Conditions and pages
paragraphs: Every question, text block and page break can Only show if … an earlier answer matches – for example “Kind is Bug”, “Topics includes Billing”, “Subject contains the text invoice”, “Importance is greater than 7” or “E-mail is answered”. A hidden page break hides its whole page.
– Hidden questions are not required, and their answers are not saved – not even when they are sent anyway. The server checks the same rules as the browser.
– A question that depends on a hidden question stays hidden as well.
– With several pages a progress bar shows how far along you are (can be switched off); Back and Next change the page, and required questions are checked per page.

en.heading: Settings
paragraphs: Under After sending, Confirmation by e-mail and Notify the team – in the form editor as well as in a survey's settings:
– Then redirect to: an address with https:// that the thank-you page leads to after a few seconds (0–60, default 3).

– Placeholders: {Name of the question} inserts the answer to that question – in the title and text after submitting, in the redirect (there only after the domain name, e.g. https://example.com/thanks?name={Name}) and in the e-mail. Unknown names stay as they are; people, relations and files are not inserted.

– Confirmation by e-mail to the people answering: subject and text are up to you. The e-mail contains the text and the answered questions as a list – without hidden and internal properties – and, with the customer portal, the link to the request (then only this one e-mail is sent). It goes to the first answered e-mail question; in forms that are not anonymous, otherwise to the signed-in account's address. Anonymous forms only write when the person types their address. E-mail must be set up (Configuration); at most 5 e-mails per hour go to an address, 10 per sender and 300 per form.
– Notify the team: the chosen members get a notification of the kind “Guest comments and guest records” for each new answer – if they may see the record.

en.heading: Continue later
paragraphs: In forms and surveys that are not anonymous, Save and continue later keeps your answers so far as a draft for you (without files). When you open the link again, you continue on the same page; after sending, the draft is gone. Drafts unchanged for half a year are deleted.

en.heading: Share a form
paragraphs: Under Share form, switch the form on and copy the link.
– Members only: answering requires signing in; the answer carries the person's name.

– Anonymous: anyone with the link can answer, without an account and without a name. Files from anonymous answers count against a daily budget: 200 MB per form and FLOWPLAN_ANONYMOUS_UPLOAD_MB for the whole instance (Configuration); each form also accepts at most 1000 answers per hour.
Person and relation questions only exist in forms for members, because they would reveal members and records.
[!NOTE] Copied or imported forms start switched off and for members only. In the demo, forms can be designed but not made public, and confirmation e-mails cannot be switched on.

en.heading: Answers
paragraphs: Every answer is a normal record: it appears in all views and can be filtered, assigned and commented on.

en.heading: Surveys
paragraphs: Turn into a survey makes a form a survey – or create a new page from the Survey template. The builder has five tabs: Questions, Preview, Settings, Share and Results.

On the left is the flow with numbered questions, text blocks and page breaks; on the right you edit the selected item. Add question shows the question types grouped into choice, rating, and text and details. Everything is saved automatically shortly after you stop typing – the dot at the top right shows the state. If something is still missing (a question without text, an empty answer, a redirect without https://), saving waits and says why.

en.heading: Question types
paragraphs: Surveys have {{facts.questionTypes}} question types:
– Text: short answer, long text, e-mail, phone, website, number, date, time
– Choice: single choice, multiple choice, dropdown, yes / no – optionally with “Other” and a text field, a random order and a minimum or maximum number
– Rating: stars (3 to 10), Net Promoter Score (0–10), a scale with labels at both ends, a slider
– Matrix (Likert): several statements with the same answers
– Ranking: put items in order
– File upload
– Also text blocks for explanations and page breaks for several pages.
Pasting several lines into an answer field adds several answers at once.

en.heading: Conditions
paragraphs: Every question, text block and page break can Only show if … an earlier answer matches – with the same comparisons as in forms. Example: “What should we improve?” only appears for a recommendation score up to 6. Hidden questions are not required, and their answers are not saved.

en.heading: Survey settings
paragraphs: – a welcome page, a progress bar for several pages, a thank-you text with placeholders
– redirect, confirmation e-mail and team notification as for forms
– Closes on and At most this many answers – after that the survey takes no more answers
– One answer per person – signed-in people by their account, anonymous ones by their connection
– an accent colour

en.heading: Sharing and results
paragraphs: Share opens the survey. It can be public, so anyone with the link can take part, and anonymous, so without signing in and without names.
Every answer is a record of the database. Each question is a property, a matrix one property per row. So you can filter and sort answers, export them as CSV and process them with automations.
Results shows:
– the answers per day,
– per question the count and share of every answer,
– averages, minimum and maximum,
– the NPS score with promoters, passives and detractors,
– matrix tables, the average places of rankings and the latest text answers.
[!NOTE] Renaming a question keeps its answers. Changing the type so that the stored kind changes (e.g. from text to number) creates a new property – earlier answers stay in the old one.

en.heading: Customer portal
paragraphs: The customer portal turns a form into a service desk: whoever sends it can follow their request afterwards.
– Under Share form, switch on the customer portal.

– Choose which properties are visible in the portal – for example Status or a due date. A select property named “Status” is preselected when you switch it on. People, relations and files always stay internal.

After sending, the person sees a private link to their request. If they answered an e-mail question and e-mail is set up, the link also arrives by e-mail – in their language; with the confirmation e-mail switched on, it is part of that one e-mail. The page shows the status, their answers and a conversation with the team.

The team replies in the record under Customer request. Replies go to the person by e-mail; when they write back, the people on the record, everyone who already replied and whoever created the database get a notification. Copy customer link passes the link on when there is no e-mail address.
[!NOTE] The link is the key: anyone who has it sees the request and can reply. Switching off the customer portal or the form stops all links from working; switching it back on restores them.

en.heading: Processing form answers
paragraphs: The workflow trigger Form answer starts a workflow for every answer – for example with the template Form → AI category → assignment: the AI puts the answer into a category, the person responsible is set and notified.
Content comes in as Markdown, CSV or an archive and goes out again as Markdown, PDF or a complete archive. The version history brings back earlier states.

en.heading: Export
paragraphs: Page actions → Export:
Format Content
Markdown (.md) One file with the page content; databases with an overview, properties and the documents of all records.

Markdown with files (.zip) index.md, sub-pages under pages/, the days of a journal in its folder under 2026/10/2026-10-27.md (see below), record documents under records/, databases also as CSV under tables/, attachments under assets/ – all linked relatively. Every record under records/ starts with its properties as YAML frontmatter (see below). With Include comments and earlier versions, .comments.md and .versions/ come along.
As Word (DOCX) A Word document of the page – see Word, PDF with sub-pages and e-book.
As PDF (with sub-pages) The page with its sub-pages as one document with a cover and a table of contents, which the print dialog saves as PDF.
As e-book (EPUB) The page with its sub-pages as an e-book for e-readers and e-book apps.
HTML / JSON The older format for documents and databases.

Print / PDF opens the browser's print view; save as PDF there. Home screen apps on iPhone and iPad cannot print themselves: they open the page in Safari under a secret address for 15 minutes. This print view shows content only – no form fields, buttons or scripts – and at the top who created it.
The export respects read permissions and contains all records regardless of view filters. Formulas and Mermaid are kept as source.
Captions in Markdown: an image's caption becomes its title, a table's a line Table: … below it (as in Pandoc), a code block's Listing: …:
Item Amount
Server €40
Table: Costs at a glance
``ts const x = 1; ``
Listing: An example

The Markdown import (also ZIP, Git and Edit as Markdown) reads these back as captions, as well as Pandoc's short form : … below a table. The title of an image from other sources (`) becomes its caption. A plain paragraph that happens to start with Table: or Listing: right below a table or code block without a caption is exported as Table\: and so stays a paragraph. When the page numbers its captions, the frontmatter says so (flowplan: captions: numbered`); the numbers themselves are not written into the text, so an import doesn't make them part of the caption.

Whiteboards come along in the ZIP as SVG images under assets/: a whiteboard page shows its image, and a whiteboard embedded in a document becomes the image with a link to the board in Flowplan. The image is cropped like Export as SVG in the board; pictures on the board sit next to it under assets/. Covered items stay covered, comment pins are not included; an empty board gives a short note instead of an image. Since SVG is text, Git shows changes to a board as a readable diff. The board cannot be edited outside Flowplan.

Journal days sort by path in the ZIP, in their journal's folder: 2026/10/2026-10-27.md next to the index.md of an exported journal, for a journal below another page under pages/-/2026/10/…. The heading is the day's title in the export's language ("Tuesday, 27 October 2026"; a renamed day keeps its title), the frontmatter names id and date (flowplan: id, date). This applies to the page and space export, the scheduled export and Git. The ZIP import turns them back into a journal with its days, without folder pages "2026" or "10"; a second file of the same date does not become a second day.

Block links in the Markdown export. Links to blocks become relative links with an anchor in the ZIP, the way Obsidian writes them: Project › Goals. The linked block carries its id as a marker: a paragraph, heading or list item at the end of its line (Our goals for 2027 ^k3x9a2b1), any other block (table, code, quote, list …) on a line of its own right below it (^k3x9a2b1). Only blocks that a link in the workspace points to are marked – the rest of the Markdown stays clean. Obsidian reads both as block references; other Markdown tools show the short marker as text. On import (ZIP, Obsidian vault, Git export with taking over changes, Edit as Markdown) the marker becomes the block's id again and the links point to it again. Outside a ZIP (a single Markdown file, MCP) the link stays the Flowplan address with &block=….

Limits per export: 500 pages, 200,000 records, 250 MB of content (at most 200 MB of it text); the ZIP may be up to 100 MB. The same limits apply to the scheduled Markdown export, which backs up whole databases with their comments and versions.

en.heading: Word, PDF with sub-pages and e-book
paragraphs: Three more formats for handbooks, reports and everything that is read or edited outside Flowplan. All three start from the same cleaned page content as the Markdown export and respect read permissions in the same way: they contain only what you may read – other people's private records, PIN-locked journals and pictures from pages you may not open stay out (a note stands in for such a picture, and a link to an inaccessible page becomes plain text).

As Word (DOCX) – Page actions → Export → As Word (DOCX), for a database also via Export in the toolbar, for a single record via the … menu in the record's header. The file is written by Flowplan itself, without a Word library, and opens in Word, LibreOffice and Pages:
– Headings (as Word heading styles, so the navigation pane works), paragraphs with alignment, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code, highlights, text colour, superscript and subscript, links.
– Bulleted and numbered lists, also nested, tasks with ☐/☑ and their due date.
– Tables with merged cells and a shaded header row.
– Pictures (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) embedded and scaled to the text width; the page's cover image at the top.
– Captions of images, tables and code in Word's "Caption" style below the block; when the page numbers its captions, the numbers are Word fields (SEQ), so a table of figures in Word picks them up.

– Callouts (note, tip, important, warning, caution) as shaded paragraphs, quotes with a side line, code blocks, formulas and Mermaid diagrams in a monospace style, toggles with their title, columns one after another.
– Footnotes as real Word footnotes, citations and the bibliography as text.
– A database becomes a table of all records followed by every record's document; a single record starts with its properties as a table.
– Not included: whiteboards, embedded videos, audio, PDFs, link cards and linked databases (they stay links to Flowplan), function plots and metrics (a note), comments and versions.

As PDF (with sub-pages) – Page actions → Export → As PDF (with sub-pages): the page with all accessible sub-pages (can be turned off) becomes a print view with a cover, a table of contents and every page as a numbered chapter on a new page; links between the pages jump within the document. As with Print / PDF, the browser's print dialog opens – save as PDF there. Home screen apps on iPhone and iPad open the view in Safari as usual. Whiteboards come along as pictures, databases as a table with the records' documents. Page numbers in the table of contents and the footer appear only in renderers that know target-counter (Prince, Paged.js); browsers leave them out. For scripts: GET /api/export/pdf?page=&children=1 returns the HTML of the print view.

As e-book (EPUB) – Page actions → Export → As e-book (EPUB): the page with its sub-pages as EPUB 3 – every page a chapter, the table of contents nested like the page tree, pictures and whiteboards as resources, links between the pages within the book, footnotes at the end of each chapter. Suitable for Apple Books, Kindle (after conversion), Calibre, Thorium and other readers. For scripts: GET /api/export/epub?page=&children=1.
Limits: 200 pages per PDF or EPUB export, 5,000 records, 100 MB of attachments (files over 25 MB are left out). Database tables with more than 200 columns cannot be exported to Word.

en.heading: Export a whole space
paragraphs: The download icon next to a space's name in the sidebar (or Settings → Import & export → Export → One space) opens the space export. Besides the Markdown ZIP it offers Space as PDF (a print view of all pages of the space with a cover and a table of contents, see above) and Space as e-book (EPUB) – each with everything you may read, up to 200 pages (GET /api/export/pdf?space= or /api/export/epub?space=). The Markdown ZIP downloads the whole space as one archive – to archive, read offline or put into your own Git repository:
– Every top-level page is in a folder of its own, -/, with everything below it – the same layout as the scheduled Markdown export. Inside, the format of Markdown with files (.zip) applies.
– index.md at the top lists the space's pages; links between pages of the space are relative, links into other spaces keep pointing to Flowplan.

– Anyone who can read the space may export it, no administrator needed. It contains only what that person may read: other people's private records and PIN-locked journals stay out, and other people's private spaces cannot be exported.
– Include comments and earlier versions works as for the page export; the same limits apply, for the whole space.
– For scripts with a read token: {"spaceId":"…","format":"zip","history":true} to /api/markdown-export (see API tokens). The space's id is shown in the export dialog.
– Regularly into a Git repository, without a script of your own: the Git export of a space, set up by the owner of the space.

en.heading: Print and PDF
