paragraphs: Page actions → Print (or > print in the quick search) prints the page as a clean A4 document – in the print dialog it can also be saved as PDF. The sidebar, toolbars, handles, comment bars and notices disappear; colours are always light, blocks are not split in the middle of a page, long code lines wrap and external links are written out with their address.

en.heading: Import
paragraphs: All imports are under Settings → Import & export → Import; at the top you choose the Target space once for all of them.

– Markdown, text or HTML: Markdown, text or HTML files. Headings, lists, tasks, tables, code and formulas become blocks; Mermaid code ( `mermaid , in HTML ` or ) becomes a code block that shows the diagram – the code is one click away (preview). This applies to every import, including AFFiNE, Notion, Obsidian, Confluence (the language of code macros) and pasted Markdown. Image titles and Table:/Listing: lines become captions, in HTML / and `. The AFFiNE import takes over the captions of images and code blocks.

– Notion, AppFlowy or Markdown export: Notion, AppFlowy or Markdown export (ZIP) accepts a ZIP with Markdown and CSV files. Markdown becomes pages, CSV databases, days of a Flowplan journal (…/2026/10/2026-10-27.md below the journal) days of that journal again, Excalidraw and draw.io files whiteboards, folders sub-pages; linked images and files are uploaded, and Notion record pages are matched to their records. Up to 100 MB, by default 10,000 pages (FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_DOCS) and 5,000 records per table; you choose the target space beforehand.
– Jira or Trello: Jira or Trello – see Projects, tickets and sprints.

– CSV: in a database, choose Import CSV or Markdown and pick a CSV file; the rows become records. A CSV exported from Flowplan comes back as it was: text that looks like a formula (=…, +…, @…) gets a protective apostrophe on export, which the import removes again; tags containing a comma (such as “Night, Weekend”) stay one tag when the column's options include it. The import finds people, related records, files and sprints by their name (people also by e-mail address) and links them again – but only when the name is unique: if two records are called “Meeting”, the cell stays empty rather than linking the wrong one. Columns missing from the file are left out instead of being emptied.
– Markdown with frontmatter into a database (such as notes from Obsidian): in the database, choose Import CSV or Markdown and pick one or more .md files or a ZIP – see below.
– Content archive (see below).

en.heading: Frontmatter: records as Markdown files
paragraphs: Notes from Obsidian, Logseq, Jekyll or Hugo carry their properties as YAML frontmatter at the top of the file:
para: Resource
area: House
tags: [heating, maintenance]
# Heating – maintenance

Import into a database: every file becomes a record. The title comes from title:, otherwise from the first # heading or the file name; the rest of the text becomes the record's document, linked images and files from the ZIP are uploaded, and links between the imported files become links to the new records. Keys are matched to properties of the same name (case does not matter):
– select and multi-select take the values and add unknown ones as new options (so tags: lands in Tags);
– relations find the linked record by its title (also as [[Title]]), people by name or e-mail;
– dates are read as ISO dates, true/false as checkboxes, numbers as numbers;

– aliases: (a list or one text, separated by commas) and alias: together fill the property of type Aliases, whatever its name; if there is none, Create missing properties adds one. A database without an aliases property but with a property named "aliases" gets the values there, as before;
– computed properties (formulas, rollups, timestamps) are not overwritten.

When importing records (Markdown, CSV) into a multi-select with the workspace's tags, the values stay names; missing tags are created if you may create tags (members with edit rights) – otherwise such values are left out.

Before the import, a preview shows which properties match and which are missing. Create missing properties adds them with a fitting type: list → multi-select, ISO date → date, true/false → checkbox, number → number, address → URL, a few recurring values → select, otherwise text. Up to 5,000 files and 100 MB per import.

Export: in the ZIP export, every record under records/ starts with title: and its properties: select as text, multi-select and relations (titles of the linked records) as lists, dates as ISO dates. Aliases are written under Obsidian's key aliases: as a list, so they survive a trip to Obsidian and back. Computed values and the record's id are below flowplan: and are skipped on import. When a record exported this way is imported into the same database again, the preview offers update instead of adding: the record with the same id gets the file's properties and text, and the previous state stays as a version. Without this choice it is added as a new record.

Pages: a page's aliases, tags and properties are written by the Markdown export (single page, space export, scheduled export and Git export) as frontmatter at the top of the file – the way Obsidian reads them:
tags:
- Customer
- Offer
Status: Sent
Budget: 12500
Owner: Emil Example
# Offer Müller Ltd
People appear by name, multi-selects as a list, checkboxes as true/false; the automatic properties (created at …) are left out. Pages without aliases, tags and values keep no frontmatter.

When importing Markdown files, Markdown ZIPs and Obsidian vaults under Settings → Import & export, aliases:/alias: becomes the new page's aliases and tags: (or tag:, as a list or “a, b”) its tags; missing tags are created. Further keys become properties: if the workspace already has a property with that name, the page gets its value there. Unknown keys are created as new properties only by workspace owners – the type follows the value (true → checkbox, number → number, 2026-12-01 → date, list → multi-select, URL, email, otherwise text). Keys of publishing tools (cssclass, publish, permalink, layout, slug, draft …) never become properties. When the whole frontmatter is taken over, it disappears from the text; otherwise it stays in the text as before. The Git export reads aliases, tags and values of changed pages back from the repository.

Where to export: in a database's toolbar, Export opens a menu with CSV (current view), Markdown with files (.zip), Markdown (.md) and As Word (DOCX). A single record is exported from the … menu in its header: Export as Markdown (.md) (with frontmatter), Markdown with files (.zip), As Word (DOCX) (properties as a table, then the document) or Print / PDF.

CSV (current view) writes the view's visible columns in their order (board, gallery and other card views always with the title) and the values as the table shows them: people (also Created by / Edited by) by name, related records by title, uploaded files by name (links stay links), sprints by name. Numbers, dates and checkboxes are written as stored. If a person's name isn't unique, their e-mail address is written instead. The CSV in the Markdown ZIP still holds all properties.

From Obsidian: links in the text are read as standard Markdown links. Convert wikilinks ([[…]], ![[…]]) first – in Obsidian, Settings → Files and links, turn off “Use [[Wikilinks]]” and choose relative paths.

en.heading: Content archive
paragraphs: Under Settings → Import & export → Export → Workspace as ZIP you download a ZIP of your workspace. To bring it back – also into another Flowplan instance – use Backups → Restore a Flowplan archive: the archive is created as a copy in new private spaces.

Backing up the whole instance (with accounts and permissions) is up to the administration: Administration → Storage & backup. The card Trash & retention leads to the trash and says how long things are kept: deleted pages and spaces until someone deletes them permanently, deleted database records 30 days; how long earlier versions stay is set by the administration.

It contains: accessible pages including the trash, databases with views and records, document content, relations, templates, comments, versions, favourites and form options, plus all files with checksums. Also the settings of databases (done rule, workflow, automations, sprints, story points – never the Git token), time entries and the status history behind burndown charts, the settings and trackers of journals with each day's values and place, handwriting on PDFs and your home page (applied only when the person importing has none of their own yet).

The workspace's tags and properties (unused ones too) and every page's tags and values come along as well. Importing creates missing tags, and missing properties only if you own the target workspace; existing ones with the same name are reused.

The archive only holds what you may see yourself: other people's private records with their comments and files are left out, as are journals behind a PIN you have not unlocked right now. Versions of a database are included only for owners, because they contain every record. Each version holds the whole database; when not all of them fit into the archive of a large database, the newest come along and older ones stay behind – the current records are always included.
– Importing creates new IDs; internal links and relations are rewritten – embedded whiteboards, synced blocks, metrics, drawing blocks and records on whiteboard cards too.
– If the archive comes from someone else, their assignments and mentions become yours; tasks in documents show under My tasks right away.
– Older archives import as before; older servers skip what they do not know.
– Imported spaces and templates are private, shares and forms are not active.
– A failed import is rolled back completely.

– Limits: 2 GB ZIP, 20,000 files, 50,000 pages, 200,000 records per database and 64 MB for pages, records, comments and versions without the files (the file flowplan.json in the archive) – depending on the content, enough for around 100,000 records. The same limit applies to export, import and restore; database versions only go along as long as they fit.
Accounts, sessions and sign-in are not part of it – operations back them up every day with the whole instance.

en.heading: Version history
paragraphs: Page actions → Version history:
– Documents save automatically at most every five minutes, databases before the first change after ten quiet minutes.
– Save current version creates a state at any time; manually saved versions are kept permanently.
– Changes compares a version with the current state or with any other version (Compare with): added and removed text, for databases new, changed and removed records and properties.

– The comparison in detail: it walks the document block by block – headings, paragraphs, list items, table cells, quotes and code stay recognisable as such – and marks the single words inside a changed block: additions green, deletions red and struck through; unchanged blocks are dimmed. A summary states how many words came and went (for example "+120 words · −35 words"), and the arrows jump from change to change, also by keyboard. The same applies to the versions of a record document. Very long documents (more than 60,000 words on both sides together) or versions that differ in too many places are reported as too large to compare; they can still be restored.

– Bring back single paragraphs: compared with the current state, every removed or changed paragraph has a Restore button. The paragraph returns to its old place with its formatting; the rest of the page stays as it is.
– Restore sets the page back to that state. The authors view then starts over; the restored text appears as "earlier".

– Databases come back with properties, options and records – and with the settings that name options: done rule, workflow, automations and the issue sync's status mapping, as they were then. So restoring the version from before an option rename doesn't leave the done rule on the new name. An automation that comes back changed then acts for the person who restored it. Older and imported versions leave the settings as they are.
Automatic versions are thinned out to one per day after seven days and deleted after 180 days (adjustable in the administration).
Flowplan runs as a single container with SQLite and a data directory. Postgres, Redis or a separate search service are not needed – PostgreSQL and several instances are possible, but optional.

en.heading: Requirements
paragraphs: – A server with Docker and a persistent volume. Text recognition for scanned PDFs briefly needs noticeable CPU when uploading.
– Already running an instance on another server? Then move it after installing instead of starting over.
– A domain with HTTPS through a reverse proxy (Traefik, Caddy, nginx, Coolify, Pangolin …). For just trying it out it works without, see Without HTTPS.
– Optionally an OpenID Connect provider for single sign-on. Without one, people sign in with e-mail and password or a passkey, see Sign-in.
– Optionally an S3-compatible storage for files and the continuous database backup, see Storage, S3 and backups.
– Optionally a PostgreSQL database instead of SQLite, see PostgreSQL. How much hardware you need for how many people is under Sizing.

en.heading: Deploy in one click
paragraphs: No server of your own yet? Three ways to a running instance without setting up Docker by hand. All of them use the same image as the Compose file below.
Method Data HTTPS and address
Render SQLite on a persistent disk Automatic, https://.onrender.com or your domain
DigitalOcean App Platform PostgreSQL (dev database), files in a Spaces bucket Automatic, https://.ondigitalocean.app or your domain
Any server (Hetzner, Netcup, IONOS …) SQLite in a Docker volume on the server Caddy with a Let's Encrypt certificate for your domain

en.heading: Render
paragraphs: Deploy to Render →

The button reads the Blueprint render.yaml from the repository: a web service from the image ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:latest in Frankfurt, a 5 GB disk on /app/data and the health check on /api/health.
– Click the button, sign in to Render and confirm the Blueprint. The SMTP fields can stay empty (see E-mail).

– Render generates FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN. Once the deploy is done, copy it from the service's Environment tab and open https://.onrender.com/register?setup= – this first account administers the instance.

Costs: persistent disks need a paid instance – the Blueprint uses Starter, the smallest one with a disk; the disk is billed per GB on top (see Render's pricing). For more than a handful of people choose a larger instance (Sizing). On the free instance the data would be lost on every restart.

Address: without APP_URL, Flowplan uses Render's own address (RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL). For your own domain, add it under Settings → Custom Domains and set APP_URL=https://flowplan.example.com under Environment – ideally before the first account, because passkeys are bound to the address.

Persistence and updates: everything lives on the disk – Render runs a service with a disk as exactly one instance and stops it briefly on every deploy. Render keeps snapshots of the disk; for backups away from Render, add S3 (Storage, S3 and backups). To update, start a Manual Deploy: Render pulls the :latest image again.

en.heading: DigitalOcean App Platform
paragraphs: Deploy to DigitalOcean →
The button reads .do/deploy.template.yaml: a service from the image, a PostgreSQL 16 dev database and the health check on /api/health, in Frankfurt (fra).

App Platform has no persistent volumes: the container's disk is reset on every deploy and restart. That is why the template uses PostgreSQL instead of SQLite (DATABASE_URL points at the database) and expects a bucket for files:

– Uploads: create a Spaces bucket and a Spaces access key, and fill in S3_BUCKET, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (S3_ENDPOINT is preset for Frankfurt, https://fra1.digitaloceanspaces.com). Flowplan then puts every file into the bucket and fetches missing ones back after a deploy. Without a bucket, uploaded files are lost on the next deploy.
– FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN (generate with openssl rand -hex 24): the first account only via /register?setup=.

– FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (generate with openssl rand -base64 32): encrypts the files in the bucket and protects stored secrets such as API keys. It must be set here, because a secrets.key on the container's disk would be replaced on every deploy. Keep a copy in a password manager.

– Optional WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY and WEB_PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY (npx web-push generate-vapid-keys): without them, new keys are made on every deploy and push in the browser stops until people turn it on again. Push to the apps is not affected.

App Platform cannot generate secrets itself, so you enter these values when creating the app (or later under the component's Settings → Environment Variables). APP_URL is App Platform's ${APP_URL}: the ondigitalocean.app address, or your domain once you add it under Settings → Domains – then deploy again.

Database: a dev database has no backups and is meant for trying out. For real use, upgrade it to a managed database cluster, or attach an existing one with PostgreSQL 16 or newer (PostgreSQL). The image ships pg_dump and pg_restore, so Flowplan's own scheduled backups work on PostgreSQL too – store them in the bucket (Storage, S3 and backups). The connection is encrypted; uselibpqcompat=true in DATABASE_URL accepts DigitalOcean's own certificate authority, as psql does with sslmode=require. If the log reports permission denied for schema public, the dev database's role may not create tables – use a managed database cluster, where the database owner can (Role without superuser rights).
Updates: start a new deploy (Actions → Force Rebuild and Deploy); App Platform pulls the :latest image again.

en.heading: Any server: cloud-init or install script
paragraphs: For a virtual server (VPS) with Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 12 at any provider. Most of them – Hetzner Cloud, Netcup, IONOS, DigitalOcean Droplets, Vultr, Scaleway, OVHcloud – accept a cloud-init file as "user data" or "cloud config" when you create the server.
– Point your domain's DNS record (A, and AAAA for IPv6) to the server – with a new server, as soon as you know its address.
– Copy deploy/cloud-init.yaml, set the one line FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN=flowplan.example.com and paste it as user data when creating the server.
– After a few minutes, sign in with SSH and read /root/flowplan-README.txt: it holds the address and the link for the first account. Progress is logged in /var/log/flowplan-install.log.
On a server that already runs, the install script does the same:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannicschuller/flowplan/main/deploy/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- flowplan.example.com
What the script sets up:
– Docker with the Compose plugin from Docker's own package repository (skipped when it is already there).

– /opt/flowplan with compose.yaml (Flowplan and Caddy, which fetches and renews the HTTPS certificate itself), the Caddyfile and a .env readable only by root. Its secrets are generated on the server with openssl: FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN and FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY – keep a copy of the key in a password manager, encrypted backups cannot be read without it.
– The data in the Docker volume flowplan-data. It survives updates and restarts; for backups off the server add S3 or SFTP (Storage, S3 and backups).

– Firewall (ufw): only SSH, 80 and 443 stay open. On a server with a firewall of its own, run the script with FLOWPLAN_FIREWALL=off. Ports 80 and 443 must be free – if another web server already holds them, put Flowplan behind it instead (Coolify and reverse proxies).
– Automatic security updates of the system (unattended-upgrades).

– Image updates are off by default: you update when it suits you with cd /opt/flowplan && docker compose pull && docker compose up -d – the administration tells you about new releases. For an automatic weekly update (Sunday night), set FLOWPLAN_AUTO_UPDATE=weekly in the cloud-init file (or before bash in the command), or later run systemctl enable --now flowplan-update.timer.

Without a domain (FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN= left empty, or the script without an argument), Flowplan starts at http:// without a certificate – fine for a test, see Without HTTPS. To switch to a domain later, point its DNS record to the server and run the script again with the domain: it sets APP_URL and the Caddyfile, and keeps the data and secrets. Do it before the first account if you can, because passkeys are bound to the address.
Further settings (e-mail, single sign-on, S3) go into /opt/flowplan/.env, followed by docker compose up -d in /opt/flowplan – see Configuration.

en.heading: With Docker Compose
paragraphs: Flowplan is open source (AGPL-3.0). The ready-made image is in the GitHub Container Registry, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64:
Tag Content
ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:latest The latest version (release)
ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:0.7.0 A fixed version (currently 0.7.0), also as :0.7 and :0
ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:beta The latest manually built development state, or a release if that is newer – for trying out, not for production
Download the Compose file and the example configuration:
mkdir flowplan && cd flowplan
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannicschuller/flowplan/main/compose.yaml
curl -o .env https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannicschuller/flowplan/main/.env.example
In .env, set at least the public address:
APP_URL=https://flowplan.example.com
# Recommended once the address is reachable from the internet: openssl rand -hex 24
FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN=

With FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN you create the first account via https://flowplan.example.com/register?setup=; without the link a new instance offers neither sign-up nor restore. If the token is missing and APP_URL is not a local address, Flowplan warns at start in the log and on the setup screen.

For single sign-on also set OIDC_ISSUER, OIDC_CLIENT_ID, OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET and OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP (see Sign-in); for e-mails (invitations, forgotten passwords) the SMTP_* values from the configuration.
docker compose up -d

The container listens on port 3000 (bound to 127.0.0.1 only in the Compose file, so that the proxy sits in front of it). The volume flowplan-data on /app/data holds all content independently of the container. Choose a fixed version with FLOWPLAN_VERSION=0.7.0 in .env.
[!NOTE] An instance opens with the sign-in page. The website flowplan.org and this documentation are separate projects; the hosted instance runs at app.flowplan.org.

en.heading: Build the image yourself
paragraphs: From the source code (github.com/yannicschuller/flowplan):
git clone https://github.com/yannicschuller/flowplan.git && cd flowplan
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up -d --build
Or without Compose:
docker build -t flowplan:latest .
docker run -d --name flowplan \
-v flowplan-data:/app/data \
--env-file .env \
flowplan:latest
The image contains Node, Litestream for the S3 backup and curl for the health check. It runs as the user node (UID 1000).

en.heading: First start
paragraphs: – Open https://flowplan.example.com/api/health – the answer is 200 with "status":"ok".

– Open the address in the browser: a new instance offers Create account. This first account administers the instance. If the address is reachable from the internet, set FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN first and create the account via /register?setup= – otherwise someone could beat you to it (Sign-in). (With single sign-on: Sign in with SSO; administrators are the members of the group in OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP.)
– In the sidebar under Administration, set the instance name, upload limit, sign-ups and the other settings.

Moving or reinstalling? Instead of the first account, the setup screen offers Restore from a backup: upload a backup file or fetch the newest backup from S3 or via SFTP, encrypted ones with the old instance's key. Afterwards you sign in with the accounts of the backup (Restore while setting up). To move from a running instance there is also Moving an instance.

[!WARNING] With SQLite, exactly one instance runs. Several replicas would write to the same SQLite file. Do not simply scale horizontally; when updating, stop the old container before the new one. Several instances only work in cluster mode with PostgreSQL, Redis and S3.

en.heading: Without HTTPS
paragraphs: For trying it out only: Flowplan also runs at a plain http:// address, for example APP_URL=http://192.168.1.20:3000 on your own network. APP_URL must then be exactly that address – with http:// and the port.
The sign-in page and Administration → Instance then show the note "This instance runs without HTTPS". That is fine for a test, not for real use:
– Passwords cross the network unencrypted – anyone on the same network can read them.
– Passkeys, the offline copy, push, and the camera, microphone and clipboard are only available in the browser over HTTPS. Flowplan hides them or says why they are missing.

– The apps for iPhone, iPad and Android connect without HTTPS only to an instance on your local network (e.g. http://192.168.1.20:3000, http://nas or http://nas.local) and warn first. On iPhone and iPad, .lan or .home.arpa names don't work – enter the IP address there. See An instance on your own network without HTTPS.
– Cookies carry no Secure flag, and the browser does not upgrade requests to HTTPS.
At http://localhost or http://127.0.0.1 on your own computer there is no note: browsers treat these addresses like a secure connection.

For real use, put a reverse proxy with a certificate in front (see Coolify and reverse proxies) and change APP_URL to the https:// address. With Caddy two lines are enough; Caddy gets the certificate itself.

[!NOTE] Up to 0.8.0 Flowplan silently required HTTPS: at an http:// address styles and scripts were missing and the registration form simply stayed put. This is fixed – and forms with a password never send credentials in the address bar again.

en.heading: Update
paragraphs: When a newer release exists, the administration shows a notice with the new version number and a link to the changes (turn off with FLOWPLAN_UPDATE_CHECK=false, see Configuration). With the image tag :latest, this is all it takes:
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
With a self-built image, use git pull and docker compose up -d --build instead.
On start, Flowplan migrates the database itself. Make a backup beforehand (see Storage, S3 and backups); going back to an older version after a migration is not supported.

en.heading: Upgrading to 0.7.0
paragraphs: Nothing to do by hand; Flowplan creates the new tables (for idempotency keys and the push relay, among others) on start. What changes for operations:
– API description only when signed in: /api/openapi.json and /api/docs need a sign-in or an API token. Public as before with FLOWPLAN_PUBLIC_API_DOCS=true (see OpenAPI and SDKs).
– A shorter health check: without a token, /api/health only answers {"service":"flowplan","status":"ok"}; the details come with FLOWPLAN_METRICS_TOKEN (see Health check).

– Push to the apps through the push relay: notifications to the apps go end-to-end encrypted through push.flowplan.org. APP_URL must be the public HTTPS address and outgoing HTTPS to the relay possible – see Push relay.
– Usage statistics: monitoring counts requests, active people and storage – numbers only. Switch it off with FLOWPLAN_METRICS=off or in the administration (see Statistics).

en.heading: Kubernetes (Helm)
paragraphs: The chart lives in the repository at deploy/helm/flowplan. Flowplan runs as exactly one pod (SQLite) with a volume for /app/data; updates replace the pod with a short downtime (strategy Recreate). The chart (version 0.1.0) installs Flowplan 0.7.0 (appVersion); choose another version with --set image.tag=….
kubectl create namespace flowplan
kubectl -n flowplan create secret generic flowplan-env \
--from-literal=FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
helm install flowplan deploy/helm/flowplan -n flowplan \
--set appUrl=https://flowplan.example.org \
--set existingSecret=flowplan-env \
--set ingress.enabled=true \
--set ingress.hosts[0].host=flowplan.example.org
– Set OIDC, SMTP and S3 via oidc., smtp. and s3.*; secrets preferably in existingSecret (keys are the names of the environment variables). Further variables via env.
– appUrl is required (or taken from the first ingress host).

– The chart generates a random FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN (kept across upgrades; your own value via setupToken or in existingSecret). Create the first account with the setup link helm install prints at the end: https://flowplan.example.org/register?setup=; read the token with kubectl -n flowplan get secret flowplan -o jsonpath='{.data.FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN}' base64 -d.
– Use a block or local volume, not NFS (SQLite).
– Health checks use /api/health; the pod runs as user 1000 without extra privileges. helm test flowplan checks that it answers.
– The volume is kept on uninstall.
– To update: git pull in the repository, then helm upgrade flowplan deploy/helm/flowplan -n flowplan --reuse-values.

The chart's README explains every value. Several pods with PostgreSQL, Redis and S3 (cluster.enabled=true): see Cluster mode. The database role in DATABASE_URL should own the database but not be a superuser (Role without superuser rights).

en.heading: Without Docker
paragraphs: Node.js 22.13 or newer (the image uses Node 26):
npm ci
npm run build
FLOWPLAN_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/flowplan npm start
For local development, npm run dev is enough. Development mode also offers Open local workspace, a shared example account; production mode has no such access.

en.heading: Next
paragraphs: – Configuration: all environment variables.
– Coolify and reverse proxies: running behind Traefik, Coolify or Pangolin.
– Moving an instance: to another server, with an example for Hetzner Cloud.
– PostgreSQL and cluster mode: for larger teams.
A journal is a page with one sub-page per day. In the morning today's page is ready, with yesterday's open tasks already on it.

en.heading: Create a journal
paragraphs: New page → Journal. The page shows Today at the top and the past days below it with relative labels such as "Yesterday". The day pages are named after the date automatically, such as "Saturday, 26 September 2026".

en.heading: How a day comes about
paragraphs: – When a new day is opened for the first time, Flowplan creates its page. The day starts at midnight in your time zone.
– Open tasks from the last day move over – including nested sub-tasks. A small ↻ at the corner of the checkbox shows that a task was carried over from an earlier day.
– Completed tasks and the rest of the text stay on their day.
– Empty days disappear: if a day got nothing of its own besides carried-over tasks, it is removed again on the next day. This way the journal only contains days on which something happened.

en.heading: Create the day's page: automatically or on the first write
paragraphs: Under Set up journal → Days you decide when today's page is created:
– Automatically (default): as described above, as soon as the day starts and the journal or the app is opened.

– On the first write: Today first shows a draft with the template and the tasks that would be carried over from the last day. Nothing is saved yet – the top bar says "Draft – created when you start writing". Only the first keystroke, a ticked task, a tracker value, a place or a file creates the page. Until then carried-over tasks stay on their day, and the draft appears neither in the sidebar nor in search, graph or export.

The draft is the same on every device: if two devices start writing at the same time, exactly one page is created and both texts end up in it. If what the day starts with changed in the meantime (for example because a task was ticked yesterday on another device), Flowplan opens the stored page and says so. Text typed offline stays on the device and creates the page as soon as the connection is back.
Every day remembers which version of the template it was created from. A day that only holds that template counts as empty even if the template was changed later.

en.heading: Remove empty days
paragraphs: Set up journal → Days → Find empty days lists old days on which nothing was written: only the template, no open tasks of its own, no tracker values or places, no files, comments, sub-pages, favourites, shares or links from other pages, title and icon unchanged (upper/lower case or spaces do not count as a change). Today always stays. You untick what should stay and move the rest with Move … days to the trash – days can be restored from there. Flowplan never removes or merges old days on its own.

en.heading: Daily template
paragraphs: Set up journal (gear on the journal page) → Template: every new day starts with this content, such as "Grateful for", "Focus today" and "Evening review". Ready-made templates are available (gratitude & focus, 5-minute journal, work log, daily review); Use today makes the current day the template. Tasks from the template come back every day and are not carried over in addition. A day that only holds the template counts as empty and disappears like any empty day.

en.heading: Trackers, place and appointments
paragraphs: Above every day there is a bar:
– Trackers: mood (😞 to 😄), scales from 1 to 5, numbers with a unit (e.g. sleep in hours) or yes/no (e.g. sport). You decide which ones exist under Set up journal → Trackers.
– Place: enter freely; Location also stores the device's coordinates with a link to the map.

– Appointments: records of all databases with a date that you may see, including recurrences. Under Set up journal → Calendar you can also add a calendar via an iCal link (Google, Apple, Outlook, Nextcloud …).
In the settings under Day bar, place and appointments can be switched off for the whole journal.

en.heading: Completed this day
paragraphs: Below every day, Completed this day lists the database records that were completed that day – with the time, a link to the record and the database's name. The list is worked out each time the day opens and is not copied into the day; tick a record off elsewhere (in another tab, too) and it is there when you come back.
– A record counts on the day it was last completed, and only while it is still done by its database's done rule – reopen it and it leaves the list. The day follows your time zone.

– All / Only mine at the top of the list: Only mine (the default) shows the records you completed yourself and those a person property assigns to you, whoever ticked them off. When an automation completes a record, it counts for the person who set up the automation. The choice is yours for this journal, on all devices.

– Only records you may see appear – no private records of others, nothing from locked journals or encrypted spaces. On a day with nothing completed, the list is missing; beyond 100 records it ends with "and … more".
– It can be switched off for the whole journal under Set up journal → Day bar → Completed this day (on by default).

en.heading: Meeting notes
paragraphs: Next to every appointment there is Create meeting note. Flowplan creates a page below the journal – with the title and date of the appointment, the Attendees, an Agenda, Notes and Tasks – and opens it. Afterwards the appointment shows Open note.

– Attendees: from the connected Google or Outlook calendar, from the iCal link and from person properties of the record. Whoever is a member of the workspace with that e-mail address is mentioned; others are listed with name and address.
– Tasks with @person show up for that person in My tasks right away.
– For records of a database the note links the record. A PIN lock of the journal also covers its meeting notes.
– The same outline is available as the template Meeting note under Templates → Meetings.

en.heading: In the sidebar
paragraphs: Even after years with thousands of days, the journal stays short in the sidebar. Below the journal you find:
– Today – also when today's page has not been created yet; a click opens the day,
– the last 7 days,
– All days … with the number of all days: opens the journal page at its list or calendar.
Other sub-pages of the journal (such as meeting notes or monthly summaries) follow below as usual.
Under Set up journal → Days you choose for each journal which days appear in the sidebar:
– None
– Last 7 days (the default)

– Grouped by year and month: as above, older days in addition in folders by year and month, such as "October 2026 · 18". The folders only exist in the sidebar, they are not pages – you cannot drag anything into them.
– All: every single day, as before.

When a day is open, the sidebar always shows it – also when it is older than 7 days; in the grouped view its year and month unfold. Days can still be dragged, and the arrow keys work in the folders too (→ opens, ← closes or jumps to the folder above).

en.heading: From day to day
paragraphs: Above every day page there is a bar:
– ← Previous day and Next day → jump to the previous or next day with an entry – gaps are skipped.
– Today opens today's day.
– The month (such as "October 2026") opens a small calendar: days with an entry are highlighted and can be opened. The arrow keys move by a day or a week, Page ↑/Page ↓ by a month; Esc closes it.

From anywhere, ⌘ ⌥ Y (Windows/Linux: Ctrl Alt Y) or the command Journal: Today in the quick search (⌘ K) takes you to today – of the journal used last. With several journals the quick search offers one entry per journal. The shortcut can be changed (see Keyboard shortcuts).

en.heading: Overview on the journal page
paragraphs: – Streak: how many days in a row you have written, plus the longest streak, entries and words.
– Heatmap: the last year as squares, the darker the more you wrote. A click opens the day.
– On this day: entries from a week, a month, half a year and whole years ago.
– Last 30 days: the course of every tracker.
– List or calendar: the list shows an excerpt, place, mood and the first photo of each day; the calendar shows a month with photos as backgrounds.

en.heading: Review
paragraphs: Review sums up a week or a month: days, words, completed and still open tasks, tracker averages, places and photos. Copy as Markdown takes the summary along, for example into a weekly report.

en.heading: Summarise with AI
paragraphs: Summarise with AI in the review has the AI sum up the week or month shown: highlights and achievements, a chronological overview and what is still open or needs following up – in the interface language. It works from each day's text, the completed and still open tasks, the trackers and places.
– The result appears as a preview first; nothing is saved. Copy, Retry and Discard sit below it.

– Save as page creates a sub-page of the journal, such as "AI summary October 2026", with a note that it was made with AI. There is one such page per journal and period: ask again for the same period and the review offers Open or Create again and replace. Replacing changes the page's content; the previous state stays in the version history.
– A journal with a PIN is closed to the AI, even while it is unlocked. Days closed to the AI (Close pages and spaces to AI) stay out, with everything that belongs to them.
– The button is only there when summaries are available to you and the AI may read the journal; otherwise it is greyed out or missing. The AI reads long periods in parts.

en.heading: Monthly summary
paragraphs: In the review of a month, Create monthly summary creates a normal sub-page of the journal – not a day – and opens it, such as "Monthly summary October 2026". It holds:
– days, words, completed and still open tasks in numbers,
– Highlights: tracker averages, places, photos and the completed tasks with a link to their day,
– Still open: tasks from this month that are still open today, with a link to the day they are on now,
– Days: every day as a link with the beginning of its text.

The page is built from your entries alone, without AI, and can be edited freely afterwards. If the month already has a summary, the review offers Open monthly summary; Create a new one anyway deliberately adds another one.

en.heading: PIN lock
paragraphs: Under Set up journal → Lock, a PIN of 6 to 8 digits protects the journal (shorter PINs set earlier keep working): days, search, previews and images stay hidden until the PIN is entered. After 15 minutes or with the lock button it locks itself again. After five wrong attempts there is a five-minute pause, after twenty in one day it is over until the next day – across server restarts too. When another person enters a wrong PIN five times, the person who created the journal gets a notification. Only the person who created the journal and the workspace owners may set or change a PIN. Changing or removing it requires the current PIN – a wrong one counts against the same limits as when unlocking, and after five wrong ones the person who created the journal is notified as well. If the PIN is forgotten, owners can remove it on the lock screen with Reset PIN. Like other important steps, they confirm this once more – with their password, a code from the authenticator app or a passkey, or, without any of these, with a sign-in no more than ten minutes ago. The reset is recorded in the activity log and the journal's creator is notified. The lock also covers sub-pages of days, databases below the journal (their records, relations, calendar subscriptions and CalDAV) as well as export, the content archive, comments and duplicating – unlock first for those. It protects against glances but is no encryption: whoever has access to the server's backups sees the content.

A journal with a PIN stays private: setting the PIN revokes every share link and publication of the journal and the pages below it, switches off public forms of its databases and takes the journal out of links and publications of pages above it. The message after locking says how many there were; the security log records it. No new links, publications or public forms can be created for a journal with a PIN – not even while it is unlocked. Sharing or publishing a page above it with its sub-pages leaves the journal out. Forms for members only stay.

en.heading: If today's page was deleted
paragraphs: If today's page is in the trash, the journal says so and offers Create again (a fresh page for today; with On the first write a new draft) or Restore from trash.

en.heading: Days in lists, search, graph and export
paragraphs: A journal soon has hundreds of days. So that they do not crowd out other pages:
– Search and @ mentions: days come after all other hits. The filter Without journal days in the quick search leaves them out completely (it stays on for the next search).

– @heute, @gestern and @2026-10-27 (also @today, @yesterday) insert a link to that day of the journal while writing – the journal in the page's space, otherwise the one written in last. Today works as when opening the journal: the page is created or, with On the first write, the link goes to the draft. Days without an entry cannot be linked.
– Graph: under Journal days the graph hides the days, shows one dot per month (default) or each day.
– Counting: the home page, space settings and administration count days separately, such as "120 pages · 340 journal days".
– Export: in the Markdown ZIP, the scheduled export and Git, days sort by path in their journal's folder under 2026/10/2026-10-27.md – see Import, export and versions.
Journals behind a PIN you have not entered appear in none of these – not even in the numbers.

en.heading: Tips
paragraphs: – /todo or [] + space creates tasks that move along. They also appear under My tasks, without any @mention.
– Day pages are normal documents: headings, tables, images, mentions – everything works.
– Journals can be shared like any page. Whoever may only read sees the days but does not create any.
– The quick search finds entries across all days; Without journal days hides them.

en.heading: Workflows: new journal day
paragraphs: The workflow trigger New journal day starts a workflow when a day's page is created – so when the day is first opened or written in (or automatically, if the journal creates days itself), not at midnight. For fixed times there is the Schedule trigger. Journals with a PIN are closed to workflows.
All shortcuts at a glance. On Windows and Linux, Ctrl stands for ⌘ and Alt for ⌥.

en.heading: Everywhere
paragraphs: Shortcut Effect
⌘ K Quick search

⌘ F Find on the page: marks every match, Enter or ⇧ Enter jumps to the next or previous one, Esc closes. Selected text becomes the query. Also works in the desktop app and the apps; on a whiteboard it searches the board.
⌘ N New page
⌘ ⌥ N Quick capture (record in the capture database)
⇧ ⌘ Space / Ctrl Shift Space Desktop app: quick capture from any app (Quick capture (desktop))

en.heading: Your own shortcuts
paragraphs: ? (outside text fields), ⌘ /, the ? at the bottom of the sidebar or Show keyboard shortcuts under Settings → Appearance & language open the overview. – The arrow resets an action to its default, × removes its shortcut altogether, Reset all restores every default. Your own shortcuts are marked Custom.
– Combinations without ⌘, Ctrl or ⌥ (like ?) only work outside text fields and the editor.
– The shortcuts of the editor, the page tree, presentations and the split view are fixed; the overview lists them for reference.
In the iPad app with a hardware keyboard, holding ⌘ lists the shortcuts with ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥ – your own combinations included – in the iPad's overlay.
The overview names the keys as your device does: ⌘ and ⌥ on a Mac, Ctrl and Alt elsewhere. Through the API, the command shortcuts.save stores the same settings (see API and webhooks).
