en.heading: In this documentation
paragraphs: / jumps into the search, arrow keys choose a hit, Enter opens it.

Flowplan is available in {{facts.languages word}} languages: German, English, French and Simplified Chinese (简体中文). English also comes as English (US): the same texts, but dates with the month first and weeks starting on Sunday. Further languages can be added without changing the app's code – with any translation tool that understands JSON files.

en.heading: Choosing a language
paragraphs: Flowplan follows your browser's language; languages Flowplan does not know show English. Under Settings → Appearance & language → Language you pick a language (with its flag) from the list – it then applies on all devices, also to e-mails and push notifications; Automatic (follows the browser) undoes the choice and picks English (US) for browsers set to US English (en-US), English for other English browsers. On the sign-in page the small button at the bottom right (e.g. 🇬🇧 EN) opens a menu with all languages.

Dates, times and numbers follow the language (French: fr-FR, e.g. “15 oct. 2026” and “2 400,5”; Chinese: zh-CN, e.g. “2026年10月15日”). Calculations in notes use the decimal comma in French as well. Calendars start the week on Sunday in English (US) and on Monday in every other language – unless the view sets its own week start.

What you create yourself – pages, databases, properties – stays in the language it was made in. Templates and example content exist in German and English; French and Chinese accounts get the English ones.

en.heading: How translation works
paragraphs: German and English sit side by side in the code. Every further language is a catalogue in the app's locales/ folder that maps the English text to its translation:
"Sign in": "Se connecter",
"{0} commented on “{1}”": "{0} a commenté « {1} »"
– locales/en.json lists every text of the app (more than 3,500) and is the source for translation tools. It is generated, not edited by hand.
– {0}, {1} … stand for values such as names or numbers. They have to appear in the translation; their order may change.
– An empty or missing entry shows the English text – so a language can grow step by step, and new texts in the app never break anything.

en.heading: Adding a language
paragraphs: – Create the catalogue, e.g. for Italian:
``sh npm run i18n -- --add it ``
This creates locales/it.json with every text and empty translations.

– Translate – by hand or with a tool such as Weblate, Crowdin, POEditor or Lokalise (format “JSON key-value” or “i18next JSON”, source file locales/en.json). Machine translation (e.g. DeepL) works as a draft; please keep placeholders and HTML tags unchanged.
– Register the language: in lib/i18n.ts under LANGUAGES with its name and date format (it: { name: "Italiano", tag: "it-IT" }), and import the catalogue in lib/i18n-catalogs.ts.
– Check:
``sh npm run i18n -- --check # progress and wrong placeholders npm run i18n -- --check --missing # what is still missing, with the place in the code ``
The language then appears in the choice on the sign-in page and in the profile, and browsers in that language get it automatically.

en.heading: Keeping catalogues up to date
paragraphs: After texts change in the code, npm run i18n collects all texts again: new ones are added empty to every catalogue, unused ones drop out, existing translations stay. The tests only report missing translations; wrong placeholders make them fail.

In the code, texts are t("Deutsch", "English") in components, tr() outside of them and ct() for content the server creates. Tables of text pairs get a marker so npm run i18n finds them, e.g. // i18n-table: 1 for [German, English] pairs.

en.heading: Text recognition
paragraphs: Text recognition for scanned PDFs and images is separate: it reads German and English, French with FLOWPLAN_OCR_LANGS=fra,eng and Chinese (Simplified) with FLOWPLAN_OCR_LANGS=chi_sim,eng (see Configuration).
Connect Claude, ChatGPT and other AI assistants to your Flowplan using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). They search, read and write with exactly your permissions, nothing more.
Besides the optional built-in AI, MCP connects the assistant you choose. It works with your pages, databases and tasks. It sees only what you can see in Flowplan.

en.heading: Set up
paragraphs: – Under Settings → API & AI assistants, create a personal API token for the assistant. Choose Read only if the assistant should only search and read. Choose Read and write if it should also create pages and records.
– Copy the address shown under AI assistants (MCP). It is your Flowplan address followed by /api/mcp, for example https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp.
– Enter both in your client (examples below). The settings page has a ready-made configuration for each client and fills in a token you have just created.
Use a separate token for each assistant. That way you can see when each one was last used, and you can revoke one without affecting the others.

en.heading: Claude Code
paragraphs: claude mcp add --transport http flowplan https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp \
--header "Authorization: Bearer fp_…"
With --scope user the connection is available in all your projects. In Claude Code, /mcp shows the connection and its tools.

en.heading: Claude Desktop
paragraphs: Claude Desktop connects to remote MCP servers that use a token through the small mcp-remote bridge, which needs Node.js. Open Settings → Developer → Edit config, add the following to claude_desktop_config.json, and restart Claude:
"mcpServers": {
"flowplan": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp", "--header", "Authorization:${FLOWPLAN_AUTH}"],
"env": { "FLOWPLAN_AUTH": "Bearer fp_…" }
The token goes in env, not in args: that way it does not appear in the process list.

en.heading: ChatGPT
paragraphs: In ChatGPT, custom MCP connectors are available in developer mode, depending on your plan and workspace settings. Under Settings → Apps & Connectors, create a new connector with the address https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp. If ChatGPT offers token or API key authentication, enter fp_… there.

If your ChatGPT version only offers OAuth or "No authentication", ChatGPT cannot connect to Flowplan yet. Flowplan currently signs in only with personal tokens (see What is supported). Never put the token into the address as a workaround: addresses end up in logs.

en.heading: Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf and others
paragraphs: Clients that speak Streamable HTTP and accept their own headers use this configuration (the exact file depends on the client, e.g. .cursor/mcp.json or .vscode/mcp.json):
"mcpServers": {
"flowplan": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp",
"headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer fp_…" }

en.heading: Tools
paragraphs: Tool What it does Token
list_workspaces Your workspaces with your role and the spaces you can see Read
list_pages Pages in a workspace, optionally in one space or below one page Read
search Full-text search across pages, records, comments and file contents; also understands #tag, OR, NOT, created_by:, created:, type:, in:, title: Read
list_collections A workspace's collections (your own and shared ones) with their query Read
run_collection The pages and records that match a collection now, with your permissions Read
read_page A page as Markdown; databases with their records, whiteboards with their racks, devices, ports and cables Read
query_database Records with properties by name, property definitions, views; text filter, a saved view, paging Read
get_record One record with all properties and its record document Read
my_tasks Your tasks from documents and records, with due dates Read
create_page New document, database or whiteboard; documents can start with Markdown content Write
append_to_page Appends Markdown to the end of a document Write
create_record New record; properties by name, optionally with its record document (document, Markdown) Write
update_record Changes individual properties and/or the record document of a record Write
save_collection Creates a collection or changes its name, query, emoji and sharing Write
delete_collection Moves a collection to the trash Write

Properties are named by their name (or ID). Dates are written as YYYY-MM-DD, options by their name, people by e-mail address or name, and relations as a list of record IDs. Text properties (except the title) are formatted text: get_database marks them with markdown: true, and they are read and written as inline Markdown (bold, _italic_, ~~strikethrough~~, ` code , label, \n; see Formatted text). update_record accepts the version from get_record`: if someone changed the record in the meantime, the change is refused instead of being overwritten.

Write the record document with document as Markdown – when creating with create_record, later with update_record. update_record replaces the document; with documentMode: "append" the text is added at the end. The previous state is kept as a version, and open editors see the change right away.
In addition, each page is available as a resource flowplan://page/ (your favourites are listed). There are two prompts: Summarize a page and Plan my day.

en.heading: Workflows
paragraphs: For workflows there are list_workflows, get_workflow, get_workflow_catalog, list_workflow_runs, get_workflow_run (reading) and, with a write token, save_workflow_draft (graph JSON into the draft, also as a new workflow page – with the check), test_workflow (dry run or test run) and run_workflow (only workflows with a manual trigger). Activating and deciding approvals are not available over MCP – those are a person's decisions about rights. So an assistant builds drafts, and you check and activate them in Flowplan.

en.heading: Permissions
paragraphs: – Every call acts as the person who owns the token, with exactly their rights. The same checks apply as in the browser: workspace membership and guest access, private spaces, page and group permissions, private records, and journals locked with a PIN.
– Read tokens only offer read tools. A write call with a read token is refused.

– Write tools run the same actions as the interface. That means automatic versions, mentions and task notifications, followers, the activity log and webhooks all work as usual. Locked pages stay locked.
– Tokens never have administrator rights and cannot create or revoke tokens.
– The public demo has no MCP access: demo accounts cannot create tokens, and browser sessions are not accepted by /api/mcp.

en.heading: Security notes
paragraphs: – Treat the token like a password. Anyone who has it can read (and with a write token change) everything you can. Revoke a token under Settings → API & AI assistants if you no longer need it or it might have leaked; the connection stops immediately.

– AI assistants can be misled by content they read (prompt injection), for example by text on a page shared with you. Give an assistant a read token if it does not need to write. With a write token, use the client's confirmation prompts for tool calls.
– Answers can contain anything you can read in Flowplan. That content goes to the provider of your assistant, so check its privacy terms first.
– /api/mcp accepts only tokens, not the sign-in cookie, so another website cannot use your browser session. Requests from a foreign Origin are refused.
– Limits: 120 requests per minute per person, 2 MB per request, and answers are cut after 200,000 characters. Write tools have the same size limits as the interface.

en.heading: What is supported
paragraphs: – Transport: Streamable HTTP (POST /api/mcp, JSON answers, no session). Protocol versions 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05.
– Sign-in: personal API tokens as Authorization: Bearer fp_…. OAuth sign-in (for clients that only support OAuth) is not available yet.
– Not included: deleting content, administration, files and uploads, whiteboard contents.

en.heading: Examples
paragraphs: – "Search Flowplan for the offer for Müller and summarize the open points."
– "Read the page Team meeting and add a section Decisions with today's results."
– "Show my overdue tasks and make a plan for today."
– "Create a record in the Bugs database: title Login on iPad hangs, status Open, assigned to anna@example.com."

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
paragraphs: Flowplan is an open-source alternative to Notion, Confluence and AppFlowy under the AGPL-3.0. This is how you bring over pages, databases, images and files from the tool you use now.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs and Obsidian
paragraphs: Under Settings → Import & export → Import choose the target space at the top and, at AFFiNE, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, GoodNotes, Microsoft Word or Obsidian, the source (or let it be detected) and whether you want a page tree or a new database. Then choose the file:

– Flowplan uploads the file (with a progress bar) and shows a preview: how many pages, folders, files (with their size) and tags will be imported, and what will not work – such as encrypted text, unsupported macros or images missing from the export.
– Import creates everything in one step. If something fails, nothing is left half imported.
For all sources:
– End-to-end encrypted spaces cannot be targets (the server sees no plaintext there).
– You need write access to the target space; the workspace's storage quota and your personal limit are checked first (the preview already warns).

– Limits per import: by default 10,000 pages (documents, folders, databases, whiteboards and collections each count as a page; as a database: 10,000 records) and 20,000 files, 5,000 records per table, 10 MB per file in the ZIP (PDFs up to 100 MB). The operator sets pages and files with FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_DOCS and FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_FILES (Configuration). When a file brings more pages, the preview shows how many, names the limit and the variable, and Import stays disabled; files above the limit are left out (the preview says how many). ZIP exports and single files may be up to 100 MB. The AFFiNE workspace file (.affine) may be as large as the largest upload (Administration → Limits & retention, can differ per person), but at least 100 MB; FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_MB sets the limit for the whole instance (Configuration). When a file is too large, the message names the limit and where to change it.

– Preview and import run in the background. After the upload the page shows the progress and then the preview or the result. A reverse proxy timeout (such as a 504) no longer cancels the import; keep the page open until it is done. Each person can run one import at a time. While Flowplan creates the pages, the server doesn't answer for a moment – with very large workspaces for longer.

– If there isn't enough memory for a very large workspace, Flowplan refuses the import with a message naming what it needs, instead of crashing. Give Flowplan more memory with NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size= (e.g. 4096) in the container, or export the workspace in several parts.
– The file is uploaded only once: the preview keeps it on the server and Import uses it. Cancelling deletes it; otherwise it is deleted after six hours at the latest.
– The content is cleaned like when pasting: scripts, forms and embedded foreign pages are dropped. File names are cleaned; files a browser could run (HTML, SVG) are only stored for download.
– Links between imported pages point to the new pages. Images and attachments are uploaded – every file once, even if several pages show it.

– As a new database, every note becomes a record with the properties Tags, Created, Updated, Folder (the folder path) and – where present – Source. As pages, tags become the page's tags; missing ones are created in the workspace.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: From Notion
paragraphs: – In Notion: Settings → Export (for the whole workspace) or Export in a page's … menu. Choose the format Markdown & CSV and turn on Include subpages.
– In Flowplan: Settings → Import & export → Import, choose the target space at the top and the ZIP at Notion, AppFlowy or Markdown export (ZIP).
– Done – the import runs in one step. If it fails, nothing is left half imported.
What it turns into:
– Every Markdown file becomes a page, every folder named like a page holds its sub-pages. The IDs Notion appends to file and folder names are dropped.
– Every CSV file becomes a database. When both versions are there, Flowplan takes Name_all.csv (all records) instead of the current view.
– Columns get a fitting type: numbers, checkboxes, dates (also in Notion's format "September 24, 2026") and selects with their options; the rest stays text.
– Record pages are matched to their records as their document.
– Images and files the pages refer to are uploaded.
– Callouts become callouts and keep their emoji as their symbol.

– Links to headings (Page.md#heading) lead to the heading; notion.so links to pages of the export lead to the imported page (Notion's Markdown has no block ids, so links to single paragraphs lead to the page).
– Large exports that Notion splits into several ZIP files inside the ZIP are recognised.
Limits per import: 100 MB, by default 10,000 pages (FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_DOCS) and 5,000 records per table. Export larger workspaces in parts, for instance page by page.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: From AppFlowy
paragraphs: – In AppFlowy, export pages as Markdown and databases as CSV.
– Put the files into one folder – sub-folders become sub-pages – and make a ZIP of it.
– Import it in Flowplan under Settings → Import & export → Import.
Markdown becomes pages, CSV becomes databases; linked images and files come along.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: From AFFiNE
paragraphs: – In the AFFiNE desktop app, choose the export Full Backup (“Export a complete workspace backup”) in the workspace settings. This gives a file Name_….affine – the whole workspace database with documents, folders, collections, journal and files. The web app has no such file; there you export documents as a Snapshot (ZIP) – this needs Enable Snapshot Import Export switched on under the experimental features of the workspace settings. A snapshot contains documents, databases, whiteboards and files, but no folders, collections, journal dates, properties or icons. Only snapshots from AFFiNE versions up to the end of 2024 (with an info.json file) contain tags; newer versions no longer write tags into snapshots. To bring tags, properties and icons along, use the workspace file (.affine) – the preview points this out.

– In Flowplan: Settings → Import & Export → Import, choose the target space and pick the .affine file or the snapshot ZIP under AFFiNE, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs or Obsidian (source AFFiNE or automatic).

– The preview shows what comes along: pages, folders, files, tags, properties, page icons, whiteboards, databases, collections, days for the journal and how many documents become the content of database records – and what cannot be imported. Import creates everything in one step.
What it becomes:

– Where it goes: a workspace file (.affine) with several items at the top – folders, documents outside folders, collections – arrives below one page named after the AFFiNE workspace; the preview names it (“Everything below a page …”). A snapshot and a workspace with a single item at the top go straight into the target space – no empty page above them. A whiteboard counts with its document; journal documents go into the journal.

– Folders become pages with their documents below them. A document in several folders lives in the first one; the others link to it. Documents outside folders sit at the top level – below the workspace page, if there is one.

– Place documents with exactly one link below it (a switch in the preview, on by default; the preview shows how many): a document outside folders that exactly one other document links to in its text goes below that document instead of the top level. Chains nest (C below B below A). Documents in folders, journal days, the content of database records and documents linked only from a database, whiteboard or journal day stay where they are. When two documents link to each other, the first goes below the other. Links are unchanged; the switch doesn't apply when importing as a database.

– Text: headings, paragraphs, bulleted and numbered lists, to-dos with their check mark, toggle lists, quotes, code blocks with their language, callouts (kind by colour: red → caution, orange/yellow → warning, green → tip, purple → important, otherwise note; their emoji becomes the callout's symbol), dividers, tables, LaTeX (block and inline), bold, italic, underline, strike-through, code, links, text and highlight colours.

– Links between documents – in the text (@ references), as linked-doc or synced-doc cards and as AFFiNE app links – point to the imported pages. Synced documents become links. References to a block (references and doc cards with a block, app links with ?blockIds=) lead to that block; references to shapes on the canvas (elementIds) lead to the page.
– Tags become the page's tags, with their colours from AFFiNE (as a new database: the Tags property).

– Properties of a document (text, number, checkbox, date) become page properties of the same name; missing ones are created by the import if you may manage the workspace. Deleted properties and AFFiNE's own fields (created by, mode, template …) are left out.
– Icons: an emoji as the icon of a document, folder or collection becomes the page's icon. Icons from AFFiNE's own icon library have no counterpart; the preview gives their number.

– Images and attachments are uploaded and shown in their place – as when uploading in the editor: images as images, PDFs with a preview (they open in the viewer), audio and video with a player, other files as links. Bookmarks and embeds (YouTube, Figma, GitHub …) become links.

– Databases become a database page below their document and appear in the document at the same place as an embedded database. Columns: title, text, number, select, multi-select, date, checkbox, link (URL), progress (number in percent) and created. Rows keep their content as the record's document. Table views stay tables, kanban views become boards by the same column. Columns keep the order of the AFFiNE view (not the order they were created in); hidden columns stay hidden and column widths are kept (80 to 800 pixels). Image columns are not imported.

– Documents made from database rows: if you turned a row of a database into a document of its own in AFFiNE (the row's title is then a reference to the document), that document becomes the record's content – text, images, attachments, embedded databases and links, as for any page. It gets no page of its own; links to the document (in text, as cards, from collections and on whiteboards) lead to the record, and a folder that held the document lists a link to it. The record keeps the row's title and columns; if the title is nothing but the reference, it takes the document's title. This also applies when the row's only content is the card of a linked or synced document, and to snapshots that contain the document.

– If such a document consists of nothing but a database (in AFFiNE a database always lives in a document), the record shows that database as an embedded view, and the database itself sits below the record's database page – records have no subpages. Documents linked only from such records also go below the database instead of the top of the space, and databases that sit only on a document's whiteboard in AFFiNE become database pages below their document.

– Templates: documents marked as templates in AFFiNE become workspace templates (category Other, with emoji and tags) instead of pages; a document that is only a database becomes a database template. Links to a template become text. Only the workspace file (.affine) says whether a document is a template – from a snapshot, templates become ordinary pages. If you may not edit the workspace, the templates are saved as "Only me". The import preview shows how many there are.

– From the workspace file (.affine) the document's emoji icon (as the record's icon) comes along, its tags go into a multi-select column “Tags” (or “Schlagwörter”) of the database, and its properties into columns of the same name and a matching type where the row has no value – values in the row's own columns always stay as they are. If the database has no such column, the tags or properties are left out; the preview gives their number.

– If several rows refer to the same document, the first one (in the order of the import) gets the content; the others keep their own content and start with a link to that record. A journal document stays a day in the journal, and a row that refers to the document holding its own database only gets a link.

– The document's own databases are created where the document was (in its folder or at the top) and stay embedded in the record; a whiteboard of the document is placed there too, and its card points to the record.
– When importing as a new database, databases are left out; such documents then become records of the new database like all others.

– Whiteboards (edgeless): a document's text always becomes a document. If its edgeless canvas holds more than the note with the text – shapes, connectors, texts, images, frames, further notes, drawings, mind maps – or AFFiNE opens the document in edgeless mode, a whiteboard “Name – Whiteboard” is created next to it. Document and whiteboard are linked: the document starts with a link to the whiteboard, and a card on the whiteboard points to the document (where the note was). Shapes (rectangle, rounded, ellipse, diamond, triangle) with text and colours, connectors (straight, elbow, curved, with arrows and labels, attached to their shapes), texts, brush strokes, images, frames, further notes (as sticky notes), groups and mind maps (nodes as shapes, branches as connectors) come along. Whatever has no counterpart is left out; the preview gives the number.

– Collections each become a page “Collection: Name” with links to their documents as of the import: those added by hand and those the rules match (tags, created/updated, title, favourites, journal). The rules are written on the page as text. If not every rule can be evaluated (rules on custom properties, for example), only the documents added by hand are listed, with a note. A collection in a folder lives in that folder.

– Journal: AFFiNE's journal documents go into the workspace's journal, each into the matching day – the journal in the target space, else one in the workspace you may write in; if there is none, the import creates one. A missing day is created; an existing day gets the text appended at the end (under the AFFiNE document's title).
– Documents in AFFiNE's trash are not imported. HTML embeds and data views are left out; the preview names them.
– Whiteboards, databases and journal days only come along when importing as pages; as a new database every document becomes a record.

– Large workspaces: the .affine file may be larger than 100 MB (see the limits above). The server writes it straight to disk while it is uploaded, reads the documents one at a time while converting them, and images and attachments one at a time while writing them – memory only ever holds one document and one file. Workspaces with thousands of documents go in one import (up to FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_DOCS, 10,000 pages by default); folders nested deeper than 50 levels are merged into the level above. A reverse proxy in front must let such large requests through (see Coolify and reverse proxies).
– Safety: the file is only read; the size, number and nesting of documents are limited, text never comes in as HTML, and links keep only http, https and mailto.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: From Confluence
paragraphs: – In Confluence: Space settings → Export (Confluence Cloud: Space settings → Export space). Choose HTML or XML, each with all pages.
– Import the ZIP in Flowplan as above (source Confluence or automatic).
What it turns into:
– The space's page tree becomes the page tree in Flowplan (from index.html or the parent pages in entities.xml; where a page is missing there, the breadcrumbs help).
– Info, tip, note and warning macros become callouts (info → note, tip → tip, note → warning, warning → caution), code macros code blocks, expand toggles, task lists tasks with their status.

– Images and attachments are uploaded; attachments the text does not show are listed as links at the end of the page. Links to other pages of the space point to the imported pages. Anchor links (Page.html#Page-Heading, #… on the same page, ac:anchor in the XML export) lead to the heading or anchor.
– In the XML export only the current version of each page counts; older versions and blog posts are skipped. Creation and modification dates are kept.
– Macros without a counterpart (such as table of contents or Jira queries) are dropped; the preview names them.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: From Evernote
paragraphs: – In Evernote, save a notebook via … → Export notebook as ENEX. Put several notebooks into one ZIP.
– Import the .enex file or the ZIP in Flowplan.
What it turns into:
– Every note becomes a page; with several notebooks, every notebook becomes a page with its notes below.
– The note text (ENML) becomes normal text with formatting, lists and tables; checkboxes become tasks.
– Images and attachments (embedded in the ENEX file) are uploaded and shown where they were in the text; PDFs and other files as links. Attachments without a place in the text go to the end.
– Tags, created/updated and the source address are kept – best import as a new database, then they are properties to filter and sort by.
– Encrypted text cannot be imported; the preview warns.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: From Google Docs
paragraphs: – At takeout.google.com choose Drive and set the format for documents to HTML (recommended) or Microsoft Word. Single documents also work via File → Download → Web page (.html, zipped) or Microsoft Word (.docx).
– Import the Takeout ZIP, the web page ZIP or the .docx file in Flowplan (source Google Docs; single .docx files also work with Microsoft Word).
What it turns into:
– Every document becomes a page, Drive folders become parent pages.

– Headings, bold, italic, underline, strike-through, nested lists, tables and links come along; Google's redirect links point straight to their target again. Links to headings and bookmarks in the same document (#h.…, #kix.…) stay links to that place.
– Images are uploaded – including the ones embedded in the HTML.
– Word files: paragraphs, headings, lists (numbered and bulleted, also nested), tables (with merged columns), links and images. Comments, footnotes and headers/footers are dropped.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: From Microsoft Word
paragraphs: Import Word documents (.docx) under Settings → Import & export → Import with the source Microsoft Word (a .docx file is also detected automatically):
– One document: choose the .docx file. It becomes a page titled by its file name.

– Several documents: put the .docx files into a ZIP and choose the ZIP. Every document becomes a page, folders in the ZIP become parent pages. When everything sits in a single folder, that folder is left out.

Paragraphs, headings, bold, italic, underline, strike-through, lists (numbered and bulleted, also nested), tables (with merged columns), links and images come along. Comments, footnotes, headers and footers are dropped. Word's lock files (~$….docx) are skipped.

Older Word files (.doc, Word 97–2003) cannot be read by Flowplan. Open the file in Word, LibreOffice or Pages and save it as .docx, then import it. When a ZIP holds .doc or OneNote files next to .docx files, the .docx files are imported and the others are listed in the preview with the reason.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: OneNote
paragraphs: Flowplan does not read OneNote files (.one, .onetoc2, .onepkg) directly – it recognises them and tells you what to do. The way goes through OneNote's own export:
– In OneNote for Windows, open the page or section and choose File → Export, with Word Document (.docx) as the format.
– Import the .docx file (or several as a ZIP) in Flowplan with Microsoft Word.
If your version of OneNote offers no export as a Word document but only PDF, import the PDF as a notebook (as from GoodNotes) or upload it as a file to a page.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: From GoodNotes
paragraphs: Bring notebooks over from GoodNotes (5 and 6, on iPad, iPhone and Mac) as PDF. Every PDF becomes a notebook titled by its file name, every page a sheet with that page as its background – in the same size and orientation. You keep writing on it in Flowplan.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: Export from GoodNotes
paragraphs: One notebook:
– Open the notebook in GoodNotes.
– Tap Share or Export at the top (depending on the version, the icon with the arrow or in the ⋯ menu) and choose Export this notebook – not just the current page.
– Choose PDF as the format. If GoodNotes offers Include page templates, leave it on; otherwise ruling, grids and inserted PDF pages are missing from the background.
– Save the PDF to Files, AirDrop it to your Mac, or open Flowplan in the browser and import it right away.

Several notebooks: in GoodNotes' document overview, mark several notebooks with Select and export them together as PDF. Whether GoodNotes hands you single PDFs or a ZIP depends on the version – Flowplan takes both.

All notebooks at once: in GoodNotes' settings, turn on Auto-Backup, choose a cloud service (iCloud Drive, Google Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive) and set the format to PDF. GoodNotes then puts every notebook as a PDF into the backup folder, with your folders. Download that folder as a ZIP (Google Drive and Dropbox offer this in the browser; on a Mac, use Compress on the folder in Finder). The menus are named slightly differently depending on the GoodNotes version.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: Import into Flowplan
paragraphs: – Open Settings → Import & export → Import and choose the target space.
– Choose GoodNotes as the source (a PDF is also detected automatically).
– Click Choose and check file and pick the PDF – or several PDFs at once, or a ZIP of PDFs.
– The preview shows how many notebooks and sheets will be created and what is skipped. Import creates the notebooks and opens the first one.
Good to know:
– Several PDFs give several notebooks. Folders in the ZIP (such as the backup's folders) become parent pages; notebooks are listed in natural order ("Book 2" before "Book 10").

– Handwriting and highlights from GoodNotes are part of the PDF and stay sharp, but in Flowplan they belong to the background: you can write over them, but you cannot move or erase the old strokes one by one.

– Search: the PDF's text – typed text and, when GoodNotes exports it, the recognised handwriting – is indexed as for every PDF (the first 200 pages of each PDF). New handwriting in Flowplan is recognised on iPhone and iPad.

– Limits: up to 500 pages per PDF (the preview names further pages and leaves them out), 1000 sheets per notebook, a PDF or ZIP of up to 100 MB. Damaged or password-protected PDFs and other files in the ZIP are skipped and named in the preview.
– Notebooks are only created when importing as pages, not as a new database.

Flowplan cannot read the GoodNotes format (.goodnotes) and backups in that format: it is GoodNotes' own, undocumented format and changes between versions. Flowplan recognises such files and tells you what to do – export the notebook as PDF, or switch Auto-Backup to PDF. When a ZIP holds .goodnotes files next to PDFs, the PDFs are imported and the others are listed in the preview.
PDFs from other note apps such as Notability, Noteshelf or OneNote become notebooks the same way.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: From Obsidian and other Markdown folders
paragraphs: – A vault as pages: make a ZIP of the vault folder (with its .obsidian folder) and import it under Settings → Import & export → Import – via AFFiNE, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, GoodNotes, Microsoft Word or Obsidian with a preview, or via the Notion/Markdown import, which recognises a vault as well.
– Folders become pages with their notes below. A folder note (Projects/Projects.md or Projects.md next to the folder) becomes the folder's page itself.

– Wikilinks [[Page]], [[Page text]], [[Folder/Page]] and [[Page#Heading]] become links to the imported pages – resolved like Obsidian does, by path or file name. Links to notes that do not exist stay text.
– [[Page#Heading]], [[Page#^id]], [[#Heading]] and Markdown links with #^id become links to that heading or block; the ^id markers at line ends leave the text and become the block's id.
– Embedded files ![[image.png]] become images, ![[file.pdf]] file links; embedded notes ![[Note]] become links.
– Callouts such as > [!note] or > [!warning] Title become callouts of the matching kind.

– Tags from the frontmatter (tags:) and in the text (#tag, not in code) are collected: on pages as the page's tags, in a new database in the Tags property – together with Folder for where a note came from. Further frontmatter keys become properties on pages.
– Notes with frontmatter into an existing database: in a database choose Import CSV or Markdown and pick the .md files or a ZIP. The YAML properties become columns – see Frontmatter.

– Aliases: aliases: [PAC, Pompe à chaleur] (or alias:) in the frontmatter becomes the page's aliases or the record's Aliases property. @ mentions, search and unlinked mentions then also find "Chauffage" by "PAC", and the Markdown export writes them back as aliases:.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: After the move
paragraphs: – Check links: links between imported pages point to the new pages; links to pages outside the export still point to the old tool.

– Links to blocks and headings are kept. If a link in the source points to a particular place of another (or the same) page, it points to the same block in Flowplan after the import: a click opens the page and jumps there (see Links to blocks). If the place cannot be found (for example because the export does not contain it), the link leads to the page.
– Set up views: an import creates one table per database. Add board, calendar, gallery or timeline afterwards – see Views.
– Sharing: permissions are not carried over. Invite members or share single pages – see Sharing and publishing.
– Your data stays portable: Flowplan exports again at any time as Markdown with frontmatter, CSV and ZIP, scheduled and pushed to Git if you like – see Import, export and versions.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word, OneNote and GoodNotes
en.heading: Why move?
paragraphs: – Completely open source: all of the source code is on GitHub under the AGPL-3.0 – with no closed enterprise edition and no features behind a licence.
– Your data, your server: hosted on flowplan.org in Germany or as one Docker container on your own server – see Installation.
– No tracking.
How to move a whole Flowplan instance to another server – say from a home server to a rented one – with all accounts, workspaces, files and keys, usually with only a few minutes of downtime.
A Flowplan instance consists of exactly four things:
Part What Moves along
Container the image ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan (for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64) install anew, the same or a newer version
Data folder /app/data flowplan.sqlite (+ -wal, -shm), uploads/, web-push-keys.json, secrets.key; ocr/ and tmp/ are recreated yes – this is the actual move
Environment variables APP_URL, keys, OIDC_*, S3_*, SMTP_* … copy by hand, above all the keys
Domain and reverse proxy DNS record, HTTPS certificate switch DNS, set up the proxy again

This holds for every way of running it: docker run, Docker Compose, Kubernetes with the Helm chart, without Docker or in a deployment panel. If you use a panel, recreate the same container with the same volume and the same variables there.

en.heading: Prepare
paragraphs: – Write down the environment variables. All the old instance gets – depending on the setup from the .env, with docker inspect (section Env), docker compose config or helm get values flowplan. The full list is under Configuration.
– Keep the keys safe, apart from the data (password manager):

– FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (or the file of FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE) and FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS: without them, encrypted backups, the encrypted files in the bucket and the stored secrets sealed with it cannot be read.

– FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY (or …_FILE), if set. If neither is set, the key for stored secrets is secrets.key in the data folder – the built-in move tool takes it along; with the other ways you copy it yourself.

– What depends on it: AI keys, calendar connections (Google, Microsoft 365), chat app tokens, Git export tokens and the accounts' two-factor secrets. Without the key, accounts with two-factor sign-in only get in with recovery codes.

– Keep the domain. The same APP_URL means passkeys, the OIDC redirect, CalDAV and CardDAV accounts, the apps, incoming webhooks (Git, tickets, inbound e-mail) and share links simply keep working after the DNS switch. With a new domain all of that must be set up again (see Another domain).
– Lower the TTL of the DNS record at least as long beforehand as the current TTL (often 1 to 24 hours), e.g. to 300 seconds. The switch then takes effect within minutes.

– Set up the new server (example: Hetzner Cloud) with the same or a newer Flowplan version – an older one cannot open a newer database – and with the same environment variables. A bucket of its own for the new instance is simplest; with the same bucket see way C.
– Make a backup: Administration → Storage & backup → Whole instance → Download. It never hurts.
– Warn the users: Administration → Maintenance & notices shows everyone a maintenance window.

en.heading: Three ways
paragraphs: Way When Downtime
A: Move tool (recommended) whenever the new server can reach the old one minutes (only the final sync)
B: Download and upload a backup small instances, no network path between the servers from the backup until the new instance starts
C: S3 and Litestream the old instance already runs with S3 and Litestream from stopping the old to starting the new instance

en.heading: Way A: The move tool
paragraphs: Under Administration → Storage & backup (admins only), the new instance fetches everything straight from the old one: server to server, resumable and with checksums.
On the old instance – "Prepare the move"
– Move instance → Prepare the move. For safety Flowplan asks for your password; with SSO the sign-in must be at most 15 minutes old (otherwise sign out and in once).

– Flowplan shows the transfer address and the move token (fpmove_…) – only this once. The token is valid for 24 hours and only for the move: it may read the instance, make it read-only for the final sync and complete the move, nothing else. Only a hash is stored; Revoke invalidates it at once, and a new token replaces the old one. Creating, revoking and every step of the move are in the activity log and a security event under Administration → Security. Ten wrong token attempts from one address lock it out for 15 minutes.
On the new instance – "Take over from another instance"
The new instance is fresh: only the first admin account you create on first start. If it already has content, Flowplan asks for an explicit confirmation, because everything is replaced.

[!TIP] Same domain, but DNS still points to the old server? Then you cannot reach the new instance at its final address yet, and its proxy cannot get a certificate for it. Two options: - Temporary address: point a second name at the new server (say new.flowplan.example.org), start the new instance with APP_URL=https://new.flowplan.example.org first and do the move there. The pre-flight check then warns about APP_URL – that is expected. Before the restart in step 6, set APP_URL to the final address (the proxy may serve both names). - Without the interface: the command line on the new server.
– Move instance → Take over from another instance: enter the address of the old instance (its APP_URL) and the move token, Start the takeover.

– If the old server is only in your own network (LAN, a VPN such as WireGuard or Tailscale, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:3000), set FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true on the new instance for the move. Without it, as for every request the server makes, only public https:// addresses are allowed.

– First copy: a consistent database snapshot, every file in uploads/ one by one with a SHA-256 checksum, web-push-keys.json and secrets.key. The page shows bytes, files and the estimated time left. The old instance keeps running as usual. If the connection drops or a server restarts, Resume continues where it stopped – files already checked are not fetched again, a half file continues from its last byte.

– Pre-flight check → Check. Flowplan compares the settings of both instances – only names and check values (an HMAC keyed with the move token), never the values themselves – and checks whether the new instance reaches S3, SMTP and the OIDC provider. The result is a list of OK, Warning and Error:
Check Meaning
Version Error if the new instance is older than the old one: update it first.

FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY Error if it is missing or different: encrypted backups, the encrypted files in the bucket, stored tokens and calendar connections would be unreadable. Set the old key (a new one only in addition, the old one then in …_PREVIOUS).
Stored secrets Error if their key is missing (FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY or FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY). A generated secrets.key comes along by itself.
APP_URL Warning for a different address, with everything that must then be set up again.
OIDC, S3, SMTP, push, AI, other Variables missing here, with a different value, or set only here. Missing OIDC_ISSUER/OIDC_CLIENT_ID is an error – nobody would get in with SSO.
Same bucket Warning: both instances would write into the same folder (see way C).
S3, SMTP, OIDC reachable Error with the service's message. Many providers block outgoing ports 25 and 465 – use port 587 then.
Change the new instance's variables and restart it until no errors remain; the move continues after the restart.

– Make the source read-only and fetch the last state: downtime starts here. The old instance accepts no more changes – everyone sees "Move in progress: This instance is read-only", reading and signing in still work, changes (also through the API, CalDAV, webhooks, inbound e-mail) are refused with a clear message. The new instance fetches a fresh database snapshot and only the files that are new or changed since the first copy; removed ones go. This usually takes minutes.

– Apply on restart → Apply: Flowplan checks the database and prepares everything for the next start – exactly like Restore from backup. The old instance is told: it now shows "This instance has moved to …", stays read-only, and its move token is used up.

– Restart the new instance (the container, the pod or the service). On start Flowplan swaps in database, files and keys; the new instance's previous state stays in the data folder as pre-move-. The log says Instanz wiederhergestellt; vorheriger Stand in …/pre-move-….
– Switch DNS (below) and check afterwards.

You now sign in on the new instance with the accounts of the old one; the new one's first admin account is replaced. Existing sign-ins (browsers, apps) stay valid as long as the domain stays the same.

On the old instance, Move instance also offers Redirect the web interface: whoever opens it in the browser goes straight to the new address. Lift read-only makes it writable again – only when the move is called off.

While the old instance is read-only, its background services pause: incoming mail (the IMAP mailbox stays unread for the new instance), calendar and issue sync, workflows, reminders, deliveries of e-mail, push, webhooks and messengers, and scheduled backups. The app can't change anything there either.
Without the interface (command line)

The same without a web interface on the new instance – before any account exists there, say, or over SSH while DNS still points to the old server. The tool is in the image as /app/move.mjs and in the source as scripts/move.mjs (npm run move). It fetches the first copy, makes the old instance read-only, fetches the last state, prepares everything for the next start and tells the old instance the new address (--target-url, otherwise APP_URL). Interrupted? Run the same command again – it continues where it stopped.
# Docker Compose (in the new instance's folder; same .env, same volume)
docker compose run --rm flowplan node /app/move.mjs \
--from https://flowplan.example.org --token fpmove_…
docker compose up -d          # starts and applies the copy
# docker run
docker run --rm -v flowplan-data:/app/data -e APP_URL=https://flowplan.example.org \
ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan node /app/move.mjs --from https://flowplan.example.org --token fpmove_…
# Kubernetes (Helm chart)
kubectl -n flowplan exec deploy/flowplan -- node /app/move.mjs --from https://flowplan.example.org --token fpmove_…
kubectl -n flowplan rollout restart deploy/flowplan
# without Docker
npm run move -- --from https://flowplan.example.org --token fpmove_… --data /var/lib/flowplan
Option Meaning
--from Address of the old instance. On the command line internal addresses and http:// are allowed too – you decide where it connects.
--token The move token (or FLOWPLAN_MOVE_TOKEN in the environment, to keep it out of the shell history).
--data Data folder, default FLOWPLAN_DATA_DIR or ./data.
--target-url Address of the new instance for the notice on the old one (default APP_URL).
--copy-only Only the first copy; the old instance stays writable. Later run it again without the option for the final sync.
--yes Replace a data folder that already has content (its previous state stays as pre-move-…).
The pre-flight check is only in the interface; on the command line compare the variables yourself (list above).

OIDC, S3, SMTP, push, AI, other Variables missing here, with a different value, or set only here. Missing OIDC_ISSUER/OIDC_CLIENT_ID is an error – nobody would get in with SSO.

S3, SMTP, OIDC reachable Error with the service's message. Many providers block outgoing ports 25 and 465 – use port 587 then.
Change the new instance's variables and restart it until no errors remain; the move continues after the restart.

– Make the source read-only and fetch the last state: downtime starts here. The old instance accepts no more changes – everyone sees "Move in progress: This instance is read-only", reading and signing in still work, changes (also through the API, CalDAV, webhooks, inbound e-mail) are refused with a clear message. The new instance fetches a fresh database snapshot and only the files that are new or changed since the first copy; removed ones go. This usually takes minutes.

– Apply on restart → Apply: Flowplan checks the database and prepares everything for the next start – exactly like Restore from backup. The old instance is told: it now shows "This instance has moved to …", stays read-only, and its move token is used up.

– Restart the new instance (the container, the pod or the service). On start Flowplan swaps in database, files and keys; the new instance's previous state stays in the data folder as pre-move-. The log says Instanz wiederhergestellt; vorheriger Stand in …/pre-move-….
– Switch DNS (below) and check afterwards.

You now sign in on the new instance with the accounts of the old one; the new one's first admin account is replaced. Existing sign-ins (browsers, apps) stay valid as long as the domain stays the same.

On the old instance, Move instance also offers Redirect the web interface: whoever opens it in the browser goes straight to the new address. Lift read-only makes it writable again – only when the move is called off.

While the old instance is read-only, its background services pause: incoming mail (the IMAP mailbox stays unread for the new instance), calendar and issue sync, workflows, reminders, deliveries of e-mail, push, webhooks and messengers, and scheduled backups. The app can't change anything there either.
Without the interface (command line)

The same without a web interface on the new instance – before any account exists there, say, or over SSH while DNS still points to the old server. The tool is in the image as /app/move.mjs and in the source as scripts/move.mjs (npm run move). It fetches the first copy, makes the old instance read-only, fetches the last state, prepares everything for the next start and tells the old instance the new address (--target-url, otherwise APP_URL). Interrupted? Run the same command again – it continues where it stopped.
# Docker Compose (in the new instance's folder; same .env, same volume)
docker compose run --rm flowplan node /app/move.mjs \
--from https://flowplan.example.org --token fpmove_…
docker compose up -d          # starts and applies the copy
# docker run
docker run --rm -v flowplan-data:/app/data -e APP_URL=https://flowplan.example.org \
ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan node /app/move.mjs --from https://flowplan.example.org --token fpmove_…
# Kubernetes (Helm chart)
kubectl -n flowplan exec deploy/flowplan -- node /app/move.mjs --from https://flowplan.example.org --token fpmove_…
kubectl -n flowplan rollout restart deploy/flowplan
# without Docker
npm run move -- --from https://flowplan.example.org --token fpmove_… --data /var/lib/flowplan
Option Meaning
--from Address of the old instance. On the command line internal addresses and http:// are allowed too – you decide where it connects.
--token The move token (or FLOWPLAN_MOVE_TOKEN in the environment, to keep it out of the shell history).
--data Data folder, default FLOWPLAN_DATA_DIR or ./data.
--target-url Address of the new instance for the notice on the old one (default APP_URL).
--copy-only Only the first copy; the old instance stays writable. Later run it again without the option for the final sync.
--yes Replace a data folder that already has content (its previous state stays as pre-move-…).
The pre-flight check is only in the interface; on the command line compare the variables yourself (list above).

en.heading: Way B: Download and upload a backup
paragraphs: – On the old instance announce maintenance – changes after the download are lost.
– Administration → Storage & backup → Whole instance → Download. With FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY the file is encrypted (.zip.enc) – the new instance then needs the same key.

– The instance backup holds the database and files but not secrets.key and web-push-keys.json. Copy both by hand (or set the keys as variables): ``bash # old docker compose cp flowplan:/app/data/secrets.key . docker compose cp flowplan:/app/data/web-push-keys.json . # new docker compose cp secrets.key flowplan:/app/data/ docker compose cp web-push-keys.json flowplan:/app/data/ docker compose exec -u root flowplan chown node:node /app/data/secrets.key /app/data/web-push-keys.json ``

– On the new instance Restore from backup → Choose backup. The proxy in front must let such large uploads through (Caddy does by itself, nginx with client_max_body_size, Cloudflare at most 100 MB); otherwise bring the file to the server with scp and upload it there. At most 50 GB.
– Restart; the previous state stays as pre-restore-…. Then switch DNS.

en.heading: Way C: S3 and Litestream
paragraphs: If the old instance runs with S3 (files in the bucket) and Litestream (a continuous copy of the database under /db/), the new instance can start straight from the bucket:
– Stop the old instance – the Litestream of two instances must never write into the same folder at the same time.

– Start the new instance with the same S3_* variables, the same FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY and an empty data folder. Litestream restores the database; Flowplan fetches files on first access right away and all others in the background.
– Copy secrets.key and web-push-keys.json as in way B unless the keys are set as variables.
– Switch DNS.

With FLOWPLAN_LITESTREAM=off there is no continuous copy: use the newest scheduled backup from /backups/ instead (see Restore). The pre-flight check of way A notices a Litestream copy in the bucket and points to this way.

[!NOTE] Active workflows arrive on the new instance paused – with their draft, versions and held runs. So nothing starts twice while the old instance is still running. Check them afterwards and activate them again.

en.heading: Switch DNS
paragraphs: – After the final sync (way A) or the start of the new instance, change the domain's A record (IPv4) and AAAA record (IPv6) to the new server. Remove a port forwarding or tunnel at the old location.
– The new server's proxy gets its certificate as soon as the domain points to it (with Let's Encrypt over port 80) – give it a minute.

– Check what the world sees with dig +short flowplan.example.org (or nslookup). Whoever still has the old address cached reaches the old instance until the TTL runs out – which then shows the notice with the new one.
– Raise the TTL again afterwards.

en.heading: Check afterwards
paragraphs: – Sign in: with password, passkey and SSO. Existing sessions stay valid.
– Administration → Monitoring: all green? Administration → Encryption shows the same key ID as before.
– Administration → Storage & backup: S3 connected, the queue drains (with S3, Flowplan uploads every file once after a takeover), Back up now succeeds.
– Administration → E-mail → Send test email and Administration → Push notifications → Send test notification.
– Open a few pages, images and attachments; upload a file.
– AI, calendar connections, chat apps: if they work without signing in again, the stored secrets are readable.
– Refresh CalDAV/CardDAV in an app, open the desktop and mobile apps, trigger incoming webhooks (Git, tickets) once.

en.heading: Clean up
paragraphs: – Remove FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE on the new instance.
– Delete pre-move-… (or pre-restore-…) in the data folder after a few days, e.g. docker compose exec flowplan sh -c 'rm -rf /app/data/pre-move-*'.
– Keep the old instance running with its notice for a few days, then stop it, wipe its volume and revoke its S3 credentials (if it had its own). The move token is already used up.
– Turn on or check a scheduled backup on the new instance (Backups).

en.heading: Going back if something goes wrong
paragraphs: Until the DNS switch nothing is lost: on the old instance Administration → Storage & backup → Move instance → Lift read-only, and everything runs as before. After the switch: switch DNS back and lift the read-only state – what was changed on the new instance in the meantime only comes back with a move in the other direction. The new instance itself returns to its previous state when you replace flowplan.sqlite* and uploads/ with the contents of pre-move-… while the container is stopped.

en.heading: Another domain
paragraphs: If the instance gets a new address, set APP_URL to it and then set up again:
– Passkeys are bound to the domain: everyone signs in with password or SSO and creates them again.
– OIDC: change the redirect address at the provider to /api/auth/callback.
– CalDAV and CardDAV: set up the accounts in the calendar and contacts apps again.
– Incoming webhooks (Git, ticket sync, inbound e-mail) and share links point to the old address.

– Desktop and mobile apps store the server's address. They keep connecting to the old instance; there everyone sees the notice "This instance has moved to …", and changes are refused with a message naming the new address. Sign out in the app and enter the new address (desktop: Profiles → Add profile …). Leave Redirect the web interface off meanwhile: the apps refuse an address that redirects to another site.

en.heading: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: Message or state Cause and fix

"Internal addresses are only allowed with FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true" The old instance has a private address (LAN, VPN, localhost) or only http://. Set FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true on the new instance, restart, remove it after the move.
"Invalid or expired move token" Copied wrongly, older than 24 hours, revoked, replaced by a new one or used up by a completed move. Create a new one on the old instance.
"Too many invalid move requests" Ten wrong tokens from one address: wait 15 minutes.
The transfer stops Resume (or run the command again). Finished files stay, half ones continue.
"Checksum does not match" The file arrived damaged and is fetched again automatically; if it keeps happening, check the connection (proxy, VPN).
"This database snapshot no longer exists" The old instance made a new snapshot in the meantime (new token, restart). Resume fetches it.

Time-out at the start (502/504) The first time, the old instance computes the checksums of all files. A proxy with a short time limit in front (nginx: proxy_read_timeout 60 s, Cloudflare 100 s) gives up. Raise the limit or use the address without the proxy (with FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE).
Pre-flight: error for FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY or stored secrets Set the old instance's key on the new one and restart. Only then switch.
SMTP not reachable Many providers block outgoing ports 25 and 465. Use SMTP_PORT=587 with STARTTLS.
Nothing happens after Apply Applying needs a restart of the new instance. The log must say Instanz wiederhergestellt.
The old instance says "read-only" although the move was called off Move instance → Lift read-only.

en.heading: Example: Hetzner Cloud
paragraphs: A concrete way from a home server to a server at Hetzner, with Docker Compose and Caddy. Plan names and prices change – the Hetzner Console is what counts.

en.heading: Server
paragraphs: Setting Recommendation

Type CAX21 (Arm64, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM) or CX32 (x86, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM), or their current successor. 4 GB is enough for small teams; text recognition of scanned PDFs needs CPU for a moment, local AI (Ollama) much more. The image exists for linux/arm64 and linux/amd64, both types fit.
Location Falkenstein (fsn1) or Nuremberg (nbg1) – Object Storage is available there too.
Image Ubuntu 24.04
Networking Public IPv4 and IPv6. Keep an IPv4 address: not every registry and mail server is reachable over IPv6.
SSH key Add your own public key; never use password sign-in.

Firewall Create and assign a Hetzner Cloud Firewall: inbound TCP 22 only from your address (or your VPN), TCP 80 and 443 and UDP 443 (HTTP/3) from anywhere. Docker bypasses ufw on the server; the Cloud Firewall in front still applies.
Backups Turn on the server's Backups (a surcharge on the server price): daily images of the whole disk, in addition to Flowplan's own backups.

en.heading: Object Storage as S3
paragraphs: – In the Hetzner Console Object Storage → Create bucket, same location as the server (e.g. Falkenstein), visibility private. The name must be unique, e.g. flowplan-.
– Security → S3 credentials → Generate credentials. The secret is shown only once.
– Into the .env:
S3_BUCKET=flowplan-example
S3_ENDPOINT=https://fsn1.your-objectstorage.com
S3_REGION=fsn1
S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=<access key>
S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<secret key>
S3_PREFIX=flowplan

Endpoint and region follow the location: https://.your-objectstorage.com with fsn1 (Falkenstein), nbg1 (Nuremberg) or hel1 (Helsinki) as S3_REGION. With FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, files and backups are stored there encrypted; the Litestream copy is not (see Litestream and encryption). Object Storage is billed monthly, with a base price that includes a quota – see Hetzner for current prices.

en.heading: Docker, Flowplan and Caddy
paragraphs: Install Docker following the official guide for Ubuntu (docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu), then:
mkdir -p /opt/flowplan && cd /opt/flowplan
curl -o .env https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannicschuller/flowplan/main/.env.example
# create compose.yaml and Caddyfile from below, fill in .env
docker compose up -d
compose.yaml:
# Flowplan with Caddy in front (HTTPS from Let's Encrypt). Exactly one instance (SQLite).
services:
flowplan:
image: ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:${FLOWPLAN_VERSION:-latest}
env_file: .env
environment:
FLOWPLAN_DATA_DIR: /app/data
# Caddy is the one proxy in front and sets X-Forwarded-For.
FLOWPLAN_TRUSTED_PROXIES: "1"
volumes:
- flowplan-data:/app/data
restart: unless-stopped
healthcheck:
test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health').then(r=>process.exit(r.ok?0:1)).catch(()=>process.exit(1))"]
interval: 30s
timeout: 5s
start_period: 20s
retries: 3
caddy:
image: caddy:2
ports:
environment:
FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN: ${FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN}
volumes:
- ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
- caddy-data:/data
- caddy-config:/config
depends_on:
- flowplan
restart: unless-stopped
volumes:
flowplan-data:
caddy-data:
caddy-config:
Caddyfile:
{$FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN} {
encode zstd gzip
reverse_proxy flowplan:3000
In the .env, besides the old instance's values:
FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN=flowplan.example.org
APP_URL=https://flowplan.example.org
# SMTP: Hetzner blocks outgoing ports 25 and 465 for new accounts – use 587 with STARTTLS.
SMTP_PORT=587
SMTP_SECURE=false
# Only for the move, when the home server is reachable only in the LAN/VPN:
# FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true

For a temporary address during the move, set FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN=new.flowplan.example.org and the matching APP_URL; after Apply, change both to the final domain and restart with docker compose up -d – the same restart applies the move. Caddy can also serve both names: {$FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN}, new.flowplan.example.org { … }.
Prefer Kubernetes? The repository's Helm chart runs on a single server too (with k3s, say); the move then goes through the interface or kubectl exec … node /app/move.mjs (above).

en.heading: The run with the home server
paragraphs: – A day before, lower the DNS record's TTL to 300 seconds.
– Set up the Hetzner server as above, with the same variables as at home (the keys!), and start it with docker compose up -d; create the first account.
– At home Prepare the move; on the Hetzner server Take over from another instance with the home server's public address (or its VPN address with FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true).
– Pre-flight check until no errors remain. Make the source read-only and fetch the last state, Apply, docker compose restart flowplan.
– Point the A and AAAA records to the Hetzner server's addresses, remove the port forwarding at the router.
– Check afterwards, clean up after a few days.

A notebook is a page of sheets to write on – with the Apple Pencil, another tablet pen, a mouse or a finger, like a paper notebook. The sheets sit one below the other and you scroll through them. Each sheet has its paper (lined, grid, dotted, Cornell, music staff …) or a page of a PDF as its background. There is also handwriting in documents: a drawing block in the middle of the text.

en.heading: Creating a notebook
paragraphs: New page → Notebook (or New notebook in the command palette). A new notebook starts with one sheet of lined A4 paper.

From a PDF: in the same dialog, choose a file under Open a PDF as the notebook. Every page of the PDF becomes a sheet with that page as its background – lecture slides, worksheets or forms are then written on as if printed. ⋯ → Import PDF … adds more PDF pages to an existing notebook, after the current sheet. Up to 500 pages per import and 1000 sheets per notebook.

From GoodNotes and other note apps: export the notebooks as PDF and import them under Settings → Import & export → Import with the source GoodNotes – several at once or as a ZIP, every PDF becomes a notebook. Step by step: Moving from GoodNotes.

en.heading: Paper
paragraphs: Template Looks like
Blank no lines
Lined (college) lines 7.1 mm apart (college ruled) with a margin
Lined (wide) lines 8.7 mm apart (wide ruled) with a margin
Grid (5 mm) squared paper
Dotted dots every 5 mm
Cornell notes title band, cue column on the left, summary at the bottom
Music staff 12 staves (8 in landscape)
Plus A4 or Letter, portrait or landscape, and light or dark. On dark paper, black ink shows light and the highlighter glows.
The lines icon in the toolbar (or Change paper … in a sheet's menu) opens the choice. Apply to:
– This sheet – only the current sheet gets its own paper;
– Notebook default – for all sheets without their own paper and for new sheets;
– All sheets – sets the default and removes every sheet's own paper.
Sheets from a PDF keep their PDF page and its size.

en.heading: Writing
paragraphs: Whoever may edit the page writes right away – there is no "Annotate" step as in the PDF viewer. At the top is the toolbar: Pen (with pressure), Highlighter, Eraser (whole strokes or partial), Lasso (move, resize, recolour, copy, duplicate, delete), Text and Laser pointer, three favourite pens, colours, widths and the pen settings. They work as when annotating PDFs: only the pen writes once you have used it, fingers scroll and zoom, a resting hand leaves no marks; holding still at the end of a stroke straightens it into a line, rectangle, ellipse …

Everything is saved as you write (on the right of the toolbar: Saved). Every change of a sheet is a version. When two people write on the same sheet at the same time, both keep their strokes; a notice says that someone wrote along. What others write appears after a few seconds.
Readers of the page see all sheets, zoom and export, but no tools.

en.heading: Keyboard shortcuts
paragraphs: Key Does
P H E L T K Pen, highlighter, eraser, lasso, text, laser pointer
⌘ Z / ⇧ ⌘ Z Undo / redo
⌘ C, ⌘ V, ⌘ D, Delete Copy, paste, duplicate, delete the selection
⌘ + / ⌘ − / ⌘ 0 Zoom in, zoom out, fit to width
⇧ ⌘ ↵ New sheet after the current one
⌥ ↓ / ⌥ ↑ Next / previous sheet
⌘ S Save now
On Windows and Linux use Ctrl instead of ⌘ and Alt instead of ⌥. On an iPad with a keyboard the same shortcuts apply.

en.heading: Page overview
paragraphs: The sidebar icon on the left of the toolbar shows all sheets as previews; a tap jumps to the sheet. With ⋯ on a preview: New sheet after, Duplicate (with everything on it), Change paper …, Move up, Move down and Delete. You also change the order by dragging a preview or with ⌥ ↑/↓ on the focused preview. + in the toolbar adds a sheet after the current sheet or at the end, as does Add sheet below the last sheet.

en.heading: Exporting as PDF
paragraphs: ⋯ → Export as PDF downloads the notebook as a PDF: one page per sheet in the sheet's size, paper and handwriting as vectors (sharp at any zoom), PDF sheets with their original page including its text. The Markdown export puts the notebook into the ZIP as a PDF as well and writes a short Markdown file with a link to it and the recognised text. The PDF, Word and EPUB exports show the sheets as pictures (Word: only their text). Published and shared notebooks are read-only.

en.heading: Handwriting in documents
paragraphs: Type /draw in a document (also /zeichnen, /dessin, /handwriting or /sketch): a drawing block across the full width appears. With a pen you write on it right away; with a mouse or finger after a tap into the block (or on Draw) – so a finger keeps scrolling the document. Then the toolbar appears with the block's paper (Blank, Lined, Grid) and Done. Drag the bottom edge to change the height (or use the arrow keys on the handle).

The handwriting belongs to the block and is saved as you draw. For working together this means: when several people draw in the same block at once, their strokes are merged instead of overwritten; the text around it you edit together as always. Copied or duplicated blocks (also into another document) take their drawing along and are independent afterwards. Permissions, locking and the trash work as for the document; on published pages, in share links and in exports the block shows as a picture.

en.heading: Recognising handwriting (iPhone and iPad)
paragraphs: In the Flowplan app for iPhone and iPad the device itself recognises what you write – the strokes do not leave the device for this:

– Search: shortly after saving, the handwriting of a sheet, a drawing block or a PDF page is recognised and its text saved along. Search then also finds notebooks, documents and PDFs by what is handwritten.

– Convert to text: select handwriting with the lasso and choose Convert to text (the Aa icon) in the selection's bar. In a notebook and on PDFs, typed text replaces the strokes in their place; in a drawing block the text becomes a paragraph below the block. Undo brings the strokes back.
In the browser and the desktop app there is no recognition; Convert to text does not appear there. Text typed on sheets, in drawing blocks and on PDFs is searchable everywhere.

en.heading: Limits
paragraphs: – Encrypted spaces have no notebooks and no drawing blocks.
– Locked pages show the handwriting; it can be changed after unlocking.
– A notebook's page versions only hold its appearance; each sheet has its own versions of the handwriting.
– Drawing blocks exist in documents and journal days, not in the documents of database records.
Flowplan runs in the browser, can be installed as an app and keeps working without a connection.

en.heading: Work without a connection
paragraphs: Flowplan always saves documents locally in the browser first (IndexedDB) and syncs them with the server as soon as it can be reached. If the connection drops, you simply keep writing; other people's changes are merged when you reconnect.

en.heading: Turn on offline use
paragraphs: Under Settings → Offline & devices, the device also stores the app, the workspace, all readable pages and the records and files you open later. Then you can open pages, read documents and databases and edit text even without a connection.
– Online, the current state always comes from the server; the copy only serves without a connection.
– If the sign-in has expired, Flowplan shows the sign-in page online – without a connection, the stored copy still opens.
– The copies contain private content. They are removed when you sign out, when you turn the feature off and when another person signs in.
The whole app on the device

The copy holds the whole app – not only the parts you already opened online. The editor, calendar, timeline and gallery views, dashboards, charts, whiteboards, notebooks, math, Mermaid diagrams and the PDF viewer then load without a connection as well.
– Storage: about 18 MB on the device (around 5 MB to download), once per version. Flowplan only stores the app's files when the device has enough space.

– New version: after an update, Flowplan loads the new version's files with the next refresh; files that did not change are taken over instead of downloaded again. As soon as the new version is stored completely, the old one is removed.
– Settings → Offline & devices shows a line like “The app is stored for offline use (version 0.7.0) · 18 MB” – or how many files are still missing.

– If a part is missing without a connection after all, Flowplan shows “Not available offline – try again when you're online” with Try again in its place; the rest of the app keeps working, and the part loads by itself once the connection is back. A record whose content is not in the copy shows “This record is not available offline.”
The copy stays current

While Flowplan is open, it keeps the copy up to date on its own: at start, when the connection comes back, when you bring the app back to the foreground, and every 6 hours. It only loads what changed since the last update – usually two small requests.
– New pages are added; changed pages, records and documents are loaded again.
– Deleted pages and pages you may no longer read (including a journal behind a PIN) leave the copy together with their records and files.
– When an update takes a moment, Updating offline copy … shows briefly in the bottom left corner.
– When the sign-in has expired, Flowplan does not update – the existing copy stays as it is.
Settings → Offline & devices shows the state, for example “Offline copy updated 2 h ago · 312 pages · 85 MB”. Update now loads every page again.

Also store record contents and files also stores the documents of all database records and the files of the pages, even ones you have never opened – at most 200 MB and only while the device has enough space. Without it, only records and files you opened once are kept. Turning it off removes the records and files stored in addition.
Without a connection, Flowplan shows the date of the copy below the offline notice when it is older than 7 days (“Offline copy from Oct 12”).

[!NOTE] Installed as an app (Chrome, Edge, Android), Flowplan also updates the copy in the background while the app is closed, when the browser allows it (Periodic Background Sync). The browser decides whether and how often – usually only for apps used often. Records and files never opened are loaded only by the open app.
