en.heading: Restore
paragraphs: – From an instance backup: upload it under Administration → Storage & backup → Restore from backup (at the very end). Flowplan checks it and applies it on the next restart; the previous state stays as pre-restore-… in the data directory.

– From a scheduled backup, with the app stopped: decrypt an encrypted one first, then move the existing flowplan.sqlite with -wal and -shm aside and put the backup in place as /app/data/flowplan.sqlite. With S3, the files follow from the bucket.

– On a new host with S3: start a new installation with the same S3_* variables and an empty volume. Litestream restores the database, the files follow in the background. Stop the old instance first; secrets.key and web-push-keys.json are not in the bucket (see Moving an instance, way C).
– Moving to another server: see Moving an instance – the built-in move tool fetches database, files and keys straight from the old instance, with a few minutes of downtime.

– From a scheduled backup of an instance with PostgreSQL (flowplan-….dump, .dump.enc): also upload it under Restore from backup, or on the setup screen of a new instance with PostgreSQL. Only the database is replaced, the files stay. Only the data of Flowplan's tables is loaded; an archive with custom functions, views or triggers in Flowplan's schema is refused – see PostgreSQL, restoring.
– An earlier point in time, with the app stopped:
litestream restore -config /etc/litestream.yml \
-timestamp 2026-09-26T12:00:00Z -o /app/data/flowplan.sqlite
Move the existing flowplan.sqlite with -wal and -shm aside first.

en.heading: Restore while setting up
paragraphs: A new, still empty instance takes over a backup right on the setup screen: under Create account, click Restore from a backup (Installation, first start). You can use

– File: a scheduled backup (flowplan-….sqlite, .sqlite.enc) or the backup of the whole instance (flowplan-instanz-….zip, .zip.enc), up to 50 GB. The upload is written straight to disk and shows its progress. If attachments are then missing – neither in the backup nor in the instance's file storage –, the page says how many; if the old instance kept its files in S3 or on an SFTP server, restore from there.
– S3: the newest scheduled backup from /backups/ of a bucket, with the files from /uploads/ – any missing there come from /.deleted/uploads/.

– SFTP: the newest backup from the folder, with the files from uploads/ (if Include files was on) – any missing there come from .deleted/uploads/. Flowplan shows the host key first; it only signs in once you confirm The fingerprint matches.

If the backup is encrypted, the page asks for the old instance's key (FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY) – or it is already set on the new one. Flowplan checks the database (intact, a Flowplan database, not from a newer version – older ones are brought up to date when they open, as with an update), puts the empty initial state aside as pre-restore-… and applies the backup right away. Afterwards you sign in with an account from the backup. If Litestream runs (S3 without FLOWPLAN_LITESTREAM=off), the backup is applied on the next restart of the container – the page says so.

This is only possible while the instance has no account, and with FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN set only via the setup link. As soon as an account exists, the server refuses every request for it; then Administration → Storage & backup → Restore from backup remains.

[!NOTE] Stored secrets (authenticator apps, AI and messenger keys, the SFTP password) can only be read with the same FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY or FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY as on the old instance; without either, the key is in secrets.key in the data folder, which is in no backup. If you entered a key while restoring, set it as FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY afterwards.

en.heading: Quotas
paragraphs: FLOWPLAN_WORKSPACE_QUOTA_MB or Administration → Limits & retention sets a default quota per workspace; under Administration → Workspaces it can be overridden per workspace. Uploads, copies, templates and imports beyond the quota are refused.
Templates are saved pages – documents, databases or whole page trees – from which new pages are created. On top of that there are record templates within a database.

en.heading: Starter templates
paragraphs: Templates in the sidebar – or From a template in the New page dialog – shows {{facts.templates}} built-in templates in {{facts.templateCategories word}} categories, each with example records and fitting views:
Category Templates
Projects Project planning, product roadmap, sprint board, project brief
Meetings Meeting notes, meeting note, 1:1 conversation, retrospective, meeting minutes
Knowledge & documentation Team wiki, how-to guide, diagram page, decision log, FAQ
Planning & goals OKRs, quarterly planning, content calendar, budget planning
Personal To-do list, reading list, habit tracker, travel planning
Other Contacts & customers, job applications, inventory, event planning
A click asks for a title and space and creates the page. Dates in the examples are set relative to today.
The Diagram page is a full-width page with one empty draw.io diagram; draw.io opens as soon as the page is created (if the instance uses draw.io).

As soon as there are templates of your own, the category My templates comes right after All: it shows only the saved templates – your personal ones ("Only me"), the workspace's and those for all workspaces – without the built-in ones.

If you open the gallery from the New page dialog, the page goes where you were creating it – in the chosen space and under the chosen page – with your own templates too. Closing the gallery takes you back to the dialog.

en.heading: Your own templates
paragraphs: – On a page, choose Page actions → Save as template.
– Choose a name, category and visibility:
– Only me,
– Workspace: all members of this workspace,
– All workspaces of the instance,
– Public gallery (administrators only): visible even without an account.

en.heading: Templates of a space or of the whole workspace
paragraphs: Like tags and properties, your own template belongs to a space or to the whole workspace. When saving, Only in this space (the page's space) is preset; In the whole workspace is saved by owners only (private templates by anyone). What existed before this distinction applies to the whole workspace.

– The gallery first shows the templates of the space the new page is created in, and those of the workspace; All spaces also shows those of other spaces. A label names the space or “Workspace”. A space's templates are seen only by those who may open it.

– Templates for the whole workspace use only tags and properties of the whole workspace. If the page carries tags or properties of its space, Flowplan names them; Save then takes them out of the template (or make them workspace-wide first).

– Using a template from another space: if it brings tags or properties of its space, a step asks for each: map (to one of the same name or another tag, or a property of the same type, in the target space), copy (into the target space, the default without one of the same name) or remove.

– Copy makes a copy of the template for another space (or the workspace) – with the same step; copied tags and properties are created in the target space right away. Edit → Applies moves the template itself there.

Templates store their own copies of the files and stay usable even if the source page is deleted. The page's tags and property values come along too; new pages from the template get them (missing tags are created). Database templates contain views, records with their content, record templates and the form design. Templates can be renamed, made private or shared and moved to the trash. In the Template trash, Restore brings a template back, Delete permanently deletes it with its files, and Empty template trash deletes all you may manage (your own; as an owner all of the workspace; templates for all workspaces only admins). Pages already created are kept. After the trash period (30 days by default) templates in the trash are deleted automatically.

en.heading: Record templates
paragraphs: In a database, Record templates opens the templates for records: property values and content are applied to every new record. One template can be the default, so that New uses it automatically.

A template is made from a record: write the content, then Save as template. To change a template, choose Edit next to it in Record templates – a draft opens as a record; save it with Save as template and, under Save as, Replace “…”. The template keeps its role as default template and in automations. You can delete the draft record afterwards.

en.heading: Placeholders
paragraphs: Text in double curly braces is replaced with the record's values when the template is applied – in the title, headings, text, tables and callouts, and in text properties of the template. Example: “Kickoff {{Company}} on {{Meeting}}”.
– {{Property}} – the value of a property of the database. Upper and lower case don't matter.

– {{Title}}, {{Today}} (also {{Date}}), {{Now}}, {{Creator}}, {{Me}} (whoever applies the template) and {{Database}} are built in. The German names ({{Titel}}, {{Heute}}, {{Datum}}, {{Jetzt}}, {{Ersteller}}, {{Ich}}, {{Datenbank}}) work too. If a property has the same name (say “Date”), the property wins.
– The { } icon next to a record's Content (Insert placeholder) inserts placeholders at the cursor and lists all properties of the database.

Values appear as in the table: dates in your language and in the property's date format, multi-select joined by commas, relations as the titles of the linked records, people by name, checkboxes as ✓ or ✗. Empty properties give empty text; unknown placeholders stay as written. Values are always inserted as plain text, never as formatting or HTML. Properties only certain people may see stay empty – the text is visible to everyone who sees the record.
Renaming properties is fine: templates remember the property, not just its name. In the draft of a template the placeholders stay as written.

en.heading: Apply a template to an existing record
paragraphs: In the … menu of an open record, or by right-clicking a row, choose Apply template …, then the template and what happens to the existing content:
– Apply only if the content is empty – if the record already has text, Flowplan says so and changes nothing.
– Append below – the template's text goes below the existing text.

Existing text is never overwritten and filled properties stay; only empty properties get the template's values. The previous content is kept as a version, and Undo in the notice brings it back. This needs edit rights on the record; the database's workflow rules apply as well. To do this automatically, use an automation.

en.heading: Public template gallery
paragraphs: Under /templates, the built-in templates and all templates with the visibility Public gallery are available even without an account, filtered by category, each with a preview. Use in my workspace takes the template over after signing in. Only administrators can add their own templates to the gallery.

en.heading: Whiteboard templates
paragraphs: On a whiteboard, Templates inserts a retrospective, a kanban board, a mind map, a SWOT analysis or a flowchart at the current spot.

en.heading: Workflow templates
paragraphs: A new workflow page offers six templates – from “Link sub-pages on the overview” to “Webhook → record”. A short assistant asks for the gaps (page, database, property, person …) and creates the draft. See Workflows.
A database can have as many views as you like. Every view shows the same records with its own layout, filters, sorting and groups.
New view: + next to the view tabs, then choose one of the {{facts.views word}} layouts. View and properties controls which properties are visible and in which order.

A right-click on a view tab opens its menu: Rename, Duplicate, Settings …, Set as default view, Move left, Move right and Delete view (the records are kept; the last view cannot be deleted). With the mouse, tabs can also be reordered by dragging, and a double-click renames them. On touch screens, swiping scrolls the tabs; a long press opens the menu with Move left and Move right.

Default view: the view that appears first when the database is opened – the board instead of the table, for example. Without it, the first view opens. A small star in the tab marks it; it can also be set in the view settings (handy on a phone).

en.heading: Reordering records by dragging
paragraphs: In tables, lists, feeds, boards and galleries, records can be dragged to another place by their handle (⋮⋮); cards on boards and in galleries also by the whole card with the mouse.

– Mouse: dragging starts only after the pointer has moved a few pixels – a simple click still opens the record, or on the handle the Move record dialog. While dragging, the cursor is the closed hand, a slightly lifted copy follows the pointer and a blue line shows where the record lands. Over a group header it lands at the end of that group (and changes the group).
– Scrolling at the edges: near the edge of the table, the board or the window the view scrolls along, sideways as well as up and down.
– Cancel: Esc during the drag puts everything back; nothing is changed.

– Touch screens: hold the handle briefly (about 0.3 seconds) until the record lifts, then drag. A quick swipe over the handle scrolls as usual; a short tap opens Move record. On boards the card handle and the column handle drag right away.

– Keyboard: focus the handle, Space lifts the record, ↑/↓ move it (on boards ←/→ to the next column, Home/End to the start or end), Space or Enter drops it, Esc cancels. Screen readers announce every position. Alt + ↑/↓ still moves it by one place at once.
– A record can also be dragged onto a database in the sidebar this way (see Copy and move records).

en.heading: Table
paragraphs: – Edit cells directly; open records as a page via their title.
– Drag columns by their header onto another column – they land before it (blue line) – and resize them at their edges. On touch screens, hold the header briefly first.
– Choose a calculation below every column.
– Grouped tables fold groups and show summaries per group.

– The title column stays in place while the table scrolls sideways. On a phone it takes at most about 60 % of the table's width, and longer titles are cut short with "…". There the column with the checkbox and drag handle scrolls with the rest. This way the table can be swiped sideways anywhere, including on the title column.

en.heading: Board
paragraphs: The kanban view groups cards into columns, for example by status, select, person or relation.
– Move cards between and within columns by drag and drop: the card lifts, the target column opens a gap, and on release the card settles in. This changes the grouping property.
– New at the foot of a column creates a record right in that group.
– Reorder, hide or collapse columns; "No group" collects records without a value.

– Add group to the right of the columns creates your own status, such as "Waiting for customer": it is saved as a new option of the grouping select property and appears right away as a column of its own.
– Sub-groups also split the board into rows (swimlanes).

– Cards show every property ticked under View → Properties and columns that has a value, in that order; empty properties are left out, and the date sits at the bottom of the card. With more properties the card grows taller.
– With multi-select and relations, a card can appear in several columns; moving it only replaces the respective assignment.

– On touch devices, drag cards by their handle (swiping over a card scrolls) and columns by the ⋮⋮ handle in their header; with the mouse, drag columns by their header. Esc cancels and the card returns to its place.

en.heading: Calendar
paragraphs: Month, week and day view by a date field.
– Week and day show an hourly grid with an all-day row and overlaps placed side by side.
– Move appointments in 15-minute steps, extend or shorten them at their edges.

– Drag whole-day entries (month view and the all-day row) to another day with the mouse, on touch devices by their ⋮⋮ handle; the target day gets a dashed outline, Esc cancels. With the keyboard, Alt + ←/→ moves a focused entry by one day, Alt + ↑/↓ in the month view by one week.
– A click on an hour creates an appointment, All day + an all-day record.
– Every view has its own time zone; without a setting the browser's applies.
– The week start (Monday or Sunday) can be set per view; without a setting it follows the reader's language – Sunday in English (US), Monday otherwise.
– Keyboard: Alt + ↑/↓ moves by 15 minutes, Alt + ←/→ by one day.

en.heading: Subscribe to a calendar
paragraphs: Subscribe in the calendar view creates your personal link for Apple Calendar, Google Calendar or Outlook. It shows the records of this view with its filters – only what you may see – and recurrences as series. The link is secret and shown only once; Create new link invalidates the old one, End subscription switches it off. If you lose access to the database, the link returns nothing anymore.

en.heading: Sync both ways (CalDAV)
paragraphs: In the same dialog, Set up access sets up sync with Apple Calendar, Thunderbird or DAVx⁵ (Android). Events you add, move, rename or delete there land in the database.
– Credentials: you get a server, a username and a password that is shown only once.

– Apple: Set up in Apple Calendar (in the app, in Safari or on a Mac) downloads a configuration profile with the account – install it under Settings → Profile Downloaded. Several calendars at once: Settings → Calendars & issues → Calendars on iPhone, iPad and Mac. By hand: Add account → Other → CalDAV account, type “Manual”.
– Thunderbird and DAVx⁵: they take the calendar address directly.

– Several devices: each profile gets its own access, so a calendar set up on the Mac keeps working when you install the profile on the iPhone. End access or Create new password ends all accesses to this calendar, those of profiles included.
– Permissions: your own rights apply – whoever can only read the database cannot change anything from the calendar. Workflow and automations apply as for any change.
Google Calendar does not support CalDAV accounts; use the calendar sync below for it.

en.heading: Contacts as an address book (CardDAV)
paragraphs: Contacts databases can be subscribed to like calendars – as an address book in Apple Contacts, Thunderbird or DAVx⁵, read-only, with the same kind of access (password shown only once) and a configuration profile for iPhone, iPad and Mac. See Subscribe as an address book.

en.heading: Sync with Google Calendar or Outlook
paragraphs: Calendar sync keeps a view with a date and a calendar in Google Calendar or Microsoft Outlook / 365 in step both ways – personally, with your own account.
– Settings → Calendars & issues → Connect calendar → Connect Google Calendar or Connect Microsoft Outlook / 365. You sign in with the provider and allow access to your calendars.
– In the database, open the calendar icon next to … (Calendar sync), pick the view, the account and the calendar, and Connect.
What is synced:
– Title ↔ event title.

– Date ↔ start and end: a date without a time becomes an all-day event, a date with a time a timed event. The view decides which date properties are start and end; the time zone of the calendar view applies to dates without their own time zone.
– The record's document ↔ description, as plain text. The description ends with a link back to the record.
– New, changed, deleted – both ways. Events deleted in the calendar move their records to the database's trash.
Good to know:
– Flowplan syncs every ten minutes and only fetches changes; Sync now in the dialog syncs right away.
– Conflicts: when both sides change the same event, the later change wins. The audit log records every conflict.
– Permissions: only records you may see and edit go to the calendar and are changed by it. Workflow and automations apply as for any change.
– Range: events from 90 days back to one year ahead. Recurring events from the calendar arrive as single records; a recurring record goes to the calendar with its first date.
– Disconnect under Settings → Calendars & issues ends every sync of that connection. You can also revoke access in your Google or Microsoft account.
– An administrator sets up the providers once, see Configuration.

en.heading: Sprints
paragraphs: Backlog, sprints with goal and period, burndown and velocity – see Projects, tickets and sprints.

en.heading: Timeline
paragraphs: Bars from a start to an end date field, on a scale of week, month, quarter or year.

– Move bars or drag their edges. On touch devices, hold a bar briefly, then drag it; a quick swipe scrolls the timeline. The handles at the edges drag at once. Esc cancels a drag in progress. The calendar icon opens a date dialog, also for unscheduled records.
– Today jumps to the current date; weekends can be highlighted.
– Keyboard: Alt + ←/→ moves by one day, with ⇧ it changes the end, with Ctrl the start.

en.heading: Dependencies (Gantt)
paragraphs: Records can wait for each other – for example "Print" only after "Proofreading":
– In the timeline's bar, choose a relation of the database to itself under Dependencies – or Set up dependencies creates a "Dependencies" property.
– Link by dragging: drag from the round handle at the end of a bar onto another bar – that one then waits for the first. Links that would create a circle are refused.
– Arrows connect the bars; if a record starts before its predecessor ends, the arrow is red. While dragging, the timeline already warns which record would be too early.

– Move successors along: moving a record moves every record that waits for it, directly or indirectly, by the same number of days – in one step. What counts is the side the link is attached to: the record's end for "End → start" and "End → end", its start for "Start → start" and "Start → end".
– Resolve all conflicts moves every record that starts too early behind its predecessor.
– Highlight critical path marks the records and arrows without slack: if one of them is delayed, the end of the whole plan moves.
In embedded views (linked databases), linking by dragging and Resolve all conflicts are not available – open the database itself for that.

en.heading: Gallery
paragraphs: Cards with a preview image and every ticked property that has a value (as on the board). The image comes from the record's content, its cover or a files property, filling the card or fitted in.

en.heading: List
paragraphs: Compact rows with the title and up to three filled-in properties, good for long collections.

en.heading: Feed
paragraphs: Records including their document content one below the other, like a blog or a log. The title, Open record or the comment count opens the full record. More records load in steps of 20.

en.heading: Chart
paragraphs: Configure chart chooses columns, bars, line or donut, the grouping and the calculation – count, sum, average, minimum, maximum. Date values can be summarised by day, week, month or year. A click on a data point shows the records behind it; Export as CSV exports all values.
– Series split every group by another property, side by side or stacked.

– More values put up to four additional calculations next to the main value, such as "sum of costs" next to "sum of revenue" per month. Every value becomes a series of its own with a legend; series and more values cannot be combined.

en.heading: Form
paragraphs: Collects records through a form, also from people without an account. See Forms.

en.heading: Linked databases
paragraphs: In a document, /db shows a view of an existing database. The embed has its own views, filters and sorting; records and their changes still belong to the source. The source name in the header opens the full database.
Reading it requires access to both the document and the source. The embed grants no additional permissions; Remove only deletes the block.
An infinite canvas for brainstorming, processes and workshops: sticky notes, shapes, connectors, pen, frames and tables – together and live.

en.heading: Tools
paragraphs: Tool Key What for
Select V Select, move, scale and rotate elements; drag a rectangle to select several
Hand H Move the canvas (also with space + drag or two fingers)
Sticky note N Coloured notes with text
Text T Free text
Shape R Rectangle, rounded, ellipse, diamond, triangle, hexagon, star, arrow, cloud
Connector L Straight, curved or elbowed; sticks to elements and follows them
Pen P Draw freehand
Eraser X Delete drawn strokes: just move over them
Frame F Group areas – and slides for presenting
Table G A simple table on the canvas
Comment C Pin a comment to a spot
Stamp E A quick reaction (👍 ❤️ ⭐ ✅ ❓ 🔥 💡 🎉) on an element; once more takes it back
Laser pointer K Point without changing anything: everyone sees a red trail that fades shortly

en.heading: How the toolbar is laid out
paragraphs: – On the left are the tools for creating: Select, Move, Sticky note, Text, Shape, Connector, Draw, Frame, Table and Comment. Draw combines pen, eraser and laser pointer: the button shows the one used last, and you switch at the top of its options. The keys in the table still work for every tool.
– + (Insert and more) opens a panel with a search – typing filters, Enter takes the first match:
– Insert: image, images and icons, emoji, stamp, link page (a card linking to a Flowplan page), embed (video, web page or PDF, see below), timeline and import (Excalidraw, draw.io, Mermaid, PlantUML)
– Templates & library: templates, shape library and racks (see Racks and cabling)
– AI, when it is on for you
– Facilitation at the top right: voting, timer, private mode, estimation, bring everyone here and follow me (see Work together). A dot on the button shows that something is running.

– At the bottom left a bar with undo and redo, zoom, the arrows to the previous and next frame, Present (both once there are frames) and … (View and actions: grid, fit, full screen, comments, frames panel, minimap, search, prototype and export).
– On phones the bar sits at the bottom: Select, Move, Sticky note, Text, Shape, Draw and More tools – the same as under +, with a search too. Facilitation is the icon at the top right.
Readers who may only view see Select, Move, the laser pointer and the bottom bar.

en.heading: Style elements
paragraphs: Selected elements show a bar with colour, font size, bold, alignment, line width and style, Bring forward/Send backward, Duplicate (⌘ D) and Delete (Del). Sticky notes and text can also be hidden – like a spoiler in a document, revealed with a click.
A double click edits an element's text. Copy and paste work within and between whiteboards. Italic and Underline apply to the whole text of an element, like Bold.

en.heading: Group
paragraphs: Select several elements and press ⌘ G (or Group in the bar): from then on they behave like one. A click selects the whole group, and it is moved, scaled at the corners, duplicated, copied, locked and deleted together. Groups can be combined into larger groups.

– A double click on a grouped element enters the group: a dashed outline shows it, and clicks now select single elements inside (in nested groups, the next level). Esc or a click elsewhere leaves the group.
– ⇧ ⌘ G or Ungroup dissolves the outermost group of the selection.
– Copies of a group are a new group of their own. Like every change, grouping is shared live and can be undone with ⌘ Z.

en.heading: Lists, links and tags
paragraphs: Sticky notes, shapes and texts know a few formats right in the text:
You write Result
- item Bulleted list (the Bulleted list and Numbered list buttons in the bar set it for the marked lines)
1. item Numbered list; Enter continues the list, an empty line ends it
bold, italic, underline Emphasise single words – while typing with ⌘ B, ⌘ I, ⌘ U
text Link – Insert a link into the text in the bar puts it around the marked text

Links may only point to https://, http:// and mailto: or to an element of the same board (see below); other addresses stay plain text. Web links open in a new tab. In addition, every element can carry a link of its own (chain icon in the bar); a small icon at its corner leads there.
Tags on sticky notes show as coloured chips along the bottom edge – a tag always has the same colour. In the board search, Only notes tagged highlights all notes with that tag and dims the rest.

en.heading: Links to frames and elements
paragraphs: Copy link to this element (in the bar of a selected element or in the frames panel) copies an address like …/#page=…&item=…. Whoever opens it sees the board zoomed to the element and selected – provided they may read the board.
Inside the board, links to elements fly there: in an element's link field or in the text as To the goal. If the element is gone, a note says so.

en.heading: Mind maps
paragraphs: Select a sticky note, shape or text and press Tab: a connected branch appears on the right, ready to be labelled. Tab on the new branch branches further, ⌥ Enter adds a sibling. The mind map arranges itself: branches sit to the right of their parent, evenly spaced and centred. Arrange mind map in an element's bar rearranges the whole tree. Typing on a selected sticky note starts writing right away.

en.heading: Diagrams: shape libraries
paragraphs: Shape library under + (or More shapes … in the shape menu) opens a searchable side panel – a sheet from the bottom on phones. A click or Enter puts the shape in the middle of the view, or drag it where you want it; arrow keys move between the shapes. Search works in English and German (“decision”, “Raute”, “gateway” …).
Library Shapes

Flowchart Process, decision, start/end, data, document(s), predefined process, manual input and operation, database, preparation, delay, display, connector, off-page connector, internal storage, merge, loop limit, annotation
BPMN Start, intermediate, end, timer and message events, task, subprocess, user and service task, exclusive, parallel and inclusive gateway, data object, data store, pool, lane, group
UML Class (with compartments), interface, enumeration, actor, use case, component, package, note, lifelines, activation, initial and final node, state, decision, fork, node, combined fragment
ER diagram Entity with attribute rows, weak entity, relationship, (key, multivalued) attribute
Org chart Person, team, open position
Network Server, database server, internet, firewall, router, switch, laptop, workstation, smartphone, tablet, user, Wi-Fi, printer, web
Cloud architecture Compute, object storage, managed database, queue, function, CDN, load balancer, container, API gateway, cache, monitoring, secrets, virtual network, events

Wireframes Browser, smartphone and tablet frames, dialog, buttons, input and search field, checkbox, radio button, toggle, dropdown, tabs, navigation bar, card, list, image and icon placeholders, avatar, text, slider, progress bar

All shapes are vector graphics, take fill, line colour and width from the bar, can be connected and look the same in the SVG, PNG and Markdown exports. A double click edits the text; in classes and entities a line -- separates the compartments (name, attributes, methods). The cloud icons are neutral icons drawn for Flowplan – no logos or icon sets of AWS, Azure or Google Cloud.

Line ends: for selected connectors you choose the start and end separately: arrow, open arrow, triangle (inheritance), diamond (aggregation), filled diamond (composition), circle, dot, cross and the crow's-foot ends for ER diagrams (one, exactly one, zero or one, many, one or many, zero or many).

en.heading: Arrange automatically
paragraphs: Select several connected shapes → Arrange automatically → Top to bottom or Left to right. Flowplan arranges the diagram in layers (with as few crossings as it can), the top left corner stays where it was and connectors stay attached. One ⌘ Z undoes it all at once. Locked elements stay put.

en.heading: Import Mermaid and PlantUML
paragraphs: Simply paste Mermaid or PlantUML text onto the board (⌘ V), drop a .mmd or .puml file on it or choose Import Mermaid/PlantUML … under +. It becomes editable shapes and connectors, laid out automatically:
– Mermaid: flowchart/graph (with shapes, labels, subgraphs as frames), sequenceDiagram, classDiagram, erDiagram (with crow's feet), stateDiagram, mindmap.
– PlantUML: activity diagrams (start, :action;, if/else, while, fork …), sequence, class, use case and component diagrams and @startmindmap.

Everything is read on your device – no PlantUML server, no Java. The dialog shows beforehand what was detected. Lines Flowplan does not understand are skipped and listed with their line numbers; pure styling (style, skinparam, themes) is ignored silently. Limits: 100,000 characters, 400 shapes, 800 connectors, 40 participants in a sequence diagram, files up to 200 KB.
Copy as Mermaid (in the export menu) copies the selected shapes with their connectors – or the whole board – to the clipboard as a Mermaid flowchart, for example for a Mermaid diagram in a document.

en.heading: Wireframes and clickable prototypes
paragraphs: Sketch screens with the wireframe shapes, ideally one frame per screen (with the smartphone frame inside, for example). Select an element – a button, a shape, a sticky note – and set On click → frame in the bar, or On click → back. A small arrow badge on the element shows the link.

Play prototype (shown once there are frames) shows the selected frame – or the first one – full screen. Clicks on linked elements change the screen; a click elsewhere or the Show clickable areas button briefly highlights everything clickable. Back (←), Restart (Home) and Esc to close. Linked elements can be reached with the keyboard too (Tab, Enter).
When copying, duplicating and pasting, links point to the frames copied along; archives and exports keep them.

en.heading: Timelines (roadmaps)
paragraphs: Timeline under + (or in the shape library under “Planning”) adds a roadmap with a time scale, lanes and bars. While the timeline is selected, move bars right on the board – into another lane, too – and drag their ends to change the start or end. A red line marks today.

A double click or Edit timeline opens the settings: title, scale (weeks, months, quarters), period (up to about three years), today marker, lanes and bars with title, lane, dates and colour (up to 40 lanes and 400 bars).

As the source you can choose a database instead of own bars: records with a date become bars (start, optional end), a select property provides the lanes. The timeline is live: it shows the current state, and anyone who may edit the records moves a record's dates by moving its bar (a time of day is kept). Everyone sees only the records they may read in the database; the records are not stored in the board and therefore do not appear in the board's exports or search.

en.heading: Racks and cabling
paragraphs: On a whiteboard you plan server racks: racks with their rack units (U), devices in them, ports on the devices and cables from port to port. Racks and devices are elements like sticky notes and shapes – combine them freely with notes, text, frames and network diagrams from the shape library. Working together, undo, comments, presenting and the export as SVG, PNG or PDF work as for every other element.

en.heading: Adding racks
paragraphs: Racks under + opens the device library (on phones under More tools, as a sheet). At the top you add a Rack 42U, Rack 24U or a Wall cabinet 12U – with a click next to the last rack, or by dragging it to a spot. Several racks stand side by side this way.

A selected rack shows its details on the right: name, location, height in U (1–60), width (10″, 19″ or 23″), View front or rear, Max. power (W) and Max. weight (kg), plus the units used, the total power and weight and the list of devices. You also change the height with the handles at the top and bottom of the rack. Front/Rear in the bar above the rack turns it around.

en.heading: Mounting devices
paragraphs: The library contains servers (1, 2 and 4U), storage/NAS, switches (24 and 48 ports, 24 × SFP+, each with SFP uplinks and console), patch panels (24 and 48 ports, fibre with 24 × LC), router, firewall, UPS, PDU (1U and vertical as 0U), blanking panels, cable managers and shelves – each with height, ports, power and weight.
– Drag a device to a spot: over a rack it snaps to whole units, next to it it lies freely on the board.

– Click it (or press Enter in the search field) to put it into the selected rack – or the rack in the middle of the view – at the highest free place. When the rack is full, the device lies next to it.

– Move mounted devices with the mouse to other units or another rack; with ↑/↓ by one unit (⇧: five units), ⌥ ↑/↓ changes the height. The handles at the top and bottom change the height in whole units too.
– Duplicate (⌘ D) puts the copy at the next free place of the same rack. Deleting a rack deletes its devices.
– When two devices overlap or one sticks out of the rack, both are hatched red and marked with !; the rack counts them in its details.

Devices can have half depth (mounted at the front or the rear): a front and a rear device then share the same units. In the other view they only show as a dashed outline. Vertical PDUs are mounted as 0U left/right in the side channel.

A device's details: name, kind, roles, manufacturer, model, serial number, host name, IP addresses, MAC address, height, position (lowest U), mounting, depth, colour, power (W), weight (kg), notes – for PDUs and UPSs also Capacity (W) with the current load. Take out of the rack puts it next to the rack.
– Roles are free tags with suggestions such as Docker host, hypervisor, bare metal, NAS, router or firewall.

– IP addresses takes one or more IPv4 or IPv6 addresses (also with /24), separated by commas, spaces or line breaks. Invalid entries are not saved and are pointed out when you leave the field. The MAC address is always stored as aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, whether you type it with -, . or no separators.
– Network ports (RJ45, SFP/QSFP) also have their own MAC and IP address – every network card has its own.

– Hovering over a device for a moment shows a card with everything at a glance: name, kind, roles, host name, IP and MAC addresses (each with a copy button), manufacturer and model, height and position, power, used ports and the start of the notes. On a phone or tablet a long press opens the card, with the keyboard I for the selected device; Esc closes it.

– Search, Markdown and CSV export and the NetBox import include host name, addresses and roles (from NetBox: the primary IP with its DNS name, MAC and IP of the interfaces, role and tags). Save as own device leaves out host name and addresses.
Save as own device stores the device with its ports and values in the workspace's library (section Own devices). The person who saved it and owners of the workspace can delete it.

en.heading: Ports
paragraphs: Every device has ports with name, type (RJ45, SFP, SFP+, SFP28, QSFP+, QSFP28, LC, SC, MPO, console, USB, C13, C14, C19, C20, Schuko, DC), side (front or rear), label and VLAN. The ports of the side the rack shows are drawn; connected ports take the colour of their cable, a tooltip shows name, type and label. In the details you change or remove ports and add several at once with Add ports (count, type, side, prefix such as Gi1/0/). Clicking a port on the board shows it in the details.

en.heading: Cables
paragraphs: Cables are connectors whose ends sit on ports: with the connector tool (L) you drag from one port to another – also between two racks. A line that starts or ends on a port becomes a cable; its type follows the ports (power, console, fibre, DAC or Cat6a). Without drawing, use a device's details: Connect … at the port, then choose the device and a free port.

Cables run like in a tidy rack: from the port to the edge of its device, through the side channel and, between racks, over the top of the racks; every cable has its own lane. When two ports face each other – on the lower edge of the upper device and the upper edge of the lower one, or on the same edge of one device – and no other device is in between, the cable goes straight across instead of through the channel. Colour and stroke follow the type (e.g. OM3 aqua, OM4 violet, OS2 yellow, power thick, DAC dashed); a colour of its own takes precedence. Hovering or selecting a cable highlights both ends. Show cables in the view menu hides and shows all cables (the choice applies in this browser).

A cable's details: its two ends (a click jumps to the device and port), cable type (Cat5e, Cat6, Cat6a, Cat7, Cat8, OM3, OM4, OM5, OS2, DAC, AOC, power, console, other), colour, label, length in metres, VLAN and notes. If more than one cable is plugged into a port, the details point it out.

en.heading: Power and weight
paragraphs: The power and weight of the devices add up per rack (in the rack's header and details). Power cables from a PDU or UPS to a device make up the PDU's load: a device with two power supplies on two PDUs shares its power between both, a PDU on a UPS passes its whole load on to the UPS. When a rack exceeds its Max. power or Max. weight, or a PDU/UPS its capacity, a warning shows in the rack's header, on the device and in the details.

en.heading: Ports and cables at a glance
paragraphs: Ports & cables (in the view menu and the device library) shows all ports of the board as a table – rack, device, port, type, connected to, cable, VLAN – and all cables with label, type, ends, length and VLAN. Filter by text, category (network, fibre, power) and assignment (connected, free), sort by clicking the column headers; clicking a row shows the device or cable on the board. Export as CSV downloads the filtered list, Print labels prints one label per cable end (label, this end, the other end, type, length, VLAN).

en.heading: Import and export
paragraphs: – Export JSON (device library) saves the racks with devices, ports and cables – the selected ones or all – as a file; Import JSON places them on a board. This way you move racks to other boards and workspaces.

– From NetBox … fetches racks from NetBox: enter the NetBox address, an API token (read-only is enough) and optionally a site (slug) and rack names. Flowplan queries racks, devices, device types (height, depth, weight), interfaces, front and rear ports, console and power ports and cables once and places them on the board (up to 20 racks). The address and token are used for this request only and are not stored on the server; Remember the address and token in this browser keeps them in your browser only. NetBox has to be reachable at a public HTTPS address – for a NetBox in the internal network see NETBOX_ALLOW_PRIVATE in the configuration.

– The board's SVG, PNG and PDF export shows the racks as they stand on the board. The Markdown export adds a section Racks and cabling to the board's SVG picture, with the devices per rack, the port assignments and the cable list as tables.

The AI and MCP (read_page) read a board's racks, devices, ports and cables as text. On phones you view and edit racks: tapping selects a device, Details in the bar opens the details as a sheet, and the device library is under More tools.

en.heading: Align, stack and sort
paragraphs: – When moving, edges and centres snap to other elements; orange guides show to which. ⌥ while dragging turns snapping off.
– Snap to grid (grid button at the bottom) snaps elements without neighbours to the 24-point grid.
– Select several elements → Arrange: align left, centre, right, top, middle or bottom, distribute evenly or stack as a row or column.
– For workshops: Group by colour, Group by person (with headings), Sort by votes or Arrange as a grid.

en.heading: Pen and shape recognition
paragraphs: With a tablet pen (such as an Apple Pencil) the stroke width follows the pressure. Choose the colour in the pen menu; with Recognise shapes, drawn lines, rectangles, circles, triangles and diamonds turn into clean shapes (⌥ on release keeps the stroke).

Once you have drawn with a pen on a device, only the pen draws: fingers move and zoom the board, a resting hand leaves no strokes. A hand resting on the screen while the pen draws neither cuts nor moves the stroke. Draw with the pen only in the pen menu switches this off – fingers then draw too, except the hand holding the pen: a touch while the pen draws or hovers, or within a moment after lifting it, moves the board instead. A pen touching down lightly does not start the stroke thick, and the width follows the pressure smoothly. Writing with Scribble in an open text on the board may run past its edges; the text stays open. A hovering Apple Pencil (iPad Pro, iPad Air M2 and later) shows where the stroke starts; the eraser end of a pen erases like the Eraser. In the iPad app, double-tapping or squeezing the Apple Pencil switches to the eraser and back, to the previous tool or to the pen, as set on the iPad. The same applies when marking up images in documents.

en.heading: Images, icons and records
paragraphs: – Images and icons (under +) searches freely licensed images on Openverse; chosen images are uploaded to the server, and the credit shows as a tooltip on the image. There is also the icon library in ten colours.

– Crop (in the bar of an image): choose the part with the mouse, a finger or the arrow keys (⇧ resizes). The image itself stays unchanged – Show the whole image undoes the crop at any time, and exports show the cropped part too.

– GIFs: when the instance has a key for GIPHY or Tenor (see Configuration), Images and icons gets a GIFs tab. The search runs through the server; a chosen GIF is stored on the server like the Openverse images (up to 8 MB), and afterwards the board loads nothing from the provider. Without a key the tab is hidden.
– Link page → Record from "…" places a database record as a card. The card shows the title and up to three properties and stays up to date when the record changes; a double click opens it.
Cards of linked documents that are tall enough show the first lines of the page as a small preview.

en.heading: Embed videos, web pages and PDFs
paragraphs: Embed under + (on phones under More tools) takes a link:

– Videos and web pages from YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Spotify, Figma and CodePen – the same list as for embeds in documents. Other addresses are refused. The board first shows only a preview with the provider; the content loads only after a click on Load, in an isolated frame (sandbox), and Close embed unloads it again. YouTube runs through youtube-nocookie.com.

– PDFs: Upload PDF … or drag a PDF file onto the board. The file is stored in the page and counts towards the storage quota; the board shows one page as a preview, with arrows to page through. A double click opens the PDF viewer.
Exports show a card with the provider and link instead of the player.

en.heading: Sticky notes as database records
paragraphs: Turn a brainstorm into a backlog: select notes → As records in database … (database icon) in the bar. Without a selection the dialog takes the notes in view, with a selected frame the notes in it. This works without any AI.
– Choose the target database – you are offered databases you may add records to.

– Mapping: the note's first line becomes the title, further lines the record's content. Optionally the colour becomes a select property (one option per note colour; options with the same name such as "Yellow" or "Red" are preselected) and the note's author a person property.

– Replace with cards swaps the notes for record cards in the same place – connectors then attach to the card. Keep and link leaves the notes and places the cards next to them, joined by a dashed line.

The cards are live: when someone changes the record in the database, the board shows it at once. Others see the new cards like any edit; one ⌘ Z takes the change to the board back in one step (the records stay in the database).
– At most 500 notes at once; the server creates them in batches of 100, progress shows how far it got, Cancel stops – whatever was created already goes onto the board.
– Trying again after an error creates nothing twice.
– Values are checked like every edit: locked properties, existing options, only members as people.

– Split with AI (when AI is available to you): the AI reads the notes' text and fills further properties – such as assignee, due date or priority. A preview first shows the values per note, anything that does not fit is listed with the reason; records are only created after that.
– In the API the command is whiteboard.toRecords.

en.heading: AI on the whiteboard
paragraphs: When AI is on for you, AI under + (on phones under More tools) opens these features. Without AI the button is missing and everything else works as usual; on boards the AI may not read, the entries are greyed out with the reason.

– Group by theme (AI) – also in the Arrange menu once two notes are selected: the AI finds themes in the selected notes (without a selection: those in view) and arranges them in labelled columns, like Group by colour. Notes without text and those that fit nowhere go under "Other".

– Summarise as a page – reads the board (or the selection or selected frame) and creates a page next to it: summary, themes, Decisions, Open questions and Action items, with a link back to the board. With Take over action items they become real tasks with person and due date where the board names them – they appear in My tasks. Frames become sections; the AI reads large boards in parts, and the page says what was left out beyond the limit of 2,000 elements.

– Create with AI … – a mind map or a flowchart from a description, such as "how a holiday request is approved". It appears in the middle of the view (or to the right of it when something is already there) as normal shapes and connectors; the mind map uses the layout of Arrange mind map. At most 60 and 40 nodes respectively.

Every action shows its progress and can be cancelled; an error shows in the dialog with Try again. The result is an ordinary change to the board: everyone sees it live, and one ⌘ Z takes it all back. Hidden notes stay hidden from the AI; it reads linked pages and records only when it may read them.

en.heading: Navigate
paragraphs: – Zoom with ⌘ + scroll wheel, trackpad gestures or the buttons in the bar at the bottom left.
– Show everything (⇧ 1) fits the view to all elements, ⇧ 2 to the selection – with a smooth camera move that any input stops at once.
– Undo ⌘ Z, redo ⇧ ⌘ Z.

– Minimap (in the … menu of the bottom bar, View and actions): a small overview of all elements with the visible part. Click or drag to go there; with the focus on the minimap the arrow keys move the view. The browser remembers whether it is open.

– Search the board (⌘ F on the board, or in the … menu at the bottom): searches sticky notes, shapes, texts, tables, frames, comments, embeds and page and record cards. Enter and ⇧ Enter (or the arrows) jump to the next or previous match, which is highlighted; Esc closes the search.

en.heading: Work together
paragraphs: – Live cursors: you see the others' pointers with names in real time, as in Miro. Someone working outside your viewport appears as a marker at the edge; a click on it jumps there.
– Changes appear for everyone within seconds, also after a time without a connection.

– A timer for workshop phases, visible to everyone. If you like, background music plays along (Calm, Focus or Lo-fi): choose it in the timer window under Music while the timer runs. It starts and stops with the timer for everyone; volume and mute are up to each person via the speaker icon in the timer. If the browser blocks sound because nothing on the page has been clicked yet, Sound on appears. The music is generated in the browser, without audio files or external services.

– Voting: set the votes per person and start; everyone puts dots on elements, and the result shows the ranking. Anonymous voting shows everyone only their own votes until the vote ends – so nobody influences the others.

– Follow me (under Facilitation): everyone else sees your viewport and follows you as you pan and zoom. Whoever pans or zooms themselves stops following and can return with Follow. End lifts it for everyone.
– Comments on spots of the canvas, with replies and mentions.

– Private mode (crossed-out eye icon) for silent brainstorming: anyone who may edit the whiteboard starts it for the whole whiteboard or just one frame. While it runs, everyone sees only their own new notes and elements in that area (outlined, “only you”); of the others' contributions only the number shows, as hidden placeholders – no text, no names. Reveal shows all contributions to everyone at once and ends the mode; anyone with edit rights can do this, even if the facilitator has left. Private content is stored separately on the server and, until it is revealed, reaches neither the others' browsers nor search, exports, previews, the API or AI features. Reloading, a second tab or joining later are no problem; changes made without a connection are sent afterwards.

– Estimate (planning poker): select notes or record cards – or a frame, then everything in it – and choose Estimate. Decks: Fibonacci (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, ?, ☕), T-shirt sizes (XS–XL) or your own values. Everyone picks a card hidden; you only see who has already estimated. Reveal cards shows the distribution, average, median and whether there is a consensus. Apply result writes the value onto the note as a label – for record cards into a number, select or text property of the record (with the usual permissions). Then Next element or Estimate again.

– Bring everyone here: everyone else jumps once to your current view – unlike “Follow me”, they move freely again afterwards. With a frame selected, the magnet icon brings everyone to this frame. The others see a notice (“Mara brought everyone here”) and return to where they were with Back.

en.heading: Frames panel
paragraphs: Frames (in the … menu of the bottom bar, View and actions) lists all frames with a small preview – on phones as a sheet from the bottom.
– A click on the preview flies to the frame; the name can be renamed right there.
– Dragging the grip (or ⌥ + arrow keys) changes the order – it is the order of the presentation and is saved with the board. Until someone sorts, reading order applies (top to bottom, left to right).
– Hide from the presentation (eye icon) skips a frame when presenting without deleting it.
– Speaker notes per frame, shown only in the presentation.
– Also: Copy link to this element, Export frame and Present from here.

en.heading: Present
paragraphs: As soon as there are frames, Present appears in the bar at the bottom left; the arrows next to it also go to the previous or next frame without presenting. The frames are shown one after another in the order of the frames panel, filling the screen; hidden frames are left out, and everything outside the current frame fades away. Arrow keys or the buttons page through, End presentation or Esc closes.
– Speaker notes shows the notes of the frame.
– Presenter view opens the same second window as for documents: the current and the next slide, the notes and the elapsed time. Both windows stay in step – you can move on in either of them.

en.heading: Templates
paragraphs: Templates opens a searchable gallery with previews, sorted by category:
Category Templates
Retrospectives Retrospective, 4L retrospective, starfish retrospective
Planning Kanban, user story map, sprint planning, project timeline, Eisenhower matrix, impact/effort matrix
Strategy OKRs, SWOT analysis, lean canvas, business model canvas, customer journey
Ideas Empathy map, brainstorm, mind map
Diagrams Flowchart, decision tree, org chart
Meetings Meeting agenda, icebreaker
A template lands in the middle of the view and is ordinary board content afterwards.

Own templates: Save as template turns the whole board or the selection into a template – For the workspace or Only for me. Comments, votes and stamps stay out; images and PDFs remain files of the workspace. Own templates are in the Own templates tab; the person who saved one and owners can delete it. At most 500 templates per workspace.

en.heading: Import Excalidraw and draw.io
paragraphs: Use Import … under + – or drop the file onto the board – to bring in drawings from:
– Excalidraw (.excalidraw),
– draw.io / diagrams.net (.drawio, .xml, also compressed and with several pages) and draw.io SVG exports with an embedded diagram.

Shapes, texts, arrows with their connections and labels, freehand strokes, frames, colours, stroke widths, dashes and rotations become whiteboard items. Several draw.io pages are placed side by side, each in a frame of its own. What Flowplan doesn't know (stencils, embeds, external images) becomes a note with its text. Embedded pictures (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) are stored as files of the page and count towards the storage quota.
– Dropping such a file into a document creates a new whiteboard below it and embeds it right away.
– In the ZIP import (see Import) .excalidraw and .drawio files become whiteboard pages.
– Limits: 20 MB per file (30 MB unpacked), 3,000 elements, 50 pages. Flowplan fetches nothing from the internet during import; texts are taken over as plain text.

en.heading: Embed and export
paragraphs: – With /board in a document, a whiteboard becomes part of a page; the button at the top right opens it large.
– Export as PNG or Export as SVG saves the whiteboard as an image.

– Export … (PNG, SVG, PDF) opens the export dialog: what (Whole board, Selection or a single frame), the format and, for PNG, the Resolution 1×, 2× or 4×. As a PDF the board comes Everything on one page or with One page per frame in presentation order (hidden frames left out). The export is made in the browser; the server sees nothing of it.
– In the Markdown export, every whiteboard comes along as an SVG automatically.
– The text on the board is searchable and appears in exports.
– Copy as Mermaid takes shapes and connectors along as a Mermaid flowchart (see above).
Every node a workflow knows – with its type (as it appears in the JSON and the API), its ports and the values later nodes use as placeholders.
This list is generated from Flowplan's node catalogue; GET /api/workflows/catalog returns every node's settings as JSON Schema.

en.heading: Triggers
paragraphs: Node Type What it does Ports Outputs
New record ⚡ trigger.record.created A record is created in a database. out record, actor, via
Record changed ⚡ trigger.record.changed Properties of a record change. out record, before, changed, actor
Record done ⚡ trigger.record.done A record becomes done. out record, actor
Date reached trigger.record.date A date of a record is reached or overdue. out record, date
Form answer ⚡ trigger.form.submitted Someone submits a database's form. out record, answers, respondent
Schedule trigger.schedule Daily, weekly or monthly at a time. out slot
New page trigger.page.created A page is created. out page, actor
Page changed trigger.page.changed A page's title or content changes (2 minutes after the last change). out page, actor, changes
Page moved trigger.page.moved A page gets a new parent or space. out page, from, to, actor
Tag added trigger.page.tagged A page gets a tag. out page, tag, actor
New comment trigger.comment.created Someone comments on a page or record. out comment, page, record, actor
Mention trigger.mention Someone is mentioned in a page, record or comment. out page, record, mentioned, actor
Start manually trigger.manual Starts with “Run”, the API or a button. out inputs, startedBy, source
Inbound webhook trigger.webhook Another service calls the workflow’s address. out body, query, headers, receivedAt
E-mail received trigger.mail.received An e-mail arrives at an address that goes to this workflow. out mail, authenticated
New journal day trigger.journal.day A day’s page is created in a journal. out day, date, journal

en.heading: Logic
paragraphs: Node Type What it does Ports Outputs
If ⚡ logic.if Branches on conditions. true, false matched
Set values ⚡ logic.set Named values for later nodes. out –
Stop ⚡ logic.stop Ends the run as succeeded or failed. – –
Switch ⚡ logic.switch Branches on the first matching case. case:…, default case
For each logic.foreach Runs the following nodes for every item of a list. item, done count, results
Wait logic.wait Waits for a duration, until a point in time or until the next time of day. out waitedUntil
Approval logic.approval Waits until a person approves or rejects. approved, rejected, timeout decidedBy, comment, decidedAt

en.heading: Records
paragraphs: Node Type What it does Ports Outputs
Create record action.record.create Creates a record in a database. out record
Update record ⚡ action.record.update Changes properties of a record. out record, before
Find records action.record.find Finds records by conditions. out records, first, count
Apply template ⚡ action.record.template Applies a record template to a record. out record

en.heading: Pages
paragraphs: Node Type What it does Ports Outputs
Create page action.page.create Creates a page below a parent page. out page
Append to page action.page.append Adds blocks at the end, the start or below a heading. out page, appended
Tag page action.page.tag Adds tags to a page or removes them. out page
Move page action.page.move Moves a page below a new parent. out page

en.heading: Notify
paragraphs: Node Type What it does Ports Outputs
Notify person ⚡ notify.person A notification in the app, by push, email or chat app. out notified
Send e-mail notify.email Sends an e-mail to people or addresses. out sent
Chat message notify.chat Posts to a chat webhook of the workspace (Slack, Matrix, Teams, Discord). out sent

en.heading: AI
paragraphs: Node Type What it does Ports Outputs
AI: Summarize ai.summarize Summarizes a text. out summary
AI: Classify ai.classify Puts a text into one of the categories. out, unclear category, categories, confidence
AI: Extract fields ai.extract Reads named values from a text. out fields, missing
AI: Custom prompt ai.prompt A prompt of your own, answered as text or JSON. out text, json

en.heading: HTTP
paragraphs: Node Type What it does Ports Outputs
HTTP request http.request Calls an HTTPS address (fixed host). out status, headers, body, json
⚡ – can run in the immediate part: right when a record is saved, in the same change.
Every node can On error retry (up to 5 times), end the run, continue through the error port or skip the error.

A workflow is a flow of nodes on a canvas: a trigger (a new page, a changed record, a schedule, an e-mail …), then logic and actions – change records and pages, notify people, ask the AI, call other services. No code at all.

Workflows are a page type of their own. They run in the background on the server, step by step, survive restarts, retry on errors and can wait days for a date or an approval. A workflow can never do more than the person who activated it.

en.heading: First steps: the template from the issue
paragraphs: This links every new sub-page of an overview page there automatically – with a one-sentence description:
– In the sidebar choose + → Workflow and give it a title.
– On the empty canvas, pick the template Link sub-pages on the overview.
– The short assistant asks for the overview page and whether a short description with AI comes along. Create the draft.
– Dry run (nothing changes) or Test run (for real, as you) – the result shows at every node.
– Activate. From now on every new sub-page lands on the overview as “• link – short text”, never twice.

en.heading: How a workflow starts
paragraphs: A new workflow page offers four ways:
– Start blank – choose the trigger and build it yourself.
– Templates – six ready flows with gaps an assistant asks for (page, database, property, person, chat webhook, e-mail address):
Template What it does
Link sub-pages on the overview New page directly below X → optional AI short description → append “• link – short text” to X, never twice
Reminder before the due date Two days before the date at 9:00 → only if not done → remind the people responsible by push
Form → AI category → assignment Form answer → the AI picks a category → per category make someone responsible and notify them; unclear → team lead
Weekly report Fridays 15:00 → find records completed this week → the AI summarises → create a report page → optionally post to the chat
Inbound e-mail → ticket E-mail to the workflow's address → the AI reads title, description, urgency → create a record → confirm to the sender
Webhook → record Another service calls the workflow's address → create a record
– Draft with AI – one sentence is enough, see AI builder.
– Import from a file – an exported workflow file, see Export and import.
Whatever you choose lands on the canvas as a draft – Undo takes it away again. A workflow never becomes active by itself.

en.heading: The canvas
paragraphs: – Node list on the left: triggers, logic, records, pages, notify, AI, HTTP – with a search. Drag, or click (appends after the selected node).
– Nodes show an icon, a label and a one-line summary; a dot marks errors or warnings of the check. The ⚡ means: runs right away when the record is saved (the “immediate part”).
– Side panel on the right: the settings of the selected node, “On error”, a note and the input and output of the last test.
– List shows the same flow as an outline – fully usable with the keyboard. Tidy up arranges the nodes from left to right.
– Several people edit the same draft at the same time; what runs only changes with Activate.

en.heading: Placeholders and filters
paragraphs: In every text field, {} (or typing {{) inserts values of earlier nodes, such as {{New page.Title}} or {{Trigger.Record.Fields.Status}}. Filters follow a :
Filter Example Result
truncate {{AI.summary \ truncate: 140}} at most 140 characters
date {{$today \ date: "yyyy-MM-dd"}} a date in your own form
add_days {{$today \ add_days: 3}} three days later
default {{Webhook.body.title \ default: "Untitled"}} a stand-in for empty values
required {{Webhook.body.title \ required}} an error when empty
join, first, last, count {{Find.records \ join: ", "}} lists to text
upper, lower, trim, replace, number, plain, json reshape text
Built-in values: $today, $now, $run, $workflow, $runner, and inside “For each” $item and $index. Placeholder values are always inserted as text, never as HTML.

en.heading: Testing
paragraphs: – Dry run: writing nodes only report what they would do (“would create record …”); e-mail, chat and push are not sent, waits are skipped, approvals count as approved or rejected (your choice). AI nodes run and cost tokens.
– Test run: acts for real – as you, not as the person the workflow runs as.
– Trigger data: example, the last real event, a record or page to pick, or your own values.
Tests always use the draft. The result shows as a status ring at every node; a click shows input and output.

en.heading: Activate, pause, “runs as”
paragraphs: Activate checks the draft (missing settings, deleted databases, pages without access …) and shows what the workflow will do and who it runs as: the person who activates it. It only sees and changes what this person may. If they lose their rights, the workflow pauses and says so.
Pause holds open runs (or cancels them, if you choose); after activating they continue on their version. After ten failures in a row, or when half of the recent runs fail, a workflow pauses itself.

en.heading: Runs and versions
paragraphs: The Runs tab lists every run with status, duration and version; filter by failed, waiting, open and tests, search for errors. A run opens the canvas in its version with the timeline of its steps (attempts, waits, errors). Retry from the failed node and Cancel are there.
Inputs and outputs of a run are only shown to the person it ran as; colleagues see status and errors and debug with a test run of their own.
Versions shows activated versions and draft states in one timeline, compares two of them and restores one as the draft.

en.heading: AI builder
paragraphs: Draft with AI (on the empty canvas or in the bar at the top) builds a draft from one sentence – for example: “When a page is created below Docker in the wiki, add it with a one-sentence description to the overview.”
– The AI only sees names of databases, properties, options, spaces and pages you may see and that are open to the AI – no contents.
– Its proposal is checked against the node catalogue: unknown nodes are left out, unknown pages or properties stay empty and are marked.
– You see the proposal first; Use as draft inserts it as one change. Activating is up to you.
– It counts against your personal AI allowance, not the workflow's budget. See AI.

en.heading: Workflow button on pages
paragraphs: /Workflow button puts a button into a document that starts a workflow with the trigger Start manually. If the trigger has input fields, the button shows a small form. After the click it says Started – editors of the workflow see the way to the runs.

The trigger decides who may press it: by default the editors of the workflow, switchable to all members who see the page with the button. Guests and share links never see the button. The run always runs as the workflow's runner; the person who clicked is recorded as “Started by”.

en.heading: Export and import
paragraphs: Export as JSON (the arrow at the top right) saves the flow as .flowplan-workflow.json: editors get the draft, readers the active version. The file names the pages, databases (with their properties) and people it uses, with their titles. Credentials, webhook addresses and runs are never included – credentials only with name, kind and host, so you can link them again.

Import from a file matches references in the workspace: same ID, otherwise same title (pages, databases), same name (people, properties). What stays open, the assistant asks for, or it stays empty. An import is always a draft.

Content archives and the instance move take workflows along with their draft and versions, without runs and secrets. Active workflows arrive paused, so nothing starts unexpectedly on the new instance.

en.heading: Phone and tablet
paragraphs: – Phone: status with an on/off switch, the flow as a list, runs and approvals. Editing happens on a tablet or computer.
– Approvals: the notification opens the workflow page on the Approvals tab – message, comment, Reject or Approve.

– Approvals in the app: in the iPhone and Android app, the notification carries Approve and Reject buttons, as long as notifications show their text on the lock screen. Approve asks for Face ID, Touch ID or a fingerprint first – without biometrics the Approvals tab opens instead. Reject needs no biometrics, but the phone has to be unlocked. The device must be signed in and active within the last 14 days; on Android the very first Approve opens the tab once, because that is when the key is created.
– Tablet: the full editor; connecting also works by tapping an output, then the target.

en.heading: Keyboard
paragraphs: Key Action
Tab / Shift+Tab between nodes
Arrow keys (further with Shift) move the selected node
Enter / Esc open / close the panel
A append a node
C connect to …
Delete delete
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo / redo
Ctrl+D duplicate
L list ↔ canvas
F fit the view

en.heading: Limits
paragraphs: Limit Default
Runs per minute and workflow 60
Runs per minute and workspace 600
Steps per run 200
Workflows triggering each other (cascade) 5 levels
Items per “For each” 100
AI tokens per workflow and day 100,000
E-mails per workflow and day 100
Keeping runs 30 days
Active workflows per workspace 100
Admins change them in the administration or with an environment variable. Editors can set lower values per workflow.

en.heading: API, MCP and SDKs
paragraphs: Workflows can be created, checked, tested, activated (with a write token) and started through the REST API; the SDKs come with ready methods. Through MCP, an AI assistant reads workflows and runs, saves drafts, tests and starts them – it cannot activate them or decide approvals.

en.heading: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs: Do workflows replace the automations of databases? No. The simple rules stay in the form under … → Automations and run on the same engine. Every rule can be extended into a workflow with Open in canvas, see Automations.
Why can't I see a workflow page? Guests see no workflow pages. Otherwise the normal page permissions apply.
Are there workflows in encrypted spaces? No – the server would have to read the contents.
Every node in detail: Node reference.
A workspace belongs to a team: its own members, groups, spaces and templates. Permissions work from the workspace via the space down to the single page and the single record.

en.heading: Workspaces
paragraphs: – Create: the name at the top of the sidebar → Create workspace. The administrators decide whether everyone may do this.
– Switch: via the same name; everyone can be a member of several workspaces.
– Settings → General: change the name and icon (Name & icon). Leaving and deleting are at the end in the Danger zone; when a button is greyed out, the text above it says why.

When leaving, a last owner has to make someone else an owner first under Settings → Members; your own spaces are handed over to a remaining owner of your choice. Deleting is only possible once you have another workspace; it removes all content, templates, files and shares for all members and cannot be undone. Both are confirmed with the workspace's name.

en.heading: Roles
paragraphs: Role May
Owner Everything, plus managing members, groups, spaces (including their order in the sidebar), tags and page properties and the workspace itself
Edit Create and change pages, set tags and property values, create new tags, comment, share
View Read and comment
Guest Only explicitly shared pages and spaces, with view or edit access

en.heading: Invite members
paragraphs: Settings → Members → Invite member opens a sheet (from the bottom on phones): e-mail address, role and – if needed – Invite as a guest. If e-mail is set up on the instance, the person gets an invitation. They create an account with this address – even if sign-ups are otherwise closed – or sign in with SSO; the workspace appears as soon as the address is confirmed. Without e-mail, afterwards copy the invitation link under Pending invitations (Copy link) and send it to them yourself.

Invitation link: the link opens the sign-up form with the invited address already filled in – even if sign-ups are otherwise closed. It creates an account only for that address. Without e-mail the person needs the link; the address alone is not enough then.

Only confirmed addresses: an existing account takes over an invitation on its own only when its address provably belongs to it – confirmed with the e-mail link, by an administrator or by the SSO provider. Otherwise (for instance on an instance without e-mail, where any address can sign up) only the invitation link counts: whoever opens it and signs in or signs up accepts the invitation. So give the link only to the person invited.

Where the invitation arrives: open invitations are listed under Settings → Members → Pending invitations – with role, guest status and shared pages, when and by whom they were invited. There they can be sent again (with e-mail) or withdrawn. The invited person finds the workspace in the workspace switcher at the top left and a notification in the inbox – right away with a new account, with an existing one the next time they open Flowplan (with single sign-on, at the next sign-in). A single page can also be shared without the whole workspace: Share a page with a person.
Existing members can be turned into guests with Make guest and back with Make member.

en.heading: Guests
paragraphs: Guests are people outside the team, such as customers or freelancers. They only see pages and spaces shared with them, including sub-pages, and cannot create pages, invite anyone or change settings. They do not see the workspace's templates, only their own. For people without any account there are links with their own permissions instead.

en.heading: Groups
paragraphs: Settings → Groups & permissions: under Groups create a group such as "Design" or "Sales" and tick members with Manage (with a search when there are many). Under Access to spaces set each space's visibility and below it View or Edit per group; single pages get a group through Share. New members of a group get its permissions right away.
With single sign-on, groups from the identity provider can maintain members and groups automatically – see Map SSO groups.

en.heading: How permissions work together
paragraphs: – The space sets the basis: open to all members or private for the people it is shared with.
– Pages inherit the permissions of their space and parent pages; under Share, people or groups are added.
– Records of a database can be made read-only or private (see Databases).
– Properties of a database can be made visible or editable only for editors, owners or selected groups (see Property visibility).
– Linked databases, mentions and links never grant additional permissions: whoever may not read the source does not see it embedded either.
Owners of a workspace also manage other members' spaces, but do not get read access to their private pages that way.

Encrypted spaces go one step further: there, not only the permission on the server decides but the key. Whoever has not been given the space key reads nothing – not even workspace owners or the administrators. See Encrypted spaces.

en.heading: Workflows: permissions and “runs as”
paragraphs: Workflow pages follow the normal page permissions: readers see the status, the flow and the runs; editors (full members with edit rights) build, test, activate and pause. Guests do not see workflow pages and cannot start or approve a workflow. An active workflow runs as the person who last activated it – it only sees and changes what they may, and pauses when they lose their rights.

en.heading: Storage quota
paragraphs: Every workspace can have a quota. Uploads, copies, templates and imports beyond it are refused. Administrators see the usage under Administration → Workspaces.
